data.retained_case_account: PAWS (Protection Assistant for Wildlife Security) is a machine-learning pipeline that predicts poaching risk and plans patrols. It was field-tested with WWF Cambodia and Ministry of Environment rangers in Srepok Wildlife Sanctuary, Cambodia, from December 2018. Only the month is given, so the first day is used. Rangers received center coordinates of fifteen 3 x 3 km blocks chosen from PAWS risk predictions, without being told each block's risk class. In the first month, 72 rangers in teams of eight detected poaching in 32 cells and removed over one thousand snares. They had reported removing two or three hundred in an average month. Low-risk blocks yielded no poaching. A second trial ran February to March 2019.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: The AI's output (risk-ranked 3 x 3 km blocks) determined where patrols went. Rangers were blinded to risk class. High-risk blocks yielded detections while low-risk blocks yielded none. The paper itself cautions that the first QENP test's increased findings “may be partially explained by factors beyond the predictive model”. The 1,000-versus-200–300 comparison relies on rangers' reported averages, not a controlled baseline. The peer-reviewed paper is written by the system's academic developers together with staff of the operating organizations (WWF, WCS, Uganda Wildlife Authority). There is no commercial vendor.

details.value: The model ranked homes for inspection and replacement. The developers wrote that their modeling had less influence on the choice of replacement homes, because those choices faced political and logistical limits. In 2023 Pierre Goovaerts, who has no tie to the developers, compared the program's order of excavation with geostatistical rankings. The program's order found lead lines fastest in its first eight months, and the rankings would have done better after that. He concluded that this weaker relative result came from something other than the decision in 2018 to stop using the model. record.title: ActiveRemediation helps Flint locate hazardous water pipes
record.summary: Researchers at the University of Michigan built ActiveRemediation, a model that ranked Flint homes by the chance of a hazardous service line, such as one of lead. Its held-out accuracy was 91.6%.
record.account: University of Michigan researchers worked with Flint’s service-line replacement program from summer 2016. ActiveRemediation used property records to recommend inspections. It used confirmed pipe materials. Its held-out prediction accuracy was 91.6%. The researchers reported that the program had replaced hazardous lines at 4,419 homes by September 2017. They wrote that their modeling had less influence on the choice of replacement homes, because those choices faced political and logistical limits. In a separate simulation they estimated that their method would have lowered the cost per successful replacement from the observed US$5,818 to about US$5,196. That is a saving of about US$622 per replacement, which is 10.7%. Reporters with no tie to the project later documented a decline in inspection success after the contractor changed its approach, alongside changes in geography and policy. A March 2019 court order required prioritization using the model’s address lists. Wired reported in January 2021 that Flint had resumed using the model. It reported that nearly 10,000 lead pipes had been replaced by the end of 2020. In March 2023 Pierre Goovaerts of BioMedware, who has no tie to the developers, compared the program's excavation order from 2016 to 2020 with geostatistical rankings. He found that the program's order found lead lines fastest in its first eight months. He found that the rankings would have done better after that. He concluded that this weaker relative result came from something other than the decision in 2018 to stop using the model. In July 2025 the Natural Resources Defense Council said that nearly 11,000 pipes had been replaced as the state reported completion to the court. No study in the sources isolates the model’s effect on residents’ health from the field evidence. None isolates its effect on actual spending.

record.title: The AI cameras of Phú Thọ provincial police identify all 18 teenagers found gathering with weapons to fight in Việt Trì within about 30 minutes. All were summoned. All confessed
record.summary: On 13 June 2026 Phú Thọ police saw teenagers preparing weapons to fight in Việt Trì. The provincial AI camera system identified all 18 faces in about 30 minutes.
record.account: On the night of Saturday 13 June 2026, Phú Thọ provincial police detected a group of teenagers gathering in Việt Trì ward. Officers were mining data from the camera system as they monitored it. Tuổi Trẻ reports that police found the group through camera monitoring, helped by tips from residents. It reported on 14 June that the teenagers were preparing weapons for a fight that would disturb public order. They had vehicles ready for it. Within about 30 minutes the AI camera system of the provincial command center had accurately identified the faces of all 18 participants. They were aged 14 to 18. They came from Việt Trì, Vân Phú and Nông Trang wards and Phù Ninh and Bình Phú communes (Tuổi Trẻ, VietNamNet). Tiền Phong says that the whole matter was clarified in just over two hours. It says that 17 of the 18 were pupils of schools including Vũ Thê Lang High School and Dữu Lâu Middle School. One had dropped out. It says that the provincial police summoned all 18. It says that at the police station they admitted the violations. None of the reports of 14 June says whether a fight took place. On 19 June 2026 Phú Thọ police said that two groups had fought with knives, swords, tridents and glass beer bottles at the Hội Thịnh roundabout around 23:30 on 13 June. They charged 10 people aged 16 to 18 with public disorder (Thanh Niên). One was detained. Nine were barred from leaving their place of residence. Thanh Niên describes most of the 10 as workers. Whether these 10 are among the 18 identified by camera is unknown.

Residents of Việt Trì were spared a street fight only if one was about to happen. Thanh Niên reports that two groups fought at the Hội Thịnh roundabout that night, and neither Thanh Niên nor the police say whether the 18 identified by camera took part.

The police account lacks matching logs, independent identity verification, false-match handling, and legal outcomes. Summons and reported admissions do not prove that violence was prevented; the sources do not state whether a fight occurred.

data.retained_case_account: On the night of Saturday 13 June 2026, Phú Thọ provincial police detected a group of teenagers gathering in Việt Trì ward. Officers were monitoring and mining data from the camera system. The teenagers were preparing weapons and vehicles to fight and disturb public order, Tuổi Trẻ reported on 14 June. Within about 30 minutes the AI camera system of the provincial command center had accurately identified the faces of all 18 participants. They were aged 14 to 18. They came from Việt Trì, Vân Phú and Nông Trang wards and Phù Ninh and Bình Phú communes (Tuổi Trẻ, VietNamNet). Tiền Phong says the whole case was clarified in just over two hours. It says 17 of the 18 were pupils of schools including Vũ Thê Lang High School and Dữu Lâu Middle School. One had dropped out. It says the provincial police summoned all 18, and that at the police station they admitted the violations. No report says whether a fight took place.

fields.account: On the night of Saturday 13 June 2026, Phú Thọ provincial police detected a group of teenagers gathering in Việt Trì ward. Officers were mining data from the camera system as they monitored it. Tuổi Trẻ reports that police found the group through camera monitoring, helped by tips from residents. It reported on 14 June that the teenagers were preparing weapons for a fight that would disturb public order. They had vehicles ready for it. Within about 30 minutes the AI camera system of the provincial command center had accurately identified the faces of all 18 participants. They were aged 14 to 18. They came from Việt Trì, Vân Phú and Nông Trang wards and Phù Ninh and Bình Phú communes (Tuổi Trẻ, VietNamNet). Tiền Phong says that the whole matter was clarified in just over two hours. It says that 17 of the 18 were pupils of schools including Vũ Thê Lang High School and Dữu Lâu Middle School. One had dropped out. It says that the provincial police summoned all 18. It says that at the police station they admitted the violations. None of the reports of 14 June says whether a fight took place. On 19 June 2026 Phú Thọ police said that two groups had fought with knives, swords, tridents and glass beer bottles at the Hội Thịnh roundabout around 23:30 on 13 June. They charged 10 people aged 16 to 18 with public disorder (Thanh Niên). One was detained. Nine were barred from leaving their place of residence. Thanh Niên describes most of the 10 as workers. Whether these 10 are among the 18 identified by camera is unknown.

fields.summary: On 13 June 2026 Phú Thọ police saw teenagers preparing weapons to fight in Việt Trì. The provincial AI camera system identified all 18 faces in about 30 minutes.
fields.account: On the night of Saturday 13 June 2026, Phú Thọ provincial police detected a group of teenagers gathering in Việt Trì ward. Officers were mining data from the camera system as they monitored it. Tuổi Trẻ reports that police found the group through camera monitoring, helped by tips from residents. It reported on 14 June that the teenagers were preparing weapons for a fight that would disturb public order. They had vehicles ready for it. Within about 30 minutes the AI camera system of the provincial command center had accurately identified the faces of all 18 participants. They were aged 14 to 18. They came from Việt Trì, Vân Phú and Nông Trang wards and Phù Ninh and Bình Phú communes (Tuổi Trẻ, VietNamNet). Tiền Phong says that the whole matter was clarified in just over two hours. It says that 17 of the 18 were pupils of schools including Vũ Thê Lang High School and Dữu Lâu Middle School. One had dropped out. It says that the provincial police summoned all 18. It says that at the police station they admitted the violations. None of the reports of 14 June says whether a fight took place. On 19 June 2026 Phú Thọ police said that two groups had fought with knives, swords, tridents and glass beer bottles at the Hội Thịnh roundabout around 23:30 on 13 June. They charged 10 people aged 16 to 18 with public disorder (Thanh Niên). One was detained. Nine were barred from leaving their place of residence. Thanh Niên describes most of the 10 as workers. Whether these 10 are among the 18 identified by camera is unknown.

record.title: A ZeroEyes alert sends Florida State University police to a man whom they charge on four counts after he pointed a stolen Glock at bystanders
record.summary: According to court documents, ZeroEyes gun detection flagged a man pointing a gun in a Florida State University garage on 2 May 2026. Police found a stolen Glock 19 on him. They charged him.
record.account: On 13 February 2026, Undark reported that there is little or no empirical evidence that AI weapons detection systems have prevented shootings in real settings such as schools. According to arrest papers cited by WCTV, Florida State University police responded to the St. Augustine parking garage at about 2:30 a.m. on Saturday 2 May 2026. ZeroEyes gun detection technology had detected an individual in black pointing a gun on the bottom level. ZeroEyes works on top of existing cameras. It routes human-verified detections to police. Camera footage showed a 19-year-old man brandishing a loaded firearm at four other people. Officers found a Glock 19 handgun, stolen from Miller County, Georgia, in his waistband. He was charged with possessing a firearm on school property. He was charged with unlawful carry. He was charged with improper display of a firearm. He was charged with grand theft of a firearm. He bonded out on Sunday 3 May 2026. The Tallahassee Democrat, citing court records, says that police responded to a “ZeroEyes camera notification”. It says that the man is not a student at the university. FOX49 reported on 5 May 2026 that, in their report, the police credit the ZeroEyes notification with helping officers respond more quickly. The police say that it helped them know what they faced. The university declined to say when it bought the system. It declined to say why.

fields.account: On 13 February 2026, Undark reported that there is little or no empirical evidence that AI weapons detection systems have prevented shootings in real settings such as schools. According to arrest papers cited by WCTV, Florida State University police responded to the St. Augustine parking garage at about 2:30 a.m. on Saturday 2 May 2026. ZeroEyes gun detection technology had detected an individual in black pointing a gun on the bottom level. ZeroEyes works on top of existing cameras. It routes human-verified detections to police. Camera footage showed a 19-year-old man brandishing a loaded firearm at four other people. Officers found a Glock 19 handgun, stolen from Miller County, Georgia, in his waistband. He was charged with possessing a firearm on school property. He was charged with unlawful carry. He was charged with improper display of a firearm. He was charged with grand theft of a firearm. He bonded out on Sunday 3 May 2026. The Tallahassee Democrat, citing court records, says that police responded to a “ZeroEyes camera notification”. It says that the man is not a student at the university. FOX49 reported on 5 May 2026 that, in their report, the police credit the ZeroEyes notification with helping officers respond more quickly. The police say that it helped them know what they faced. The university declined to say when it bought the system. It declined to say why.

record.title: Thames Water estimates that it saves 8.7 million liters a day by fixing over 800 leaks that its crews find from Origin Orbit satellite points in an 18-week trial
record.summary: In an 18-week trial, Origin Orbit flagged suspected leaks from satellite data. Thames Water found over 800 leaks, which by its own figures saves an estimated 8.7 million liters a day.
record.account: Thames Water tested Origin Orbit, the satellite leak-detection product of North East England start-up Origin Tech Ltd (founded 2019). The company and the utility describe it as applying artificial intelligence to satellite data to flag suspected underground leaks within a 30-meter search radius. In August 2025 The Times reported that Northumbrian Water technicians used Origin's satellite points to narrow leak searches to a 20-meter radius. The company's founding director told the paper that its leak totals came mainly from trials. Thames Water says that in an 18-week trial it found over 800 leaks across the network, saving an estimated 8.7 million liters of water a day. Several of the leaks ran at more than 10 liters per second. The Thames Water trial is undated. On the strength of the trial, Thames Water signed a 13-month contract, launched in March 2026 according to the utility's release. It deploys 20 specialists. Leak-detection crews are expected to find about 25 leaks a week each. Thames Water aims to cut leakage by 100 million liters a day. That makes Thames Water the first water company to integrate Origin Orbit into business-as-usual leakage operations. Smart Water Magazine reported the result on 5 May 2026. The BBC reported the utility's figures on 20 May 2026. Trade press reproduced them. Origin's co-founder John Marsden told the BBC that the satellites pass over Swindon roughly every six days. Marsden said that they produce points on a map for Thames Water crews. On its own site, Origin Tech claims in 2026 that Origin Orbit identified over 5,000 leaks (73.45 megaliters a day) across its customers. In June 2026 the Irish News reported that NI Water had signed a three-year Origin Orbit contract. On 24 August 2026 Thames Water described the satellite detection as part of its drought-response leak hunting, without reporting leak counts after the trial. Thames Water's release of 24 August 2026 gives the initial trial's length as 19 weeks, against 18 weeks in its April release. All figures originate with the utility and the vendor. No regulator has measured them. No independent party has measured them.

data.retained_case_account: Thames Water trialed Origin Orbit, the satellite leak-detection product of North East England start-up Origin Tech Ltd (founded 2019). The company and the utility describe it as using AI on satellite data to flag suspected underground leaks within a 30-meter search radius. Origin's co-founder John Marsden told the BBC the satellites pass over Swindon roughly every six days. He said they produce points on a map for Thames Water crews. Thames Water's statements say an 18-week trial found over 800 leaks across the network. They were reported by the BBC (20 May 2026) and reproduced in trade press. It saved an estimated 8.7 million liters of water a day, with several leaks running at more than 10 liters per second. On the strength of the trial, Thames Water signed a 13-month contract, launched in March 2026 per the utility's release. It deploys 20 specialists, with leak-detection crews expected to find about 25 leaks a week each, and aims to cut leakage by 100 million liters a day. That makes it the first water company to integrate Origin Orbit into business-as-usual leakage operations. Origin Tech's own site adds a 2026 claim that Origin Orbit identified over 5,000 leaks (73.45 ML/d) across its customers. All figures originate with the utility and the vendor, and no regulator or independent measurement is among the sources. The trial dates are not given. Smart Water Magazine reported the result on 5 May 2026. Cambridgeshire County Council's AI inspection contract (April 2026) and Hertfordshire's ARRES robot (January 2024) have no outcomes on record. They are not among the sources.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: Only the vendor and the utility describe the AI role. The BBC caption says the AI-generated satellite technology detects moisture and movement in the ground, and Origin Tech describes AI-driven satellite insights. The system outputs suspected-leak points that Thames Water crews then locate and repair with conventional methods. The 800-leak and 8.7 million liters a day figures are Thames Water's estimates relayed by the BBC. They are reproduced in the utility's press release (Water Magazine) and trade press. Origin Tech's site adds vendor claims. No independent verification is among the sources.

The company and the utility describe it as applying artificial intelligence to satellite data to flag suspected underground leaks within a 30-meter search radius. In August 2025 The Times reported that Northumbrian Water technicians used Origin's satellite points to narrow leak searches to a 20-meter radius. The company's founding director told the paper that its leak totals came mainly from trials. Thames Water says that in an 18-week trial it found over 800 leaks across the network, saving an estimated 8.7 million liters of water a day. Several of the leaks ran at more than 10 liters per second. The Thames Water trial is undated. On the strength of the trial, Thames Water signed a 13-month contract, launched in March 2026 according to the utility's release. It deploys 20 specialists. Leak-detection crews are expected to find about 25 leaks a week each. Thames Water aims to cut leakage by 100 million liters a day. record.title: An operator in Alberta repairs a methane leak a week after a United Nations satellite alert in April 2026
record.summary: The Methane Alert and Response System of the United Nations Environment Programme detected a leak in Alberta on 10 April 2026. The operator repaired it on 17 April 2026.
record.account: The original case document CAN_S_002 of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) concerns a methane leak from a failed ball valve connected to pigging equipment in southeastern Alberta. The first satellite detection was on 10 April 2026. The reported repair was on 17 April 2026. UNEP estimates that the leak released 175 tonnes of methane in a single week. That equals 4,900 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent. Optical gas imaging on the ground showed that the leak had ceased after repair. The operator is not named. UNEP does not separate the AI's contribution from the other steps (satellite analysis, expert review, notification, physical repair). UNEP updated the case document on 1 July 2026. On 15 July 2026 UNEP reported that its algorithms flag 80 to 85% of confirmed emissions before its experts do. UNEP reported that experts check every alert (ForkLog, 26 October 2026). UNEP also describes the mitigation in its August snapshot of the Methane Alert and Response System (MARS). The Chemical Engineer relayed that snapshot on 4 September 2026. The Chemical Engineer reports that the Alberta alert was the first MARS notification of a Canadian site since the program began in 2023.

The first satellite detection was on 10 April 2026. The reported repair was on 17 April 2026. UNEP estimates that the leak released 175 tonnes of methane in a single week. That equals 4,900 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent. Optical gas imaging on the ground showed that the leak had ceased after repair. The operator is not named. UNEP does not separate the AI's contribution from the other steps (satellite analysis, expert review, notification, physical repair). UNEP updated the case document on 1 July 2026. On 15 July 2026 UNEP reported that its algorithms flag 80 to 85% of confirmed emissions before its experts do. UNEP reported that experts check every alert (ForkLog, 26 October 2026). UNEP also describes the mitigation in its August snapshot of the Methane Alert and Response System (MARS). The Chemical Engineer relayed that snapshot on 4 September 2026. The Chemical Engineer reports that the Alberta alert was the first MARS notification of a Canadian site since the program began in 2023.

record.title: In an operation whose details are undisclosed, Ukrainian unmanned systems may have taken a Russian position without infantry, losing no one
record.summary: President Zelenskyy said on 13 April 2026 that Ukrainian unmanned systems had taken an enemy position with no infantry. He said that Ukraine lost no one. The sources hold no independent check.
record.account: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy gave an Arms Makers' Day address on Monday 13 April 2026. “For the first time in the history of this war, an enemy position was taken exclusively by unmanned platforms — ground systems and drones,” he said. He added that “the occupiers surrendered, and the operation was carried out without infantry and without losses on our side” (Politico, Business Insider, Censor.NET). He said that ground robotic systems performed more than 22,000 missions on Ukraine's front line in the first three months of 2026. He named Ratel, TerMIT, Ardal, Rys, Zmiy, Protector and Volia. Newsweek reports that he did not say where the advance took place. No outlet gives a date. None names the unit. None gives a count of prisoners. Ars Technica reports that the claim is not independently verified. It reports that the claim may refer to a 3rd Separate Assault Brigade action in Kharkiv Oblast the previous year. Politico describes the robots as “currently piloted by humans from a safe distance”. No outlet has since confirmed the place of the April operation. None has confirmed its date. None has confirmed the unit. Unmanned assaults spread later in 2026: on 17 July Forbes described a recent fully unmanned assault by the 33rd Separate Assault Regiment near Dobropillya. In September the 3rd Army Corps said that its drones had dropped armed robots behind Russian lines in Operation Vivaldi.

record.title: AI smoke-detection camera for Arizona Public Service spots early signs of the March 2026 Diamond Fire, which crews hold to 7 acres in Coconino National Forest
record.summary: An AI smoke-detection camera of unnamed make, installed for Arizona Public Service, spotted early signs of the Diamond Fire near Flagstaff on 26 March 2026. Crews held the fire to 7 acres.
record.account: In a staff report of 26 March 2026, the Arizona Daily Sun reports that a small fire later named the Diamond Fire began shortly after 2 p.m. on Thursday, 26 March 2026. It started just north of Lake Mary Road, about three miles southeast of the intersection of Lake Mary Road and Beulah Boulevard. That is south of Pine Canyon Golf Club. It is east of Flagstaff Pulliam Airport. It reached seven acres by 3:16 p.m., according to WatchDuty. Its forward progress was stopped at 3:37 p.m., about 80 minutes after the first report. It was 100% contained at 6:09 p.m. The Daily Sun does not mention a camera, the Coconino National Forest or who made the first report. In the interagency wildfire record (2026-AZCOF-000289), the Diamond Fire is on the Coconino National Forest. It was discovered at 2:15 p.m. Mountain Standard Time on 26 March 2026 at a tenth of an acre. The record gives a final size of 7 acres, a human cause and containment at 6:08 p.m. Who detected it is not recorded. No official incident record that lists the camera has been found. The “Diamond Fire” on InciWeb is a different fire, in Scottsdale in June 2023. The Associated Press reported on 4 May 2026 that artificial intelligence had detected something resembling smoke on a camera feed from Arizona's Coconino National Forest on a March afternoon. The report is by Dorany Pineda and Brittany Peterson, on record in the KPBS and Courthouse News republications. One of dozens of AI cameras installed for the utility Arizona Public Service had spotted early signs of the fire that came to be known as the Diamond Fire. The Associated Press says that human analysts verified the camera's detection before they alerted the state forest service and Arizona Public Service. Firefighters raced to the scene. They contained it before it grew past 7 acres (2.8 hectares). The Daily Sun and Associated Press accounts match on the fire's name, month and size. The Associated Press says that Arizona Public Service has nearly 40 active AI smoke-detection cameras. It says that the utility plans 71 by summer's end. Cindy Kobold, a meteorologist at Arizona Public Service, says that the technology notifies the utility about 45 minutes faster on average than the first 911 call. Pano AI, launched in 2020, charges around $50,000 a year per camera. It counts Arizona Public Service among its customers. It says that it detected 725 wildfires in the United States in the previous year. The Associated Press does not state outright which company made the camera that spotted the Diamond Fire.

data.retained_case_account: The Associated Press reported on 4 May 2026 that artificial intelligence detected something resembling smoke on a camera feed from Arizona's Coconino National Forest. The report is by Dorany Pineda and Brittany Peterson, on record in the KPBS and Courthouse News republications. The detection came on a March afternoon. One of dozens of AI cameras installed for the utility Arizona Public Service had spotted early signs. The fire came to be known as the Diamond Fire. Firefighters raced to the scene and contained it before it grew past 7 acres (2.8 hectares). AP says APS has nearly 40 active AI smoke-detection cameras and plans 71 by summer's end. APS meteorologist Cindy Kobold says the technology notifies the utility about 45 minutes faster on average than the first 911 call. Pano AI, launched in 2020 and charging around $50,000 a year per camera, counts APS among its customers. It says it detected 725 wildfires in the US last year. AP does not state outright which company made the camera that spotted the Diamond Fire. The Arizona Daily Sun (staff report, 26 March 2026) reports that a small fire later named the Diamond Fire began shortly after 2 p.m. on Thursday. It started just north of Lake Mary Road, about three miles south-east of Lake Mary Road and Beulah Boulevard. That is south of Pine Canyon Golf Club and east of Flagstaff Pulliam Airport. It reached seven acres by 3:16 p.m. according to WatchDuty. Its forward progress was stopped at 3:37 p.m., about 80 minutes after the first report, and it was 100% contained at 6:09 p.m. The Daily Sun does not mention a camera, the Coconino National Forest or who made the first report. The two accounts are matched by the fire's name, month and size. No official incident record naming the camera was found; InciWeb's “Diamond Fire” is a June 2023 Scottsdale fire. The Daily Sun reported the fire that Thursday.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: AP reports that the camera's AI detected something resembling smoke and spotted early signs of the fire. It does not say whether the alert was the first report or what the fire agencies did with it. The Daily Sun's timeline does not mention the camera: first report, 7 acres by 3:16 p.m., progress stopped 3:37 p.m., contained 6:09 p.m. The attribution to AI rests on one news report, and the camera's maker is implied rather than stated. No official record naming the camera was found.

fields.account: In a staff report of 26 March 2026, the Arizona Daily Sun reports that a small fire later named the Diamond Fire began shortly after 2 p.m. on Thursday, 26 March 2026. It started just north of Lake Mary Road, about three miles southeast of the intersection of Lake Mary Road and Beulah Boulevard. That is south of Pine Canyon Golf Club. It is east of Flagstaff Pulliam Airport. It reached seven acres by 3:16 p.m., according to WatchDuty. Its forward progress was stopped at 3:37 p.m., about 80 minutes after the first report. It was 100% contained at 6:09 p.m. The Daily Sun does not mention a camera, the Coconino National Forest or who made the first report. In the interagency wildfire record (2026-AZCOF-000289), the Diamond Fire is on the Coconino National Forest. It was discovered at 2:15 p.m. Mountain Standard Time on 26 March 2026 at a tenth of an acre. The record gives a final size of 7 acres, a human cause and containment at 6:08 p.m. Who detected it is not recorded. No official incident record that lists the camera has been found. The “Diamond Fire” on InciWeb is a different fire, in Scottsdale in June 2023. The Associated Press reported on 4 May 2026 that artificial intelligence had detected something resembling smoke on a camera feed from Arizona's Coconino National Forest on a March afternoon. The report is by Dorany Pineda and Brittany Peterson, on record in the KPBS and Courthouse News republications. One of dozens of AI cameras installed for the utility Arizona Public Service had spotted early signs of the fire that came to be known as the Diamond Fire. The Associated Press says that human analysts verified the camera's detection before they alerted the state forest service and Arizona Public Service. Firefighters raced to the scene. They contained it before it grew past 7 acres (2.8 hectares). The Daily Sun and Associated Press accounts match on the fire's name, month and size. The Associated Press says that Arizona Public Service has nearly 40 active AI smoke-detection cameras. It says that the utility plans 71 by summer's end. Cindy Kobold, a meteorologist at Arizona Public Service, says that the technology notifies the utility about 45 minutes faster on average than the first 911 call. Pano AI, launched in 2020, charges around $50,000 a year per camera. It counts Arizona Public Service among its customers. It says that it detected 725 wildfires in the United States in the previous year. The Associated Press does not state outright which company made the camera that spotted the Diamond Fire.

details.label: Contribution of the AI
details.value: The AI's documented contribution is speed of analysis, on the researchers' own account. Wiz writes that AI-augmented reverse-engineering tooling, particularly IDA MCP, let it rapidly analyze GitHub's compiled binaries and reconstruct internal protocols. Wiz says that speed would not have been feasible manually. Sagi Tzadik told Dark Reading that with AI tools it took under 48 hours from idea to working exploit. The Register adds that the team used Claude Code “to take a lot of the legwork out of the process”. The hypothesis, the exploit, the report and the fix were human work. Six named Wiz researchers confirmed RCE on GHES 3.19.1 and wrote what GitHub called a thorough report. GitHub's security and engineering teams reproduced the bug within 40 minutes and deployed the fix. In its own post, the CVE record and the GHES release notes, GitHub describes a Bug Bounty report without mentioning AI. So the claim of help from AI rests on Wiz and on outlets quoting Wiz. In its write-up, Wiz names IDA MCP and does not name Claude.

record.summary: Wiz researchers used Claude Code and IDA MCP to reverse engineer GitHub's binaries. They found a critical remote code execution flaw, which GitHub fixed on github.com the same day.
record.account: On 4 March 2026, Wiz Research reported a critical remote code execution flaw to GitHub, later numbered CVE-2026-3854. The flaw sat in GitHub's internal git infrastructure. Git push options were not sanitized before being written into internal headers. Any authenticated user could therefore run arbitrary commands on GitHub's servers with a single git push. Wiz says that AI-augmented tooling made the research feasible, particularly automated reverse engineering of GitHub's compiled binaries with IDA MCP. The Register reports that the team used Claude Code and went from idea to working exploit in under 48 hours. GitHub reproduced the bug within 40 minutes. It deployed a fix to github.com at 7:00 pm UTC that day. It released patches for GitHub Enterprise Server from 10 March 2026. The National Vulnerability Database entry, published on 10 March 2026, scores the flaw 8.8 (High) under version 3.1 of the Common Vulnerability Scoring System. On 28 April 2026, GitHub disclosed the flaw. It reported that its forensic investigation found no exploitation beyond the researchers' own testing. The same day, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency recorded no known exploitation in its enrichment of the entry. Wiz published its own account that day. It wrote that its data showed that 88% of GitHub Enterprise Server instances were still vulnerable.

produced_by: A closed-source target that researchers could obtain and disassemble. GitHub's backend git services also ship as GitHub Enterprise Server binaries. Those binaries gave automated reverse engineering something to work on, and GHES 3.19.1 gave a place to confirm the exploit.

AI-augmented tooling for reverse engineering: IDA MCP (per Wiz) driven by Claude Code (per The Register). It reconstructed internal protocols and traced where user input could influence server behavior across the pipeline.

Experienced vulnerability researchers: six named Wiz authors formed the hypothesis and built and confirmed a working exploit. They wrote what GitHub called a thorough report that clearly demonstrated the impact.
A beneficiary with a Bug Bounty intake and an on-call security team. GitHub reproduced the bug within 40 minutes of the report. It deployed a fix to github.com at 7:00 pm UTC the same day.
must_hold: AI output has to be confirmed by exploit, not trusted. Wiz confirmed RCE on a GHES 3.19.1 instance before reporting. That is why GitHub could validate the report in 40 minutes.

The receiving organization must be able to patch its own service and ship fixes to self-hosted customers. GHES customers stayed exposed until they upgraded to the patched versions released from 10 March 2026.
Disclosure must wait for the patches, here from 4 March to 28 April 2026. No exploitation had occurred, so the benefit is an exposure closed, not a loss recovered.

data.retained_case_account: On 4 March 2026 Wiz Research reported a critical remote code execution (RCE) flaw to GitHub, later CVE-2026–3854. It sat in GitHub's internal git infrastructure. Git push options were not sanitized before being written into internal headers. Any authenticated user could therefore run arbitrary commands on GitHub's servers with a single git push. Wiz says AI-augmented tooling made the research feasible, particularly automated reverse engineering of GitHub's compiled binaries with IDA MCP. The Register reports that the team used Claude Code and went from idea to working exploit in under 48 hours. GitHub reproduced the bug within 40 minutes and deployed a fix to github.com at 7:00 pm UTC that day. It released GitHub Enterprise Server (GHES) patches from 10 March, and found no exploitation.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: The AI's documented contribution is speed of analysis, on the researchers' own account. Wiz writes that AI-augmented reverse-engineering tooling, particularly IDA MCP, let it rapidly analyze GitHub's compiled binaries and reconstruct internal protocols. Wiz says that speed would not have been feasible manually. Sagi Tzadik told Dark Reading that with AI tools it took under 48 hours from idea to working exploit. The Register adds that the team used Claude Code “to take a lot of the legwork out of the process”. The hypothesis, the exploit, the report and the fix were human work. Six named Wiz researchers confirmed RCE on GHES 3.19.1 and wrote what GitHub called a thorough report. GitHub's security and engineering teams reproduced the bug within 40 minutes and deployed the fix. GitHub's own post, the CVE record and the GHES release notes describe a Bug Bounty report without mentioning AI. The AI-assistance claim therefore rests on Wiz and on outlets quoting Wiz. Wiz's write-up, in the text as read, names IDA MCP and not Claude.

ratings.reason: GitHub closed a remote code execution hole in its git push pipeline within hours of the report. The fix reached github.com at 7:00 pm UTC on 4 March 2026. GitHub also shipped patches for six GitHub Enterprise Server release lines. Wiz earned what GitHub calls one of the highest rewards in the history of its Bug Bounty program. The loss avoided is hypothetical. GitHub's forensic investigation found that no other account had triggered the code path, and CISA records no exploitation. Wiz wrote that its data showed that 88% of GitHub Enterprise Server instances were still vulnerable when it published on 28 April 2026, so many self-hosted servers stayed exposed. NIST rates the flaw High (8.8).

A beneficiary with a Bug Bounty intake and an on-call security team. GitHub reproduced the bug within 40 minutes of the report. It deployed a fix to github.com at 7:00 pm UTC the same day.
must_hold: AI output has to be confirmed by exploit, not trusted. Wiz confirmed RCE on a GHES 3.19.1 instance before reporting. That is why GitHub could validate the report in 40 minutes.

The receiving organization must be able to patch its own service and ship fixes to self-hosted customers. GHES customers stayed exposed until they upgraded to the patched versions released from 10 March 2026.
Disclosure must wait for the patches, here from 4 March to 28 April 2026. No exploitation had occurred, so the benefit is an exposure closed, not a loss recovered.

record.title: Operators in Iraq divert gas from a methane source after United Nations satellite alerts. UNEP records the mitigation on 25 February 2026
record.summary: After alerts from UNEP's Methane Alert and Response System, which uses AI, operators diverted gas from an Iraqi source by 25 February 2026. UNEP estimates that it had emitted 60,500 tonnes of methane.
record.account: UNEP states that its International Methane Emissions Observatory (IMEO) combines data from more than 30 satellite instruments, scientific expertise and advanced AI models. It uses them to notify governments of emissions. It notifies companies. In its original case document for source IRQ_S_050, UNEP records first detection at an Iraqi oil and gas facility on 21 August 2025. The document shows two detected plumes. It gives an estimated 60,500 tonnes of methane emissions. Operators diverted production to newer infrastructure, with its associated gas. The document gives the date of mitigation as 25 February 2026. UNEP updated the document on 15 April 2026. It does not name the operator. On 5 May 2026 The Chemical Engineer reported that the largest source mitigated that year was a flare in Iraq. It had released an estimated 1.7 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent since 2023. The magazine links the source to the Zubair area. It reports a leak-detection campaign by Eni. Eni did not confirm closure of this specific source. In its September 2026 snapshot, UNEP lists no Iraqi source among its top 50 emitters. Satellite non-detection is limited by the instrument’s sensitivity. Observation conditions limit it.

The magazine links the source to the Zubair area. It reports a leak-detection campaign by Eni. Eni did not confirm closure of this specific source. In its September 2026 snapshot, UNEP lists no Iraqi source among its top 50 emitters. Satellite non-detection is limited by the instrument’s sensitivity. Observation conditions limit it.

record.title: Istanbul police first use their AVCI messaging-analysis system in a drug operation across 14 provinces on 10 February 2026 that closes 69 groups of dealers, with 325 suspects remanded
record.summary: Istanbul police first used their AI-supported AVCI messaging-analysis system on 10 February 2026, in a drug operation across 14 provinces: 325 detained and remanded, 69 groups closed.
record.account: AVCI (Açık Kaynak İstihbaratı Analiz Sistemi, Open Source Intelligence Analysis System) is an AI-supported program. The Istanbul Police Department's narcotics and cybercrime divisions built it in-house with a special software team. Police chief Selami Yıldız ordered the work. It infiltrates closed groups and channels on end-to-end encrypted messaging apps. It analyzes messages. It analyzes voice notes. It analyzes photos. It analyzes location data. It decodes the slang of dealers. It links profiles. It maps the relationships inside groups. By copying traffic to its own servers while the traffic is accessible, it preserves material that users later delete. Police first used AVCI on 10 February 2026, in a drug operation that was centered on Istanbul and ran across 14 provinces. Anadolu Agency reported that day that the simultaneous raids had taken place that morning in 14 provinces and 35 districts. It reported that 305 of 346 sought suspects had been detained. On 13 February 2026 the Istanbul Chief Public Prosecutor's Office said that 324 suspects had been caught, 21 of them group administrators. Criminal judgeships of peace had remanded all of them. Anadolu Agency reported on 6 April 2026 that 325 suspects had been detained in the operation. All 325 referred to court were remanded in custody. Police closed 69 groups on messaging apps.

fields.account: AVCI (Açık Kaynak İstihbaratı Analiz Sistemi, Open Source Intelligence Analysis System) is an AI-supported program. The Istanbul Police Department's narcotics and cybercrime divisions built it in-house with a special software team. Police chief Selami Yıldız ordered the work. It infiltrates closed groups and channels on end-to-end encrypted messaging apps. It analyzes messages. It analyzes voice notes. It analyzes photos. It analyzes location data. It decodes the slang of dealers. It links profiles. It maps the relationships inside groups. By copying traffic to its own servers while the traffic is accessible, it preserves material that users later delete. Police first used AVCI on 10 February 2026, in a drug operation that was centered on Istanbul and ran across 14 provinces. Anadolu Agency reported that day that the simultaneous raids had taken place that morning in 14 provinces and 35 districts. It reported that 305 of 346 sought suspects had been detained. On 13 February 2026 the Istanbul Chief Public Prosecutor's Office said that 324 suspects had been caught, 21 of them group administrators. Criminal judgeships of peace had remanded all of them. Anadolu Agency reported on 6 April 2026 that 325 suspects had been detained in the operation. All 325 referred to court were remanded in custody. Police closed 69 groups on messaging apps.

value.text: Anadolu Agency reported on 17 July 2026 that police had used AVCI again in an Istanbul-based operation across 35 provinces. According to the agency, 110 suspects were detained and 65 Telegram groups and channels were closed in that operation. No source follows the groups closed in February or the cases of the 325 suspects.

record.title: After ChatGPT flags warning signs about a fake share adviser, a 77-year-old man in Bengaluru reports a Rs 67.10 lakh fraud to police
record.summary: After withdrawals were refused, a 77-year-old Bengaluru man checked the firm with ChatGPT. It flagged warning signs. He reported a Rs 67.10 lakh fraud to police.
record.account: The New Indian Express (6 January 2026) reported on a 77-year-old resident of Binnypet, Bengaluru. In November 2025 a man using a false name contacted him. He claimed to be an adviser with IIFL Wealth Management. He promised assured allotment of shares before an initial public offering (pre-IPO shares). The victim first transferred Rs 5 lakh for a supposed ICICI Prudential AMC pre-IPO. He was shown profits in a digital wallet. Over the following weeks he made multiple real-time gross settlement (RTGS) transfers totaling Rs 67.10 lakh. His requests to withdraw even part of the funds were denied. The fraudsters demanded more payments to repay a loan before any withdrawal. He then searched for details about the company and its representatives using ChatGPT. It reportedly showed complaints. It showed inconsistencies in the company's credentials. It showed indicators associated with investment fraud. He approached the police, who registered a case under the Information Technology Act. The police said that efforts were under way to trace the money. On 6 January 2026 the Deccan Herald published a report by Prajwal D'Souza. In its headline, the paper credits the ChatGPT response with saving him from losing more money to cybercriminals. No police official is named. The victim is not named. No arrest or recovery had been reported by 29 October 2026. ABC7 had reported something similar on 6 December 2025. A widow in San Jose, California, recognized a pig-butchering scheme after ChatGPT told her that it was a scam. It told her that she should go to the police. She had already lost nearly $1 million.

data.retained_case_account: The New Indian Express (6 January 2026) reported on a 77-year-old resident of Binnypet, Bengaluru. In November 2025 a man using a false name contacted him. He claimed to be an adviser with IIFL Wealth Management and promised assured allotment of pre-IPO shares. The victim first transferred Rs 5 lakh for a supposed ICICI Prudential AMC pre-IPO and was shown profits in a digital wallet. Over the following weeks he made multiple RTGS transfers totaling Rs 67.10 lakh. When requests to withdraw even part of the funds were denied, he searched for details about the company and its representatives using ChatGPT. It reportedly flagged complaints, inconsistencies in company credentials and indicators associated with investment fraud. He then approached the police, who registered a case under the Information Technology Act. The police said that efforts were under way to trace the money. Deccan Herald (Prajwal D'Souza, 6 January 2026) framed the ChatGPT response as saving him from losing more money. No police official is named, no recovery is reported and the victim is unnamed.

details.label: Contribution of the AI
details.value: The Finance Ministry counts the system's contribution as the gap between importers' declared values and the assessed values. The system analyzed about 366,000 declarations, and 24 percent triggered more than one valuation risk indicator for review by customs officers. Officers review its suggested values, and importers who object with documents such as bank records or contracts can have them set aside. The customs division has not separated the system's flags from the officers' decisions, and the count is the deployer's own.

record.title: Ghana's Finance Minister credits the Publican AI Trade Solution with over US$300 million in added customs assessments, after a pilot reported to have recovered GH¢15 million
record.summary: Ghana's Finance Minister reported that the Publican AI Trade Solution raised assessed customs collections by over US$300 million from January to 17 July 2026, a 17.5 percent uplift.
record.account: On 16 January 2026 MyJoyOnline reported that the Ghana Revenue Authority had launched Publican AI. The platform analyzes trade data to identify customs fraud. It identifies undervaluation. It identifies falsified import documentation. In its original report on the launch, MyJoy credits the pilot with GH¢15 million in revenue recovered from five companies. The reports include no ledger of recoveries. The Ghanaian Times (Kingsley Asare, 19 January 2026) reported remarks by Commissioner-General Dr Anthony Sarpong. He said that the Publican AI system would cover 100 percent of assessments. He said that assessments that took about two hours could be completed within five minutes. He said that pilots showed 40–45% revenue gains. He said that rollout would begin at Tema Port on 1 February 2026. Asare cites no realized recovery in the article. The vendor is described there only as a Cyprus-based firm. On 7 April 2026 the Member of Parliament for New Juaben South called for the system's suspension. MyJoyOnline reported that a coalition of traders and freight forwarders demanded the same. Some importers reported duty assessments rising from about GH¢900,000 to over GH¢2.1 million. On 22 April 2026 a welfare officer of the Ghana Union of Traders Association said that some traders were reportedly paying up to 300% more in duties than before. The next day a Customs Laboratory official of the authority said that officers review the system's suggested values. The official said that they set the values aside when importers prove their prices. Finance Minister Cassiel Ato Forson presented the 2026 Mid-Year Fiscal Policy Review on 23 July 2026. In it, the minister reported that Publican raised assessed customs collections by over US$300 million from January to 17 July 2026, a 17.5 percent uplift over declared values. On 9 August 2026 MyJoyOnline reported the Commissioner-General's figures. Monthly customs revenue had averaged about GH¢4 billion before the full implementation of the system. It reached GH¢6.1 billion in July 2026.

fields.account: On 16 January 2026 MyJoyOnline reported that the Ghana Revenue Authority had launched Publican AI. The platform analyzes trade data to identify customs fraud. It identifies undervaluation. It identifies falsified import documentation. In its original report on the launch, MyJoy credits the pilot with GH¢15 million in revenue recovered from five companies. The reports include no ledger of recoveries. The Ghanaian Times (Kingsley Asare, 19 January 2026) reported remarks by Commissioner-General Dr Anthony Sarpong. He said that the Publican AI system would cover 100 percent of assessments. He said that assessments that took about two hours could be completed within five minutes. He said that pilots showed 40–45% revenue gains. He said that rollout would begin at Tema Port on 1 February 2026. Asare cites no realized recovery in the article. The vendor is described there only as a Cyprus-based firm. On 7 April 2026 the Member of Parliament for New Juaben South called for the system's suspension. MyJoyOnline reported that a coalition of traders and freight forwarders demanded the same. Some importers reported duty assessments rising from about GH¢900,000 to over GH¢2.1 million. On 22 April 2026 a welfare officer of the Ghana Union of Traders Association said that some traders were reportedly paying up to 300% more in duties than before. The next day a Customs Laboratory official of the authority said that officers review the system's suggested values. The official said that they set the values aside when importers prove their prices. Finance Minister Cassiel Ato Forson presented the 2026 Mid-Year Fiscal Policy Review on 23 July 2026. In it, the minister reported that Publican raised assessed customs collections by over US$300 million from January to 17 July 2026, a 17.5 percent uplift over declared values. On 9 August 2026 MyJoyOnline reported the Commissioner-General's figures. Monthly customs revenue had averaged about GH¢4 billion before the full implementation of the system. It reached GH¢6.1 billion in July 2026.

fields.summary: Ghana's Finance Minister reported that the Publican AI Trade Solution raised assessed customs collections by over US$300 million from January to 17 July 2026, a 17.5 percent uplift.
fields.account: On 16 January 2026 MyJoyOnline reported that the Ghana Revenue Authority had launched Publican AI. The platform analyzes trade data to identify customs fraud. It identifies undervaluation. It identifies falsified import documentation. In its original report on the launch, MyJoy credits the pilot with GH¢15 million in revenue recovered from five companies. The reports include no ledger of recoveries. The Ghanaian Times (Kingsley Asare, 19 January 2026) reported remarks by Commissioner-General Dr Anthony Sarpong. He said that the Publican AI system would cover 100 percent of assessments. He said that assessments that took about two hours could be completed within five minutes. He said that pilots showed 40–45% revenue gains. He said that rollout would begin at Tema Port on 1 February 2026. Asare cites no realized recovery in the article. The vendor is described there only as a Cyprus-based firm. On 7 April 2026 the Member of Parliament for New Juaben South called for the system's suspension. MyJoyOnline reported that a coalition of traders and freight forwarders demanded the same. Some importers reported duty assessments rising from about GH¢900,000 to over GH¢2.1 million. On 22 April 2026 a welfare officer of the Ghana Union of Traders Association said that some traders were reportedly paying up to 300% more in duties than before. The next day a Customs Laboratory official of the authority said that officers review the system's suggested values. The official said that they set the values aside when importers prove their prices. Finance Minister Cassiel Ato Forson presented the 2026 Mid-Year Fiscal Policy Review on 23 July 2026. In it, the minister reported that Publican raised assessed customs collections by over US$300 million from January to 17 July 2026, a 17.5 percent uplift over declared values. On 9 August 2026 MyJoyOnline reported the Commissioner-General's figures. Monthly customs revenue had averaged about GH¢4 billion before the full implementation of the system. It reached GH¢6.1 billion in July 2026.

record.title: A week after a driver-reported defect cost over 10,000 delay minutes, LNER's on-train video review flags a minor track fault near Retford that engineers fix overnight with zero delay minutes
record.summary: LNER reports that One Big Circle's Automated Intelligent Video Review (AIVR) system detected a minor track fault near Retford, which engineers repaired overnight with no delay to passengers.
record.account: LNER runs the Pantograph Damage Assessment System (PANDAS) and One Big Circle's Automated Intelligent Video Review (AIVR) on a number of its trains. They assess overhead line equipment. They assess track. They report potential damage to Network Rail. LNER states that AIVR, with underbody line-scanning cameras, was fitted to two bi-mode Azuma units in January 2026. In January 2026 a train driver in Cambridgeshire reported a track defect. It caused over 10,000 delay minutes. It caused multiple cancellations. It caused a full day of disruption. A week later the AIVR system identified a minor fault near Retford with the potential to become a larger issue. The Retford detection therefore came within weeks of installation. The exact day of the detection is not given. Engineers carried out an overnight repair with no delay to passengers and zero delay minutes. LNER announced the Retford result on 9 April 2026. The 10,000 delay minutes concern the separate Cambridgeshire event. No source measures the delay saved at Retford. On 3 July 2026 the system flagged a snake as a track defect. New Civil Engineer's Tom Pashby reported the snake alert on 6 July 2026. His article reproduces LNER's announcement of 9 April 2026. An LNER spokesperson said that the information is fed back to Network Rail to target areas for attention. A Network Rail spokesperson said that the snake would be raised automatically as standard practice.

display.answer: The Retford figures come from LNER's announcement of 9 April 2026, which New Civil Engineer reproduced on 6 July 2026 in its own report on the snake alert. Network Rail's story of 31 October 2022 names One Big Circle as the developer of AIVR.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: LNER reports that One Big Circle's Automated Intelligent Video Review (AIVR) system detected a minor track fault near Retford, which engineers repaired overnight with no delay to passengers.
fields.account: LNER runs the Pantograph Damage Assessment System (PANDAS) and One Big Circle's Automated Intelligent Video Review (AIVR) on a number of its trains. They assess overhead line equipment. They assess track. They report potential damage to Network Rail. LNER states that AIVR, with underbody line-scanning cameras, was fitted to two bi-mode Azuma units in January 2026. In January 2026 a train driver in Cambridgeshire reported a track defect. It caused over 10,000 delay minutes. It caused multiple cancellations. It caused a full day of disruption. A week later the AIVR system identified a minor fault near Retford with the potential to become a larger issue. The Retford detection therefore came within weeks of installation. The exact day of the detection is not given. Engineers carried out an overnight repair with no delay to passengers and zero delay minutes. LNER announced the Retford result on 9 April 2026. The 10,000 delay minutes concern the separate Cambridgeshire event. No source measures the delay saved at Retford. On 3 July 2026 the system flagged a snake as a track defect. New Civil Engineer's Tom Pashby reported the snake alert on 6 July 2026. His article reproduces LNER's announcement of 9 April 2026. An LNER spokesperson said that the information is fed back to Network Rail to target areas for attention. A Network Rail spokesperson said that the snake would be raised automatically as standard practice.

value.text: AIVR automatically raised a possible infrastructure problem. People determined its significance and arranged the repair.

record.title: AI cameras in Ho Chi Minh City identify a masked burglar by features such as his gait before Tân Hưng ward police detain him within two days
record.summary: With unnamed AI street cameras, Ho Chi Minh City police identified a masked burglar who took two laptops on 23 December 2025. He took 14 million VND. Police detained him on 24 December.
record.account: Early on 23 December 2025 an intruder entered a rented room in Tân Hưng ward, Ho Chi Minh City. He took two laptops. He took the wallet of the tenant, a 33-year-old. He took the identity papers. He took the bank card. A withdrawal of 14 million VND was made from the tenant's bank account. The tenant reported the burglary that morning. Tân Hưng Ward Police and the Criminal Police Division used the street AI camera system. It analyzed the masked man's gait. It analyzed his build. It analyzed his clothing. It analyzed his movement. It analyzed his facial data. It identified him. It reconstructed his route. At 11 p.m. on 24 December officers found the suspect, a 23-year-old man, at an internet café on Tô Ký street. He had a previous conviction for theft. He confessed. VietNamNet reports that police held the suspect for investigation of theft on 25 December 2025. Dân trí reports that he told investigators that he had sold the stolen property. The police have not said that the property was recovered.

fields.account: Early on 23 December 2025 an intruder entered a rented room in Tân Hưng ward, Ho Chi Minh City. He took two laptops. He took the wallet of the tenant, a 33-year-old. He took the identity papers. He took the bank card. A withdrawal of 14 million VND was made from the tenant's bank account. The tenant reported the burglary that morning. Tân Hưng Ward Police and the Criminal Police Division used the street AI camera system. It analyzed the masked man's gait. It analyzed his build. It analyzed his clothing. It analyzed his movement. It analyzed his facial data. It identified him. It reconstructed his route. At 11 p.m. on 24 December officers found the suspect, a 23-year-old man, at an internet café on Tô Ký street. He had a previous conviction for theft. He confessed. VietNamNet reports that police held the suspect for investigation of theft on 25 December 2025. Dân trí reports that he told investigators that he had sold the stolen property. The police have not said that the property was recovered.

details.label: Purpose
details.value: Garmin built Autoland to take complete control of an aircraft and land it when the pilot cannot fly. It engages on its own when the cabin altitude exceeds a set level, as it did here. The two pilots were not incapacitated, though, and chose to let it finish.

details.label: Contribution of the AI
details.value: Autoland engaged itself when the cabin altitude exceeded the limit. It declared the emergency to controllers with automated “pilot incapacitation” broadcasts and flew the descent, approach and landing. The pilots chose to leave it engaged and did not take over. So the landing is the system's work, but the sources do not show that the crew could not have landed the aircraft. Garmin, the FAA and the operator all call it an automated system, and none of them calls it AI. The Register describes it choosing landing sites from runway length, distance and fuel range.

record.title: Garmin Autoland lands a King Air B200 at Broomfield, Colorado, in its first real emergency use after the plane loses cabin pressure at 23,000 feet
record.summary: Garmin Autoland engaged when a King Air B200 lost cabin pressure on 20 December 2025. It landed the plane at Rocky Mountain Metropolitan Airport, with the two pilots unhurt.
record.account: On Saturday 20 December 2025 Buffalo River Aviation's Beechcraft Super King Air B200, N479BR, left Aspen-Pitkin County Airport at 1:43 p.m. It carried two pilots and no passengers. At about 23,000 feet it suffered a rapid, uncommanded loss of pressurization. When cabin altitude passed the safe limit, Garmin Autoland engaged automatically. It sent automated emergency broadcasts to air traffic control. The crew chose to leave it engaged. It flew the aircraft to a landing on Runway 30 at Rocky Mountain Metropolitan Airport, Broomfield, Colorado, shortly after 2 p.m. Nobody was treated. The operator said that the aircraft returned to service the next day. The Federal Aviation Administration said that it was investigating. The National Transportation Safety Board said that it was gathering information. Garmin called it the first use of Autoland from start to finish in an actual emergency. On 27 December 2025 AvBrief reported audio that Max Trescott, a host of the NTSB NewsTalk podcast, recorded while flying nearby. The audio shows that with Autoland engaged the crew could transmit only on the guard frequency. It shows that they could not switch to the controllers' frequencies. The National Transportation Safety Board lists nothing for the aircraft in its database of investigations. On 14 October 2026 Garmin reported that more than 2,500 aircraft carry the system. In 2026 Autoland was certified on four more models, which included the first twin-engine jets. No second real-world activation had been reported by then. The two federal agencies had reported no finding on the Colorado flight.
record.purpose: Garmin built Autoland to take complete control of an aircraft and land it when the pilot cannot fly. It engages on its own when the cabin altitude exceeds a set level, as it did here. The two pilots were not incapacitated, though, and chose to let it finish.

ratings.reason: Two pilots who had lost cabin pressure at 23,000 feet were on the ground in Broomfield within about 35 minutes of departure, untreated and uninjured. They were conscious and could have flown the descent themselves. The benefit is a safe automatic recovery, and no source shows a life saved.

Buffalo River Aviation's aircraft “landed safely without incident”, in the airport spokeswoman's words. No damage is reported, and the operator said that the aircraft returned to service the next day.

data.retained_case_account: On Saturday 20 December 2025 Buffalo River Aviation's Beechcraft Super King Air B200, N479BR, left Aspen-Pitkin County Airport at 1:43 p.m. It carried two pilots and no passengers. At about 23,000 ft it suffered a rapid, uncommanded loss of pressurization. When cabin altitude passed the safe limit, Garmin Autoland engaged automatically. It sent automated emergency broadcasts to air traffic control. It flew the aircraft to a landing on Runway 30 at Rocky Mountain Metropolitan Airport, Broomfield, Colorado, shortly after 2 p.m. The crew chose to leave it engaged. Nobody was treated. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said it was investigating and the NTSB that it was gathering information. Garmin called it the first use of Autoland from start to finish in an actual emergency.

fields.account: On Saturday 20 December 2025 Buffalo River Aviation's Beechcraft Super King Air B200, N479BR, left Aspen-Pitkin County Airport at 1:43 p.m. It carried two pilots and no passengers. fields.title: Garmin Autoland lands a King Air B200 at Broomfield, Colorado, in its first real emergency use after the plane loses cabin pressure at 23,000 feet
fields.headline: Garmin Autoland safely lands a depressurized King Air B200

value.role: SHA-256 of the complete public record and its assessments

version.evidence_note: SHA-256 of the public record, its assessments, and its displayed answers and notes, excluding its own identifier and the derived coverage summary.

fields.account: On Saturday 20 December 2025 Buffalo River Aviation's Beechcraft Super King Air B200, N479BR, left Aspen-Pitkin County Airport at 1:43 p.m. It carried two pilots and no passengers. At about 23,000 feet it suffered a rapid, uncommanded loss of pressurization. When cabin altitude passed the safe limit, Garmin Autoland engaged automatically. It sent automated emergency broadcasts to air traffic control. The crew chose to leave it engaged. It flew the aircraft to a landing on Runway 30 at Rocky Mountain Metropolitan Airport, Broomfield, Colorado, shortly after 2 p.m. Nobody was treated. The operator said that the aircraft returned to service the next day. The Federal Aviation Administration said that it was investigating. The National Transportation Safety Board said that it was gathering information. Garmin called it the first use of Autoland from start to finish in an actual emergency. On 27 December 2025 AvBrief reported audio that Max Trescott, a host of the NTSB NewsTalk podcast, recorded while flying nearby. The audio shows that with Autoland engaged the crew could transmit only on the guard frequency. It shows that they could not switch to the controllers' frequencies. The National Transportation Safety Board lists nothing for the aircraft in its database of investigations. On 14 October 2026 Garmin reported that more than 2,500 aircraft carry the system. In 2026 Autoland was certified on four more models, which included the first twin-engine jets. No second real-world activation had been reported by then. The two federal agencies had reported no finding on the Colorado flight.

record.title: The National Energy System Operator's control room runs Open Climate Fix's Quartz Solar, which may avoid £30m a year in imbalance costs
record.summary: Open Climate Fix's machine-learning solar forecast, Quartz Solar, is live in the control room of Great Britain's grid operator. The maker claims at least £30m a year in avoided imbalance costs.
record.account: On 24 April 2025 Open Climate Fix, a not-for-profit, published a case study. In it, the organization said that its forecast service, Quartz Solar, had halved the solar forecast errors of the National Energy System Operator (NESO). Open Climate Fix had already described use in the control room and the same estimated savings in that case study. On 6 November 2025 Open Climate Fix announced that Quartz Solar was live in NESO's control room. Its AI-powered tool for forecasting output from solar panels combines machine learning with live satellite imagery. The tool's inputs include weather data. The Energyst reproduced the announcement on 6 November 2025. In the announcement, Open Climate Fix says that the tool started as a Network Innovation Allowance project. By its account, the tool is now fully integrated from day-ahead scheduling to real-time control. It says that the tool helps avoid at least £30 million in imbalance costs a year. Its figure for the tool's cut in carbon dioxide (CO2) is around 300,000 tonnes. Open Climate Fix says that Quartz Solar has halved large errors. It rates the tool as 2.8 times more accurate than the tools for forecasting solar generation that NESO used before. Open Climate Fix quotes Carolina Tortora, NESO's Head of AI, Digitalisation and Innovation. She says that the tool can accurately predict solar generation up to 36 hours in advance. According to her, it is revolutionizing solar forecasts in the control room. She does not state the £30m figure. On 7 November 2025 pv magazine credited the saving of £30 million (US$39 million) a year to Quartz Solar itself. It reports that Open Climate Fix claims to have halved forecasting errors across about 300 grid supply points. On its website, Open Climate Fix says that NESO uses the forecast daily. The savings are the maker's estimate. The sources contain neither a figure from NESO nor an audited figure. Because Open Climate Fix had already described use in the control room in its case study of April 2025, the first deployment cannot be dated from the announcement of November 2025. On 21 September 2026 the International Energy Agency listed NESO's solar forecasting among early AI deployments. The agency gives estimated savings of £30 million a year in reserve costs as the reported outcome. It makes no measurement of its own.

data.retained_case_account: On 6 November 2025 Open Climate Fix (OCF), a not-for-profit, announced that Quartz Solar was live in the National Energy System Operator's (NESO) control room. OCF's AI-powered solar PV forecasting tool combines machine learning, live satellite imagery and weather data. It is fully integrated from day-ahead scheduling to real-time control after starting as a Network Innovation Allowance project (The Energyst, 6 November 2025). The announcement says the tool helps avoid at least £30 million in imbalance costs a year and cuts around 300,000 tonnes of CO2. NESO's Carolina Tortora, Head of AI, Digitalisation and Innovation, is quoted saying it can accurately predict solar generation up to 36 hours in advance. She says it is revolutionizing solar forecasts in the control room. She does not state the £30m figure. pv magazine (7 November 2025) attributes the £30 million (US$39 million) per year saving to Quartz Solar itself. It reports OCF's claim of halving forecasting errors across about 300 grid supply points. OCF's website says the forecast is used daily by NESO. The savings are the maker's estimate, not an operator-reported or audited figure. OCF’s April 24, 2025 case study already described control-room use and the same estimated savings. The November announcement therefore does not establish the first deployment date.

fields.account: On 24 April 2025 Open Climate Fix, a not-for-profit, published a case study. In it, the organization said that its forecast service, Quartz Solar, had halved the solar forecast errors of the National Energy System Operator (NESO). Open Climate Fix had already described use in the control room and the same estimated savings in that case study. On 6 November 2025 Open Climate Fix announced that Quartz Solar was live in NESO's control room. Its AI-powered tool for forecasting output from solar panels combines machine learning with live satellite imagery. The tool's inputs include weather data. The Energyst reproduced the announcement on 6 November 2025. In the announcement, Open Climate Fix says that the tool started as a Network Innovation Allowance project. By its account, the tool is now fully integrated from day-ahead scheduling to real-time control. It says that the tool helps avoid at least £30 million in imbalance costs a year. Its figure for the tool's cut in carbon dioxide (CO2) is around 300,000 tonnes. Open Climate Fix says that Quartz Solar has halved large errors. It rates the tool as 2.8 times more accurate than the tools for forecasting solar generation that NESO used before. Open Climate Fix quotes Carolina Tortora, NESO's Head of AI, Digitalisation and Innovation. She says that the tool can accurately predict solar generation up to 36 hours in advance. According to her, it is revolutionizing solar forecasts in the control room. She does not state the £30m figure. On 7 November 2025 pv magazine credited the saving of £30 million (US$39 million) a year to Quartz Solar itself. It reports that Open Climate Fix claims to have halved forecasting errors across about 300 grid supply points. On its website, Open Climate Fix says that NESO uses the forecast daily. The savings are the maker's estimate. The sources contain neither a figure from NESO nor an audited figure. Because Open Climate Fix had already described use in the control room in its case study of April 2025, the first deployment cannot be dated from the announcement of November 2025. On 21 September 2026 the International Energy Agency listed NESO's solar forecasting among early AI deployments. The agency gives estimated savings of £30 million a year in reserve costs as the reported outcome. It makes no measurement of its own.

record.title: NHC blended Google DeepMind's AI ensemble into official Hurricane Melissa forecasts before its Category 5 landfall in Jamaica
record.summary: The US National Hurricane Center blended Google DeepMind's AI ensemble into its Melissa forecasts from 21 October 2025. The center's track errors at 120 hours were less than half its five-year mean.
record.account: The US National Hurricane Center (NHC) blended Google DeepMind's experimental AI hurricane model into official forecasts for Tropical Storm Melissa from its first advisory on 21 October 2025. In NHC's guidance, the model's ensemble mean is labeled GDMI. In Discussion 1, the forecasters placed the official track between the DeepMind ensemble mean and the corrected consensus aid HCCA. In Discussion 2, they described the track as a blend of the DeepMind mean, HCCA and the simple consensus TVCA. In Discussion 8, on 23 October, they moved the track toward a blend of the DeepMind mean and HCCA. Later that day, in Discussion 10, they blended the HCCA and GDMI aids. They set an intensity forecast in best agreement with GDMI after all 50 DeepMind members showed a major hurricane. Also on 23 October, the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) approved a CHF 80,000 Imminent DREF (Disaster Response Emergency Fund) allocation with a five-day lead time. On 24 October, in Discussion 13, they noted that every DeepMind member showed the system becoming a Category 4 hurricane or stronger. In Discussion 14, they put the intensity forecast closest to GDMI. On 28 October 2025 Melissa made landfall in southwestern Jamaica near New Hope with winds of 185 miles per hour and a pressure of 892 millibars. The IFRC reported 45 deaths and about 1.6 million people affected. It relayed an estimate by the World Bank and the Inter-American Development Bank of US$8.8 billion in physical damage. On 3 November 2025 Michael Lowry, a hurricane specialist, wrote that the model gave NHC forecasters extra confidence to issue uncharacteristically aggressive forecasts. CNN reported on 3 December 2025 that the DeepMind ensemble gave NHC forecasters an unusually high degree of confidence in Melissa's rapid intensification about three days before landfall. In its own report on Melissa, first issued on 25 February 2026, NHC says that this was the first time it had predicted Category 5 strength from a Category 1 start. Its errors in the track of Melissa at 120 hours were less than half its five-year mean. The DeepMind ensemble mean alone had lower track errors than the official forecast at 48 hours, 32.6 against 40.3 nautical miles. At 120 hours its errors were higher, 113.2 against 87.7 nautical miles. In its verification report for 2025, dated 30 March 2026, NHC says that its track errors were well below average for major hurricanes, including Melissa.

ratings.reason: The National Hurricane Center has not credited the AI guidance with an outcome for any individual. The impacts reported cover only the population as a whole.

NHC forecasters blended the DeepMind ensemble into official track forecasts from Discussion 1 and set intensity forecasts closest to it from Discussion 10. Melissa's official track error at 120 hours was 87.7 nautical miles, against a five-year mean of 185.4 nautical miles. NHC's Science Operations Officer called the AI guidance very valuable for Melissa.

No cited report shows that the AI guidance changed preparations or losses in Jamaica. The forecasts covered a Category 5 landfall that affected about 1.6 million people, and the IFRC approved its emergency allocation five days ahead.

data.retained_case_account: The US National Hurricane Center (NHC) blended Google DeepMind's experimental AI hurricane model (ensemble mean GDMI) into official forecasts for Tropical Storm Melissa. It did so from its first advisory, 21 October 2025. Discussion 1 placed the official track between the DeepMind ensemble mean and the consensus aid HCCA. Discussion 2 described the track as a blend of the DeepMind mean, HCCA and TVCA. Discussion 8 (23 October) moved the track toward a blend of the DeepMind mean and HCCA. Discussion 10 blended the HCCA and GDMI aids. It set an intensity forecast in best agreement with GDMI after all 50 DeepMind members showed a major hurricane. On 28 October 2025 Melissa made landfall in southwestern Jamaica near New Hope with 185 mph winds and 892 mb pressure. IFRC reported 45 deaths and about 1.6 million people affected. It relayed a World Bank/IDB estimate of US$8.8 billion in physical damage. Its CHF 80,000 Imminent DREF was approved on 23 October with a five-day lead time.
