record.title: A passenger's iPhone Crash Detection sends a “strong impact” alert to the local fire service before a sightseeing helicopter near Mount Aso goes missing, 20 January 2026
record.summary: Apple Crash Detection on a passenger's iPhone called the fire service about 46 minutes before the operator reported a sightseeing helicopter missing near Mount Aso. All three aboard died.
record.account: On 20 January 2026 a sightseeing helicopter operated by Takumi Aviation of Okayama took off from Aso Cadre Dominion at 10:52 Japan time and lost contact at 11:04. It carried a pilot in his sixties and two Taiwanese passengers (a 41-year-old man and a 36-year-old woman). Police told Jiji Press that the automatic call reached the fire service at 11:04 on 20 January 2026. They said that the operator's agent reported the helicopter missing at about 11:50. The Asahi Shimbun cited the fire service as saying that the call came from near the Nakadake crater. Jiji reported that the helicopter's GPS track also ended near the crater. Storm Media Japan, drawing on fire-service information, wrote that the phone function gave the search its first important lead. That afternoon a police helicopter found an object believed to be the helicopter around the first crater of Mount Aso's Nakadake. On 21 January 2026 Taiwan's SETN, citing Japanese media, reported that the local fire department had received a “strong impact” notification from a passenger's phone. It came before contact was lost. The notification apparently came from the iPhone Crash Detection feature. Callbacks to the phone failed. SETN does not cite a named Japanese agency. It quotes a firefighter on crash detection in general. It quotes a nurse. On 18 February 2026 the fire department said that bodies believed to be those of the three occupants had been found inside the crater. Apple's feature, on iPhone 14 and later, uses motion sensors with an algorithm on the device. It calls emergency services after a 10-second countdown. The link to transport safety is indirect. The device alerted responders to an aviation crash that it did not prevent.

fields.account: On 20 January 2026 a sightseeing helicopter operated by Takumi Aviation of Okayama took off from Aso Cadre Dominion at 10:52 Japan time and lost contact at 11:04. It carried a pilot in his sixties and two Taiwanese passengers (a 41-year-old man and a 36-year-old woman). Police told Jiji Press that the automatic call reached the fire service at 11:04 on 20 January 2026. They said that the operator's agent reported the helicopter missing at about 11:50. The Asahi Shimbun cited the fire service as saying that the call came from near the Nakadake crater. Jiji reported that the helicopter's GPS track also ended near the crater. Storm Media Japan, drawing on fire-service information, wrote that the phone function gave the search its first important lead. That afternoon a police helicopter found an object believed to be the helicopter around the first crater of Mount Aso's Nakadake. On 21 January 2026 Taiwan's SETN, citing Japanese media, reported that the local fire department had received a “strong impact” notification from a passenger's phone. It came before contact was lost. The notification apparently came from the iPhone Crash Detection feature. Callbacks to the phone failed. SETN does not cite a named Japanese agency. It quotes a firefighter on crash detection in general. It quotes a nurse. On 18 February 2026 the fire department said that bodies believed to be those of the three occupants had been found inside the crater. Apple's feature, on iPhone 14 and later, uses motion sensors with an algorithm on the device. It calls emergency services after a 10-second countdown. The link to transport safety is indirect. The device alerted responders to an aviation crash that it did not prevent.

record.title: An operator in Kazakhstan reroutes gas to stop a methane leak from a pipeline after a United Nations satellite alert, but new emissions appear at the site by May 2026
record.summary: After an alert from UNEP's Methane Alert and Response System, which uses AI, an operator in Kazakhstan rerouted gas to stop a pipeline leak. By 21 May 2026 UNEP had observed new emissions there.
record.account: The International Methane Emissions Observatory (IMEO) of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) publishes a case document of its Methane Alert and Response System (MARS) for source KAZ_S_136. On its MARS page, UNEP states that IMEO combines data from more than 30 satellite instruments, scientific expertise and advanced AI models. It uses them to notify governments. It notifies companies. The source is an oil-and-gas pipeline in Kazakhstan at 43.39767°, 52.49505°. UNEP gives only coordinates in the case document. UNEP records first detection in September 2025, a plume imaged by the EnMAP instrument of the German Aerospace Center (DLR) on 29 October 2025 and estimated emissions of 1,200 tonnes. The operator transferred the gas flow from the affected pipeline to another pipeline, stopping the emissions. Mitigation was reported on 26 November 2025. The document shows that emissions were last detected on 12 March 2026. UNEP updated it on 15 April 2026. On 5 May 2026 The Chemical Engineer relayed UNEP's snapshot. It counted one Kazakhstan source among six that stopped emitting in 2026 after MARS alerts. In a footnote to the case document, UNEP states that as of 21 May 2026 IMEO had observed subsequent methane emissions at the location. UNEP states that IMEO continues to engage stakeholders. In its September 2026 snapshot, UNEP reports a confirmed mitigation of a Kazakhstan gas pipeline that released an estimated 365 tonnes over one month. The Chemical Engineer gives no case identifier in its report. UNEP gives no case identifier in its September snapshot, so whether these reports concern KAZ_S_136 is unknown. In its October 2026 snapshot, UNEP reports a separate pipeline leak in Kazakhstan, of an estimated 200 tonnes over one week, that was mitigated after a MARS notification. It gives no case identifier. On 22 October 2026, on its MARS case studies page, UNEP named the site as Kamenistoe. It still listed KAZ_S_136 as a mitigation case for March 2026.

data.retained_case_account: UNEP's International Methane Emissions Observatory (IMEO) publishes a Methane Alert and Response System (MARS) case document for source KAZ_S_136. It is an oil-and-gas pipeline in Kazakhstan at 43.39767°, 52.49505°. The document gives coordinates only. The document records first detection in September 2025, a plume imaged by DLR's EnMAP on 29 October 2025 and estimated emissions of 1,200 tonnes. The operator transferred the gas flow from the affected pipeline to another pipeline, stopping the emissions. Mitigation was reported on 26 November 2025. Last emissions were detected on 12 March 2026 (document updated 15 April 2026). A footnote states that as of 21 May 2026 IMEO observed subsequent methane emissions at the location and continues to engage stakeholders. UNEP's MARS page states that IMEO uses data from more than 30 satellite instruments coupled with scientific expertise and advanced AI models. It uses them to notify governments and companies. The Chemical Engineer (5 May 2026), relaying UNEP's snapshot, counts one Kazakhstan source among six that stopped emitting in 2026 after MARS alerts. UNEP's September 2026 snapshot reports a confirmed Kazakhstan gas-pipeline mitigation of an estimated 365 tonnes over one month. Neither gives a case ID, so their correspondence to KAZ_S_136 is not established.

fields.account: The International Methane Emissions Observatory (IMEO) of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) publishes a case document of its Methane Alert and Response System (MARS) for source KAZ_S_136. On its MARS page, UNEP states that IMEO combines data from more than 30 satellite instruments, scientific expertise and advanced AI models. It uses them to notify governments. It notifies companies. The source is an oil-and-gas pipeline in Kazakhstan at 43.39767°, 52.49505°. UNEP gives only coordinates in the case document. UNEP records first detection in September 2025, a plume imaged by the EnMAP instrument of the German Aerospace Center (DLR) on 29 October 2025 and estimated emissions of 1,200 tonnes. The operator transferred the gas flow from the affected pipeline to another pipeline, stopping the emissions. Mitigation was reported on 26 November 2025. The document shows that emissions were last detected on 12 March 2026. UNEP updated it on 15 April 2026. On 5 May 2026 The Chemical Engineer relayed UNEP's snapshot. It counted one Kazakhstan source among six that stopped emitting in 2026 after MARS alerts. In a footnote to the case document, UNEP states that as of 21 May 2026 IMEO had observed subsequent methane emissions at the location. UNEP states that IMEO continues to engage stakeholders. In its September 2026 snapshot, UNEP reports a confirmed mitigation of a Kazakhstan gas pipeline that released an estimated 365 tonnes over one month. The Chemical Engineer gives no case identifier in its report. UNEP gives no case identifier in its September snapshot, so whether these reports concern KAZ_S_136 is unknown. In its October 2026 snapshot, UNEP reports a separate pipeline leak in Kazakhstan, of an estimated 200 tonnes over one week, that was mitigated after a MARS notification. It gives no case identifier. On 22 October 2026, on its MARS case studies page, UNEP named the site as Kamenistoe. It still listed KAZ_S_136 as a mitigation case for March 2026.

value.text: Mitigation was reported on 26 November 2025, and emissions were last detected on 12 March 2026. A footnote records subsequent emissions at the site as of 21 May 2026, although UNEP still listed the case as a mitigation on 22 October 2026.

fields.summary: After an alert from UNEP's Methane Alert and Response System, which uses AI, an operator in Kazakhstan rerouted gas to stop a pipeline leak. By 21 May 2026 UNEP had observed new emissions there.
fields.account: The International Methane Emissions Observatory (IMEO) of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) publishes a case document of its Methane Alert and Response System (MARS) for source KAZ_S_136. On its MARS page, UNEP states that IMEO combines data from more than 30 satellite instruments, scientific expertise and advanced AI models. It uses them to notify governments. It notifies companies. The source is an oil-and-gas pipeline in Kazakhstan at 43.39767°, 52.49505°. UNEP gives only coordinates in the case document. UNEP records first detection in September 2025, a plume imaged by the EnMAP instrument of the German Aerospace Center (DLR) on 29 October 2025 and estimated emissions of 1,200 tonnes. The operator transferred the gas flow from the affected pipeline to another pipeline, stopping the emissions. Mitigation was reported on 26 November 2025. The document shows that emissions were last detected on 12 March 2026. UNEP updated it on 15 April 2026. On 5 May 2026 The Chemical Engineer relayed UNEP's snapshot. It counted one Kazakhstan source among six that stopped emitting in 2026 after MARS alerts. In a footnote to the case document, UNEP states that as of 21 May 2026 IMEO had observed subsequent methane emissions at the location. UNEP states that IMEO continues to engage stakeholders. In its September 2026 snapshot, UNEP reports a confirmed mitigation of a Kazakhstan gas pipeline that released an estimated 365 tonnes over one month. The Chemical Engineer gives no case identifier in its report. UNEP gives no case identifier in its September snapshot, so whether these reports concern KAZ_S_136 is unknown. In its October 2026 snapshot, UNEP reports a separate pipeline leak in Kazakhstan, of an estimated 200 tonnes over one week, that was mitigated after a MARS notification. It gives no case identifier. On 22 October 2026, on its MARS case studies page, UNEP named the site as Kamenistoe. It still listed KAZ_S_136 as a mitigation case for March 2026.

details.label: Focus
details.value: Public safety

details.label: Purpose
details.value: Sheng Siong rolled out its AI-driven facial recognition CCTV system in April 2024 to identify repeat shoplifters and flag their return. It worked with the Singapore Police Force under its Shop Theft for Retailers (STAR) program. In August 2025 it announced an extension to all 83 outlets. Staff upload the photograph of a suspect identified from footage, and the system alerts store managers' phones when that person enters any branch. Sheng Siong said that thefts per store rose from 4.91 in 2023 to 8 in 2024, and its CEO credited the rise to catching cases that the human eye had missed.

details.label: Contribution of the AI
details.value: The system's documented contribution came after a human detection. On 10 September 2025 a staff member found discrepancies in a stock check. Colleagues reviewed CCTV and saw the woman leaving without paying. They uploaded her face. The Straits Times reports that the system “then automatically identified the other instances” of theft. That turned one observed theft into an amalgamated charge covering seven visits. On 11 September the system's alert reached the retail manager's phone when she entered. He intercepted her at the self-checkout kiosk with three unscanned bottles. The interception, the bag check, the police call, the prosecution and the restitution were human and institutional. Sheng Siong has not named the vendor or the model, given an accuracy figure or reported a false match in this case.

record.title: After a stock check at the Punggol Central outlet on 10 September 2025, Sheng Siong's staff give its facial-recognition CCTV a shoplifter's face. It matches her to six earlier wine thefts. It alerts the manager's phone when she returns at noon the next day. Staff stop her with three unscanned bottles. Police arrest her. She repays the chain. On 12 May 2026 she is jailed eight days
record.summary: Sheng Siong's facial recognition system matched a wine thief to six prior thefts and flagged her return, which led to her arrest, restitution and an eight-day jail term.
record.account: A 51-year-old woman took 19 Jacob's Creek wine bottles worth about S$556 from the Sheng Siong supermarket at Block 622D Punggol Central, Singapore. She bagged them unscanned at self-checkout from 2 to 11 September 2025. On 10 September staff found stock discrepancies. They reviewed closed-circuit television (CCTV). They uploaded her face to the chain's AI-driven facial recognition system. It automatically identified the earlier thefts. When she returned at noon on 11 September the retail manager got a phone alert. He stopped her at the self-checkout kiosk. He found three unscanned bottles. Police arrested her. The Straits Times reports that the alert and the interception happened at noon on 11 September 2025. Something similar followed at the chain's Sin Ming Avenue outlet, where the system alerted staff on 1 October 2025 to a woman who had stolen on 12 visits. On 12 May 2026 District Judge Brenda Chua jailed the woman for eight days on an amalgamated theft charge after full restitution of about S$470. The woman caught at the Sin Ming Avenue outlet was jailed for one week on 8 October 2026.

produced_by: A chain-wide facial recognition layer on existing CCTV (rolled out from April 2024, extended to all 83 outlets after August 2025). Staff upload a suspect's face, and managers get app alerts when that person re-enters any branch.
A human trigger: a stock check on 10 September 2025 that revealed missing bottles. Staff then reviewed the footage and uploaded the face the same day.
A repeat offender who came back to the same outlet at noon the next day, which gave the alert something to fire on.

A manager on the premises with his phone, able to intercept at the self-checkout kiosk. A police and court process (the STAR program, an amalgamated theft charge) that turned the identification into restitution and a sentence.
must_hold: The system identifies, it does not detect. Stock counts or staff still have to notice the first theft. Sheng Siong's CEO implied as much when he said the human eye had missed cases.
Someone must act on the alert within minutes. The gain here was an interception before she left the store, not the alert itself.
The match must be right and lawful. A wrong face flagged at the door would produce a wrongful stop. No source reports a false match in this case. None names the vendor or any accuracy figure.

fields.account: A 51-year-old woman took 19 Jacob's Creek wine bottles worth about S$556 from the Sheng Siong supermarket at Block 622D Punggol Central, Singapore. She bagged them unscanned at self-checkout from 2 to 11 September 2025. On 10 September staff found stock discrepancies. They reviewed closed-circuit television (CCTV). They uploaded her face to the chain's AI-driven facial recognition system. It automatically identified the earlier thefts. When she returned at noon on 11 September the retail manager got a phone alert. He stopped her at the self-checkout kiosk. He found three unscanned bottles. Police arrested her. The Straits Times reports that the alert and the interception happened at noon on 11 September 2025. Something similar followed at the chain's Sin Ming Avenue outlet, where the system alerted staff on 1 October 2025 to a woman who had stolen on 12 visits. On 12 May 2026 District Judge Brenda Chua jailed the woman for eight days on an amalgamated theft charge after full restitution of about S$470. The woman caught at the Sin Ming Avenue outlet was jailed for one week on 8 October 2026.

value.text: The benefit was a single interception on 11 September 2025. Restitution followed, and on 12 May 2026 a district judge jailed the shoplifter for eight days. On 1 October 2025 the system flagged a different repeat shoplifter at the chain's Sin Ming Avenue outlet. That case repeats the benefit elsewhere in the chain. It does not establish persistence in this case.

fields.purpose: Sheng Siong rolled out its AI-driven facial recognition CCTV system in April 2024 to identify repeat shoplifters and flag their return. It worked with the Singapore Police Force under its Shop Theft for Retailers (STAR) program. In August 2025 it announced an extension to all 83 outlets. Staff upload the photograph of a suspect identified from footage, and the system alerts store managers' phones when that person enters any branch. Sheng Siong said that thefts per store rose from 4.91 in 2023 to 8 in 2024, and its CEO credited the rise to catching cases that the human eye had missed.

A repeat offender who came back to the same outlet at noon the next day, which gave the alert something to fire on.

details.value: Students at Karadeniz Technical University built the system to warn phones of an earthquake before the shaking arrives. The alert came during the team's own presentation to members of parliament, before the Kulu quake was felt.

details.label: Contribution of the AI
details.value: DHA calls the system yapay zeka tabanlı (AI-based), following the students' description. None of the reports explains how it detects quakes, what data it uses or whether the alert time was logged. record.account: On 15 May 2025 software-engineering students from Karadeniz Technical University were presenting their Erken Uyarı Merkezi (Early Warning Center) to members of parliament. fields.summary: Erken Uyarı Merkezi, an AI-based app built by Karadeniz Technical University students, alerted their phones about 30 seconds before a quake was felt at Turkey's parliament.
fields.account: On 15 May 2025 software-engineering students from Karadeniz Technical University were presenting their Erken Uyarı Merkezi (Early Warning Center) to members of parliament. The news agency DHA describes it as an AI-based system that warns of earthquakes early. The presentation took place in the Public Relations building of the Turkish parliament (TBMM) in Ankara. During it, a quake centered in Kulu, Konya, was felt in the capital. DHA gave the magnitude as 5.2. The U.S. Geological Survey recorded M5.0 at 15:46 local time (12:46:37 UTC), 14 km east-north-east of Kulu at 10 km depth. Student Birkan Yılmaz said that notifications had reached their phones 30 seconds before the quake. Students went outside. Some members of parliament went outside. Building staff went outside. None of the cited reports mentions damage or injuries.

details.value: If the reports are right, Google's system produced the alert from start to finish. Google's servers combined signals from the accelerometers of many phones to detect the quake and then pushed alerts ahead of the slower waves. Google described the method in 2020, and authors described it in Science in 2025. Google does not use the words AI or machine learning on its pages. In the abstract of the Science paper, the authors write of smartphone-based earthquake detection algorithms. The claim that alerts arrived seconds before the shaking rests on unattributed statements in four Greek outlets within a day of the quake. None quotes a recipient, a seismologist or Google, and no confirmation of this event from Google has been found.

record.title: Google's Android Earthquake Alerts System reached phones in Crete and the Dodecanese seconds before a magnitude 6.0 quake near Kasos on 14 May 2025
record.summary: Google's Android Earthquake Alerts System sent Android users in Crete and the Dodecanese a warning seconds before a magnitude 6.0 quake near Kasos on 14 May 2025.
record.account: Google switched on its Android Earthquake Alerts System in Greece on 28 April 2021. In Europe the system detects quakes with the accelerometers in phones and uses no seismographs. On 23 April 2025 the magnitude 6.2 Marmara Ereğlisi earthquake struck Türkiye. Google's team reports that the system detected it 5.31 seconds after it began. They report that it alerted more than 16 million users. Three weeks later, at 01:51 local time on Wednesday 14 May 2025 (22:51 UTC on 13 May), an earthquake struck between Kasos and Karpathos. The U.S. Geological Survey put its magnitude at 6.0. Greek reporters put it at 6.1. It was centered 20 km south-south-east of Fry on Kasos, at 76 km depth. The U.S. Geological Survey logged 931 felt reports and a green alert level. On 14 and 15 May Newsbomb, GizChina Greece, in.gr and Alphafreepress reported that the system notified users in Crete, the Dodecanese and farther away seconds before the shaking. Notice came by message with an audible signal similar to the 112 alert. None of the reports names a recipient. None gives a lead time in seconds. None mentions damage or injuries. On 15 October 2026 Google extended the service to more than 200 regions.

produced_by: A magnitude 6.0 (USGS) quake above the system's 4.5 alert threshold, centered offshore south of Kasos at about 76 km depth. A push alert could therefore outrun the slower waves to Crete and the Dodecanese.

Enough Android phones near the epicentre with the Earthquake Alerts setting on to trigger Google's server-side detection. In Europe the system uses the accelerometers in phones instead of seismographs (in.gr).
Receiving phones with location (GPS) enabled and an internet connection, which Alphafreepress lists as requirements for the alerts
must_hold: The server's magnitude and location estimate must be right and early. The 2025 Science paper reports that only 36% of alert recipients got the alert before shaking.
Recipients must know what to do with seconds of notice. The Greek reports document no protective action by anyone who received the alert.
The phone must have the Earthquake Alerts setting enabled (Alphafreepress: Settings > Safety & Emergency > Earthquake Alerts). The feature must be supported in the region.

data.retained_case_account: At 01:51 local time on Wednesday 14 May 2025 (22:51 UTC on 13 May) a magnitude 6.0 (USGS; Greek outlets 6.1) earthquake struck. It struck 20 km south-south-east of Fry on Kasos, between Kasos and Karpathos, at 76 km depth. USGS logged 931 felt reports and a green alert level. Newsbomb, GizChina Greece, in.gr and Alphafreepress reported on 14 and 15 May on Google's Android Earthquake Alerts System. In Europe it detects quakes from phone accelerometers rather than seismographs. It notified users in Crete, the Dodecanese and farther away seconds before the shaking. Notice came by message and an audible signal similar to the 112 alert. None of the reports names a recipient, gives a lead time in seconds, or mentions damage or injuries.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: If the reports are right, the alert was produced end to end by Google's system. Accelerometer triggers from many phones were combined on Google's servers to detect the quake. Alerts were then pushed ahead of the slower waves, as Google's 2020 description and the 2025 Science paper set out. Google's own pages do not use the words AI or machine learning. The Science abstract speaks of smartphone-based earthquake detection algorithms. That alerts arrived seconds before shaking rests on unattributed statements in four Greek outlets published within a day of the quake. None quotes a recipient, a seismologist or Google. No Google per-event confirmation was found.

fields.account: Google switched on its Android Earthquake Alerts System in Greece on 28 April 2021. In Europe the system detects quakes with the accelerometers in phones and uses no seismographs. On 23 April 2025 the magnitude 6.2 Marmara Ereğlisi earthquake struck Türkiye. Google's team reports that the system detected it 5.31 seconds after it began. They report that it alerted more than 16 million users. Three weeks later, at 01:51 local time on Wednesday 14 May 2025 (22:51 UTC on 13 May), an earthquake struck between Kasos and Karpathos. The U.S. Geological Survey put its magnitude at 6.0. Greek reporters put it at 6.1. It was centered 20 km south-south-east of Fry on Kasos, at 76 km depth. The U.S. Geological Survey logged 931 felt reports and a green alert level. On 14 and 15 May Newsbomb, GizChina Greece, in.gr and Alphafreepress reported that the system notified users in Crete, the Dodecanese and farther away seconds before the shaking. Notice came by message with an audible signal similar to the 112 alert. None of the reports names a recipient. None gives a lead time in seconds. None mentions damage or injuries. On 15 October 2026 Google extended the service to more than 200 regions.

display.answer: Observed 14 May 2025. The quake struck at 01:51 local time on Wednesday 14 May 2025 (22:51 UTC on 13 May, per USGS), and the alerts went out seconds before the shaking. In.gr, writing on Thursday 15 May, places the quake in the early hours of Wednesday.

produced_by: A magnitude 6.0 (USGS) quake above the system's 4.5 alert threshold, centered offshore south of Kasos at about 76 km depth. A push alert could therefore outrun the slower waves to Crete and the Dodecanese.

Enough Android phones near the epicentre with the Earthquake Alerts setting on to trigger Google's server-side detection. In Europe the system uses the accelerometers in phones instead of seismographs (in.gr).
Receiving phones with location (GPS) enabled and an internet connection, which Alphafreepress lists as requirements for the alerts
must_hold: The server's magnitude and location estimate must be right and early. The 2025 Science paper reports that only 36% of alert recipients got the alert before shaking.
Recipients must know what to do with seconds of notice. The Greek reports document no protective action by anyone who received the alert.
The phone must have the Earthquake Alerts setting enabled (Alphafreepress: Settings > Safety & Emergency > Earthquake Alerts). The feature must be supported in the region.

fields.account: Google switched on its Android Earthquake Alerts System in Greece on 28 April 2021. In Europe the system detects quakes with the accelerometers in phones and uses no seismographs. On 23 April 2025 the magnitude 6.2 Marmara Ereğlisi earthquake struck Türkiye. Google's team reports that the system detected it 5.31 seconds after it began. They report that it alerted more than 16 million users. Three weeks later, at 01:51 local time on Wednesday 14 May 2025 (22:51 UTC on 13 May), an earthquake struck between Kasos and Karpathos. The U.S. Geological Survey put its magnitude at 6.0. Greek reporters put it at 6.1. It was centered 20 km south-south-east of Fry on Kasos, at 76 km depth. The U.S. Geological Survey logged 931 felt reports and a green alert level. On 14 and 15 May Newsbomb, GizChina Greece, in.gr and Alphafreepress reported that the system notified users in Crete, the Dodecanese and farther away seconds before the shaking. Notice came by message with an audible signal similar to the 112 alert. None of the reports names a recipient. None gives a lead time in seconds. None mentions damage or injuries. On 15 October 2026 Google extended the service to more than 200 regions.

produced_by: A magnitude 6.0 (USGS) quake above the system's 4.5 alert threshold, centered offshore south of Kasos at about 76 km depth. A push alert could therefore outrun the slower waves to Crete and the Dodecanese.

Recipients must know what to do with seconds of notice. The Greek reports document no protective action by anyone who received the alert.
The phone must have the Earthquake Alerts setting enabled (Alphafreepress: Settings > Safety & Emergency > Earthquake Alerts). The feature must be supported in the region.

record.title: The HALO Trust trains AI, supported by Amazon Web Services, to find explosive remnants in drone imagery of Ukrainian minefields. It reaches about 70% accuracy. No clearance outcome is attributed to it
record.summary: The HALO Trust's AI detects mines in drone imagery of Ukrainian minefields with about 70% accuracy. HALO says that it cuts analysis from days to hours. No cleared land is credited to it.
record.account: The HALO Trust announced a US$4 million package of support from Amazon Web Services on 26 June 2024. An archived copy of the page, dated 20 May 2026, is among the sources. The package “will enable HALO to trial artificial intelligence (AI) to assist in the process of detecting debris of war (including landmines and other explosives) in drone imagery for existing minefields and battlefields in Ukraine”. The package covers machine-learning detection of damaged buildings in satellite imagery with SageMaker. By then HALO had flown 542 drone flights over Ukrainian minefields, producing 11 terabytes of imagery. HALO said that training would require manually labeling thousands of images. It said that training would require ongoing vetting by HALO staff to remove false results. On a page of 21 February 2025, HALO describes the pilot through its head of research and development, Matthew Abercrombie. He says that an analyst “can take three to five days to look through the imagery for an average minefield”. HALO reports no results there. On 24 April 2026 HALO wrote that Prince Harry had flown an AI-powered drone at one of its sites near Bucha. HALO said that its AI models now analyze terrain in hours where manual assessments took days. It gave no measured figure. Reuters (Sergiy Karazy, 30 April 2026, syndicated by KELO) reported from Myrotske, 40 km northwest of Kyiv. It reported that HALO “has turned to AI to analyse high-resolution drone imagery of contaminated areas and train systems to identify mines and explosive remnants, achieving around 70% accuracy already”. It quoted HALO media manager Olena Shustova. Reuters does not mention Amazon Web Services. It credits no cleared land to the model. It credits no found mine to it. It credits no time saving to it. No later milestone is dated.

fields.summary: The HALO Trust's AI detects mines in drone imagery of Ukrainian minefields with about 70% accuracy. HALO says that it cuts analysis from days to hours. No cleared land is credited to it.
fields.account: The HALO Trust announced a US$4 million package of support from Amazon Web Services on 26 June 2024. An archived copy of the page, dated 20 May 2026, is among the sources. The package “will enable HALO to trial artificial intelligence (AI) to assist in the process of detecting debris of war (including landmines and other explosives) in drone imagery for existing minefields and battlefields in Ukraine”. The package covers machine-learning detection of damaged buildings in satellite imagery with SageMaker. By then HALO had flown 542 drone flights over Ukrainian minefields, producing 11 terabytes of imagery. HALO said that training would require manually labeling thousands of images. It said that training would require ongoing vetting by HALO staff to remove false results. On a page of 21 February 2025, HALO describes the pilot through its head of research and development, Matthew Abercrombie. He says that an analyst “can take three to five days to look through the imagery for an average minefield”. HALO reports no results there. On 24 April 2026 HALO wrote that Prince Harry had flown an AI-powered drone at one of its sites near Bucha. HALO said that its AI models now analyze terrain in hours where manual assessments took days. It gave no measured figure. Reuters (Sergiy Karazy, 30 April 2026, syndicated by KELO) reported from Myrotske, 40 km northwest of Kyiv. It reported that HALO “has turned to AI to analyse high-resolution drone imagery of contaminated areas and train systems to identify mines and explosive remnants, achieving around 70% accuracy already”. It quoted HALO media manager Olena Shustova. Reuters does not mention Amazon Web Services. It credits no cleared land to the model. It credits no found mine to it. It credits no time saving to it. No later milestone is dated.

record.title: Dudhwa Tiger Reserve officials identify armed poachers from images that a TrailGuard AI camera in Kishanpur Wildlife Sanctuary transmits on two dates
record.summary: A TrailGuard AI camera in Kishanpur Wildlife Sanctuary sent officials images of armed poachers on two dates in 2022. Officials identified them. Its makers later claimed arrests.
record.account: Dertien, Negi, Dinerstein and colleagues (BioScience 73(10):748–757, published online 14 September 2023) report deploying the TrailGuard AI camera-alert system. The system “runs on-the-edge artificial intelligence algorithms to detect tigers and poachers and transmit real-time images”. It was deployed in the Kanha-Pench corridor and in Dudhwa Tiger Reserve, Uttar Pradesh. The authors state that the seven Dudhwa units ran from early September 2022 to mid-December 2022. All seven transmitted images. Three sent objects of interest to forest department officials. “One unit within Kishanpur Wildlife Sanctuary captured a group of poachers carrying a gun and knives on two separate dates, and a presumably poached chital (Axis axis) on the second detection”. The authors do not give the dates of the detections, so the two detections of poachers can be placed only within the deployment period. Tigers were detected at the same spot three days before the second poacher detection. “Authorities were able to quickly identify the individuals via the transmitted images and were investigating the matter”. The authors include RESOLVE and CVEDIA staff (the system's developers) alongside Dudhwa Tiger Reserve, Wildlife Institute of India and Global Tiger Forum co-authors. A Clemson University release of 15 September 2023 carries Nightjar and RESOLVE boilerplate. In the release, Clemson University states that the alerts “led the authorities to the arrest of these individuals for poaching a few weeks later”. Clemson quotes Sanjay Kumar Pathak, former field director of Dudhwa, as saying that the system “led to the detection and arrest of poachers in Dudhwa”. The Hindu (16 September 2023) cited a person involved in the experiment as saying that poachers caught on camera had helped forest authorities secure a conviction a year later. It quoted Piyush Yadav of Nightjar, the manufacturer: “A year down, these poachers were arrested with images from TrailGuard playing a key role”. The article's lead puts the capture in Kanha-Pench. It puts the Yadav quote in Dudhwa. Agence France-Presse (Taipei Times, 6 October 2023) reported the authors' claim of “identifying a team of poachers”. No statement from the forest department about an arrest was found. No court record of one was found. It names no reserve. It does not name a case.

The paper does not date the detections. The system “runs on-the-edge artificial intelligence algorithms to detect tigers and poachers and transmit real-time images”. It was deployed in the Kanha-Pench corridor and in Dudhwa Tiger Reserve, Uttar Pradesh. All seven Dudhwa units transmitted images; three transmitted objects of interest to forest department officials. “One unit within Kishanpur Wildlife Sanctuary captured a group of poachers carrying a gun and knives on two separate dates, and a presumably poached chital (Axis axis) on the second detection”. “Authorities were able to quickly identify the individuals via the transmitted images and were investigating the matter”. Tigers were detected at the same spot three days before the second poacher detection. The authors include RESOLVE and CVEDIA staff (the system's developers) alongside Dudhwa Tiger Reserve, Wildlife Institute of India and Global Tiger Forum co-authors. AFP (Taipei Times, 6 October 2023) reported the study's claim of “identifying a team of poachers”. A Clemson University release of 15 September 2023 carries Nightjar/RESOLVE boilerplate. It states that the alerts “led the authorities to the arrest of these individuals for poaching a few weeks later”. It quotes Sanjay Kumar Pathak, former field director of Dudhwa, that the system “led to the detection and arrest of poachers in Dudhwa”. The Hindu (16 September 2023) cited a person involved in the experiment. Poachers caught on camera had a year later helped forest authorities secure a conviction. It quoted Piyush Yadav of Nightjar, the manufacturer, that “A year down, these poachers were arrested with images from TrailGuard playing a key role”. The article's lead puts the capture in Kanha-Pench and the Yadav quote in Dudhwa. No forest-department statement or court record of an arrest was found.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: The camera's on-board classifier filtered motion triggers to people and tigers and transmitted the poachers' images to officials' phones within about a minute. Identification and investigation were done by officials. The peer-reviewed account is co-authored by the developers (RESOLVE, CVEDIA) with Dudhwa and Wildlife Institute of India staff and stops at “investigating”. The arrest claim rests on a Clemson release quoting the ex-field director, developer press releases and The Hindu quoting the manufacturer and an unnamed participant.

record.title: Rainforest Connection's Guardian, an acoustic AI, flags chainsaws to patrollers in West Sumatra, one of whom says that logging stopped
record.summary: Rainforest Connection's Guardian sensors use AI to detect chainsaws. They alert patrols. In West Sumatra an alert led a patrol to a logger in August 2019. A patroller said that logging stopped.
record.account: Rainforest Connection (RFCx), a US non-profit founded by Topher White, deploys solar-powered “Guardian” acoustic sensors. In its own words, they use “sound & artificial intelligence” to track chainsaws. The sensors pick out vehicle engines. Hunting dogs are tracked. They track gunshots. They send real-time alerts to a mobile app so that “an agent nearby” can respond. On its impact page, RFCx states that it has protected over 726,000 hectares across 8,662+ projects in 137 countries. Its guardian page gives 750,000 hectares. Antara reported on a KKI Warsi press conference on 16 July 2020. There, Warsi said that the first 12 Guardian units went up in July 2019 in Sirukam and other nagari forests. In August 2019, a Guardian alert led the Sirukam patrol to a logger. The patrol caught the logger, who then escaped. Warsi counted 12 chainsaw alerts from sensors at 17 sites. It said that not all of them were illegal. A Thomson Reuters Foundation report published by The Straits Times on 11 February 2021 is the one independent account. It is from Solok regency, West Sumatra, Indonesia, where 27 Guardian sensors had been installed more than a year earlier. Audio streams are analyzed by AI trained to pick out chainsaw sounds. An alert goes to community patrols. Patroller Jasrialdi said that logging “has totally stopped” in the area. The head of West Sumatra's forestry department, Yozarwardi Usama Putra, said that he would like to expand the “early-warning system”. The reporters credit the decline in logging partly to a wider enforcement crackdown. They report that about 200 of Sirukam's 6,000 residents had worked in illegal logging. One former logger quit in 2018, before the sensors, because of the crackdown. The reporters add that RFCx planned to collect data for peer review to prove that the system curbs logging. No document from a park authority shows an alert that led to an interception. Ministries have published no such document. Courts have issued none.

data.retained_case_account: Rainforest Connection (RFCx), a US non-profit founded by Topher White, deploys solar-powered “Guardian” acoustic sensors. In its own words, they use “sound & artificial intelligence” to track chainsaws, vehicle engines, hunting dogs and gunshots. They send real-time alerts to a mobile app so that “an agent nearby” can respond. RFCx states it has protected over 726,000 (impact page) or 750,000 (guardian page) hectares across 8,662+ projects in 137 countries. The only non-vendor account read is a Thomson Reuters Foundation report published by The Straits Times on 11 February 2021. It is from Solok regency, West Sumatra, Indonesia, where 27 Guardian sensors had been installed more than a year earlier. Audio streams are analyzed by AI trained to pick out chainsaw sounds, and an alert goes to community patrols. Patroller Jasrialdi said logging “has totally stopped” in the area. The head of West Sumatra's forestry department, Yozarwardi Usama Putra, said he would like to expand the “early-warning system”. The same report attributes the decline in logging to a wider enforcement crackdown as well. It says RFCx planned to collect data for peer review to prove the system curbs logging. No park authority, ministry or court document records a specific alert leading to an interception, so no event is recorded.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: RFCx's own pages describe AI classification of streamed audio generating app alerts for responders. The 2021 Reuters report confirms the mechanism at the Solok site: AI picks out chainsaw sounds and patrols are alerted. It quotes a patroller that logging stopped, while also crediting a government enforcement crackdown. Apart from that single news item, only the maker's account is among the sources. No park authority, ministry or court record of an AI-triggered interception was found. RFCx itself said in 2021 that peer-review data to prove the effect was still being collected.

fields.account: Rainforest Connection (RFCx), a US non-profit founded by Topher White, deploys solar-powered “Guardian” acoustic sensors. In its own words, they use “sound & artificial intelligence” to track chainsaws. The sensors pick out vehicle engines. Hunting dogs are tracked. They track gunshots. They send real-time alerts to a mobile app so that “an agent nearby” can respond. On its impact page, RFCx states that it has protected over 726,000 hectares across 8,662+ projects in 137 countries. Its guardian page gives 750,000 hectares. Antara reported on a KKI Warsi press conference on 16 July 2020. There, Warsi said that the first 12 Guardian units went up in July 2019 in Sirukam and other nagari forests. In August 2019, a Guardian alert led the Sirukam patrol to a logger. The patrol caught the logger, who then escaped. Warsi counted 12 chainsaw alerts from sensors at 17 sites. It said that not all of them were illegal. A Thomson Reuters Foundation report published by The Straits Times on 11 February 2021 is the one independent account. It is from Solok regency, West Sumatra, Indonesia, where 27 Guardian sensors had been installed more than a year earlier. Audio streams are analyzed by AI trained to pick out chainsaw sounds. An alert goes to community patrols. Patroller Jasrialdi said that logging “has totally stopped” in the area. The head of West Sumatra's forestry department, Yozarwardi Usama Putra, said that he would like to expand the “early-warning system”. The reporters credit the decline in logging partly to a wider enforcement crackdown. They report that about 200 of Sirukam's 6,000 residents had worked in illegal logging. One former logger quit in 2018, before the sensors, because of the crackdown. The reporters add that RFCx planned to collect data for peer review to prove that the system curbs logging. No document from a park authority shows an alert that led to an interception. Ministries have published no such document. Courts have issued none.

display.answer: RFCx describes the system and its reach on its own pages. The Thomson Reuters Foundation report of 11 February 2021 is the one independent account of the Solok site. The Antara report of 16 July 2020 relays a press conference by KKI Warsi on its Guardian program in West Sumatra. Its statements come from Warsi's program manager and a Sirukam patroller.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: Rainforest Connection's Guardian sensors use AI to detect chainsaws. They alert patrols. In West Sumatra an alert led a patrol to a logger in August 2019. A patroller said that logging stopped.
fields.account: Rainforest Connection (RFCx), a US non-profit founded by Topher White, deploys solar-powered “Guardian” acoustic sensors. In its own words, they use “sound & artificial intelligence” to track chainsaws. The sensors pick out vehicle engines. Hunting dogs are tracked. They track gunshots. They send real-time alerts to a mobile app so that “an agent nearby” can respond. On its impact page, RFCx states that it has protected over 726,000 hectares across 8,662+ projects in 137 countries. Its guardian page gives 750,000 hectares. Antara reported on a KKI Warsi press conference on 16 July 2020. There, Warsi said that the first 12 Guardian units went up in July 2019 in Sirukam and other nagari forests. In August 2019, a Guardian alert led the Sirukam patrol to a logger. The patrol caught the logger, who then escaped. Warsi counted 12 chainsaw alerts from sensors at 17 sites. It said that not all of them were illegal. A Thomson Reuters Foundation report published by The Straits Times on 11 February 2021 is the one independent account. It is from Solok regency, West Sumatra, Indonesia, where 27 Guardian sensors had been installed more than a year earlier. Audio streams are analyzed by AI trained to pick out chainsaw sounds. An alert goes to community patrols. Patroller Jasrialdi said that logging “has totally stopped” in the area. The head of West Sumatra's forestry department, Yozarwardi Usama Putra, said that he would like to expand the “early-warning system”. The reporters credit the decline in logging partly to a wider enforcement crackdown. They report that about 200 of Sirukam's 6,000 residents had worked in illegal logging. One former logger quit in 2018, before the sensors, because of the crackdown. The reporters add that RFCx planned to collect data for peer review to prove that the system curbs logging. No document from a park authority shows an alert that led to an interception. Ministries have published no such document. Courts have issued none.

record.title: Odakyu Electric Railway starts an AI crossing image-analysis system at four Odawara Line crossings that signals approaching trains to stop when people are left inside
record.summary: Odakyu's AI crossing image-analysis system reads existing crossing cameras. It signals approaching trains to stop when someone is left inside. Trains made 17 emergency stops in two months.
record.account: Meitetsu EI Engineer, Toyota Systems and Toho Electric Industries developed a system that analyzes images of crossings with AI. It was tested from January 2023. The work covered the accuracy of detection at night. It covered accuracy in rain. ITmedia's 岡田有花 reported on 22 June 2026 that Odakyu Electric Railway would introduce an “AI踏切画像解析システム” from 24 June 2026. It covers four crossings on its Odawara Line. They are Minami-Shinjuku Nos. 2, 4 and 5 between Minami-Shinjuku and Sangubashi stations. The fourth is Mukogaoka-Yuen No. 9 between Mukogaoka-Yuen and Ikuta stations. The AI analyzes footage from the existing safety-confirmation cameras in real time. It identifies pedestrians. It identifies wheelchair users. It identifies bicycles. It identifies motorcycles. It tracks them. When it detects someone left inside after the barriers come down, it sends a signal through the signaling equipment. That signal applies the brakes of approaching trains. It lights the crossing's special signal lamps to alert crews. Both are released automatically once the crossing is clear. Images are used only for hazard detection. The system does not identify individuals. Analysis data are destroyed within a year. railf.jp carried the same announcement on 25 June 2026. Yomiuri reported on 19 September 2026 that trains made 17 emergency stops on detected anomalies in the system's first two months. Yomiuri does not say whether any stop averted an accident. It adds that the transport ministry now pays up to half the installation cost of such systems. Professor Ryo Takagi of Kogakuin University told the paper that such systems are very effective for accident prevention. He warned that AI does not make crossings fully safe.

fields.account: Meitetsu EI Engineer, Toyota Systems and Toho Electric Industries developed a system that analyzes images of crossings with AI. It was tested from January 2023. The work covered the accuracy of detection at night. It covered accuracy in rain. ITmedia's 岡田有花 reported on 22 June 2026 that Odakyu Electric Railway would introduce an “AI踏切画像解析システム” from 24 June 2026. It covers four crossings on its Odawara Line. They are Minami-Shinjuku Nos. 2, 4 and 5 between Minami-Shinjuku and Sangubashi stations. The fourth is Mukogaoka-Yuen No. 9 between Mukogaoka-Yuen and Ikuta stations. The AI analyzes footage from the existing safety-confirmation cameras in real time. It identifies pedestrians. It identifies wheelchair users. It identifies bicycles. It identifies motorcycles. It tracks them. When it detects someone left inside after the barriers come down, it sends a signal through the signaling equipment. That signal applies the brakes of approaching trains. It lights the crossing's special signal lamps to alert crews. Both are released automatically once the crossing is clear. Images are used only for hazard detection. The system does not identify individuals. Analysis data are destroyed within a year. railf.jp carried the same announcement on 25 June 2026. Yomiuri reported on 19 September 2026 that trains made 17 emergency stops on detected anomalies in the system's first two months. Yomiuri does not say whether any stop averted an accident. It adds that the transport ministry now pays up to half the installation cost of such systems. Professor Ryo Takagi of Kogakuin University told the paper that such systems are very effective for accident prevention. He warned that AI does not make crossings fully safe.

record.summary: Greece's deputy transport minister described an AI system from an unnamed supplier that transcribes railway radio calls to check them against protocols. He gave no measured safety result.
record.account: Deputy Minister of Transport Konstantinos Kyranakis said that the ministry presented an AI system on Saturday 16 May 2026. SKAI reported his interview about the system on 18 May 2026. In the interview he described a system that transcribes GSM-R communications between stationmasters and train drivers. GSM-R is the digital radio network that railways use. He said that the system would identify departures from railway communication protocols so that the control center could intervene. He called it a new safeguard that works in real time. He contrasted it with investigation after an accident. The interview names no developer. It gives no date for the start of operation. It gives no accuracy of transcription. It gives no counts of alerts. It gives no measured safety result.

details.value: Rafael and Israel's Ministry of Defense built Iron Beam, a high-energy laser, to intercept rockets, mortars and drones at short range. It is a low-cost complement to Iron Dome, David's Sling and Arrow.

details.label: Contribution of the AI
details.value: No reporter describes Iron Beam as an AI or machine-learning system. Ynet, JPost, Army Recognition, TimesNow, The Conversation, Moneycontrol and Wikipedia describe a high-power laser with a beam director and electro-optical targeting. So does the Times of Israel (28 December 2025, 16 March, 27 March and 30 June 2026). Rafael's CEO described machine learning as a future capability (Breaking Defense, 22 October 2025). The IDF has not confirmed the engagement itself, so neither an AI role nor a contribution can be assessed.

record.title: Israel's Iron Beam laser may have made its first combat interception, of a Hezbollah drone, in footage of 2 March 2026, though the military said on 12 March that Iron Beam had not been used
record.summary: Footage of 2 March 2026 may show Israel's Iron Beam laser downing a Hezbollah drone. On 12 March the military said that Iron Beam had not been used. No cited source lists the laser as AI.
record.account: None of the cited outlets describes Iron Beam as an AI system. The only other mention of AI is Rafael's chief executive describing artificial intelligence as a next step for the system (Breaking Defense, 22 October 2025). The only confirmed combat use of a laser came earlier. It is reported only in aggregate. A lower-powered, shorter-range variant shot down some 35 drones from Lebanon in 2024 (Times of Israel/AFP). The Ministry of Defense announced it in May 2025 (The Jerusalem Post). The ministry said that no Iron Beam components were involved (Wikipedia). The Times of Israel reports the Defense Ministry's handover of the first operational system on 28 December 2025, after tests against rockets, mortars and drones. The Iron Beam claim rests on social-media footage from Monday 2 March 2026. Ynet (Yair Kraus) reports that the footage “appeared to show the first operational use” of the system. It was delivered to the Israeli Air Force in late December 2025. Hezbollah fired rockets from Lebanon after the killing of Iran's Supreme Leader. It fired drones, with one drone intercepted near Shlomi. The Jerusalem Post (Seth Frantzman, 2 March 2026) says that the circulated video “did not show lasers intercepting rockets”. TimesNow (2 March 2026) says that whether this was Iron Beam's first combat use “awaits official confirmation”. Army Recognition (3 March 2026) says that officials “have not formally confirmed the specific engagements”. It says that the system appears in no authoritative combat log. The Conversation (4 March 2026) calls the reports unconfirmed. The Jerusalem Post reported on 12 March 2026 that the Israel Defense Forces said that Iron Beam had not been used. They said that it was not ready for regular use in the war. Times of Israel/AFP (16 March 2026) reports that the military “has so far refused to comment on its use during the ongoing war”. Times of Israel (Stav Levaton, 27 March 2026) reports that “military officials said it has not yet been declared operational within the IDF”. On 1 May 2026 the Israel Air Force said that the system saw less use because it needs 14 batteries to have much effect. Times of Israel (Emanuel Fabian, 30 June 2026) reports that the one deployed system “has seen limited use and has not yet been declared operational within the IDF”. A senior officer called its coverage partial. A senior defense official told Ynetnews on 9 August 2026 that the one system delivered in December 2025 was still not operational.

data.retained_case_account: It separately bundles a Hankyoreh item (dated 10 October 2023) on Hamas rockets penetrating Iron Dome. The Iron Beam claim rests on social-media footage from Monday 2 March 2026, not 28 February. Ynet (Yair Kraus) reports that the footage “appeared to show the first operational use” of the system. It was delivered to the Israeli Air Force in late December 2025. Hezbollah fired rockets and drones from Lebanon after the killing of Iran's Supreme Leader, with one drone intercepted near Shlomi. The Jerusalem Post (Seth Frantzman, 2 March 2026) says that the circulated video “did not show lasers intercepting rockets”. TimesNow (2 March 2026) says that whether this was Iron Beam's first combat use “awaits official confirmation”. Army Recognition (3 March 2026) says that officials “have not formally confirmed the specific engagements” and that no authoritative combat log names the system. The Conversation (4 March 2026) calls the reports unconfirmed. Moneycontrol (3 March 2026) sources its “first-ever use” to an “Israel War Room” social-media video. The Times of Israel reports the Defense Ministry's handover of the first operational system on 28 December 2025, after tests against rockets, mortars and drones. Times of Israel/AFP (16 March 2026) reports that the IDF “has so far refused to comment on its use during the ongoing war”. Times of Israel (Stav Levaton, 27 March 2026) reports that “military officials said it has not yet been declared operational within the IDF”. Times of Israel (Emanuel Fabian, 30 June 2026) reports that the one deployed system “has seen limited use and has not yet been declared operational within the IDF”. A senior officer called its coverage partial. The only confirmed laser combat use is aggregate and earlier. A lower-powered, shorter-range variant shot down some 35 drones from Lebanon in 2024 (Times of Israel/AFP). The Ministry of Defense announced it in May 2025 (JPost). The MoD said that no Iron Beam components were involved (Wikipedia). No cited source describes Iron Beam as an AI system. The only AI mention found is Rafael's CEO framing machine learning as a future capability (Breaking Defense, 22 October 2025). That piece is not among the sources.

fields.account: None of the cited outlets describes Iron Beam as an AI system. The only other mention of AI is Rafael's chief executive describing artificial intelligence as a next step for the system (Breaking Defense, 22 October 2025). The only confirmed combat use of a laser came earlier. It is reported only in aggregate. A lower-powered, shorter-range variant shot down some 35 drones from Lebanon in 2024 (Times of Israel/AFP). The Ministry of Defense announced it in May 2025 (The Jerusalem Post). The ministry said that no Iron Beam components were involved (Wikipedia). The Times of Israel reports the Defense Ministry's handover of the first operational system on 28 December 2025, after tests against rockets, mortars and drones. The Iron Beam claim rests on social-media footage from Monday 2 March 2026. Ynet (Yair Kraus) reports that the footage “appeared to show the first operational use” of the system. It was delivered to the Israeli Air Force in late December 2025. Hezbollah fired rockets from Lebanon after the killing of Iran's Supreme Leader. It fired drones, with one drone intercepted near Shlomi. The Jerusalem Post (Seth Frantzman, 2 March 2026) says that the circulated video “did not show lasers intercepting rockets”. TimesNow (2 March 2026) says that whether this was Iron Beam's first combat use “awaits official confirmation”. Army Recognition (3 March 2026) says that officials “have not formally confirmed the specific engagements”. It says that the system appears in no authoritative combat log. The Conversation (4 March 2026) calls the reports unconfirmed. The Jerusalem Post reported on 12 March 2026 that the Israel Defense Forces said that Iron Beam had not been used. They said that it was not ready for regular use in the war. Times of Israel/AFP (16 March 2026) reports that the military “has so far refused to comment on its use during the ongoing war”. Times of Israel (Stav Levaton, 27 March 2026) reports that “military officials said it has not yet been declared operational within the IDF”. On 1 May 2026 the Israel Air Force said that the system saw less use because it needs 14 batteries to have much effect. Times of Israel (Emanuel Fabian, 30 June 2026) reports that the one deployed system “has seen limited use and has not yet been declared operational within the IDF”. A senior officer called its coverage partial. A senior defense official told Ynetnews on 9 August 2026 that the one system delivered in December 2025 was still not operational.

fields.summary: Footage of 2 March 2026 may show Israel's Iron Beam laser downing a Hezbollah drone. On 12 March the military said that Iron Beam had not been used. No cited source lists the laser as AI.
fields.account: None of the cited outlets describes Iron Beam as an AI system. The only other mention of AI is Rafael's chief executive describing artificial intelligence as a next step for the system (Breaking Defense, 22 October 2025). The only confirmed combat use of a laser came earlier. It is reported only in aggregate. A lower-powered, shorter-range variant shot down some 35 drones from Lebanon in 2024 (Times of Israel/AFP). The Ministry of Defense announced it in May 2025 (The Jerusalem Post). The ministry said that no Iron Beam components were involved (Wikipedia). The Times of Israel reports the Defense Ministry's handover of the first operational system on 28 December 2025, after tests against rockets, mortars and drones. The Iron Beam claim rests on social-media footage from Monday 2 March 2026. Ynet (Yair Kraus) reports that the footage “appeared to show the first operational use” of the system. It was delivered to the Israeli Air Force in late December 2025. Hezbollah fired rockets from Lebanon after the killing of Iran's Supreme Leader. It fired drones, with one drone intercepted near Shlomi. The Jerusalem Post (Seth Frantzman, 2 March 2026) says that the circulated video “did not show lasers intercepting rockets”. TimesNow (2 March 2026) says that whether this was Iron Beam's first combat use “awaits official confirmation”. Army Recognition (3 March 2026) says that officials “have not formally confirmed the specific engagements”. It says that the system appears in no authoritative combat log. The Conversation (4 March 2026) calls the reports unconfirmed. The Jerusalem Post reported on 12 March 2026 that the Israel Defense Forces said that Iron Beam had not been used. They said that it was not ready for regular use in the war. Times of Israel/AFP (16 March 2026) reports that the military “has so far refused to comment on its use during the ongoing war”. Times of Israel (Stav Levaton, 27 March 2026) reports that “military officials said it has not yet been declared operational within the IDF”. On 1 May 2026 the Israel Air Force said that the system saw less use because it needs 14 batteries to have much effect. Times of Israel (Emanuel Fabian, 30 June 2026) reports that the one deployed system “has seen limited use and has not yet been declared operational within the IDF”. A senior officer called its coverage partial. A senior defense official told Ynetnews on 9 August 2026 that the one system delivered in December 2025 was still not operational.

record.title: ProRail uses Genetec analytics across 7,000 cameras to flag trespassers to train dispatchers as it replaces 288 lineside cameras with AI “smart cameras” in 2026
record.summary: ProRail replaces 288 lineside cameras with smart cameras in 2026. It runs Genetec video analytics on its 7,000 cameras to flag trespassers to dispatchers. No results have been published.
record.account: ProRail, the Dutch rail infrastructure manager, issued a press release on 31 January 2026. In the release, ProRail said that AI software in its smart cameras flags unwanted situations to staff in its Smart Monitoring Room. Those staff alert the rail control room when needed. ProRail cites research that it says shows that suicides on the track fall 45 percent at locations where cameras are combined with physical measures. It does not name the study. It does not separate the effect of the AI cameras. SpoorPro.nl reported on 2 February 2026 that ProRail is replacing 288 lineside cameras in 2026 with new “smart” cameras. ProRail is testing autonomous drones that analyze images. SpoorPro quotes ProRail as saying that these forms of camera surveillance help it see incidents sooner. According to ProRail, they help it prevent incidents sooner. The results, it says, are a safer track, fewer disruptions and fewer delays. According to a photo caption in the article, the AI cameras' images are monitored 24/7. The rest of the text is behind a paywall. SpoorPro reported on 3 March 2026 that ProRail is bringing the 7,000 security cameras that it manages into one Genetec platform. It is monitored from ProRail's Smart Monitoring Room. Genetec Mission Control has three functions: filtering alerts, analyzing them and forwarding relevant images to an operator with suggested actions. Video analysis is used among other things to flag spoorlopers (people on the track). In that case the train dispatcher can warn drivers. In the article, SpoorPro quotes ProRail project lead Kristian Ruiter and Genetec's Bob van Keulen. On 10 September 2026 Genetec, the platform vendor, published a customer story titled “From incident to response in under a minute at ProRail”. ProRail and Genetec have reported no detection count, no stopped train and no fall in trespass due to the analytics.

fields.account: ProRail, the Dutch rail infrastructure manager, issued a press release on 31 January 2026. In the release, ProRail said that AI software in its smart cameras flags unwanted situations to staff in its Smart Monitoring Room. Those staff alert the rail control room when needed. ProRail cites research that it says shows that suicides on the track fall 45 percent at locations where cameras are combined with physical measures. It does not name the study. It does not separate the effect of the AI cameras. SpoorPro.nl reported on 2 February 2026 that ProRail is replacing 288 lineside cameras in 2026 with new “smart” cameras. ProRail is testing autonomous drones that analyze images. SpoorPro quotes ProRail as saying that these forms of camera surveillance help it see incidents sooner. According to ProRail, they help it prevent incidents sooner. The results, it says, are a safer track, fewer disruptions and fewer delays. According to a photo caption in the article, the AI cameras' images are monitored 24/7. The rest of the text is behind a paywall. SpoorPro reported on 3 March 2026 that ProRail is bringing the 7,000 security cameras that it manages into one Genetec platform. It is monitored from ProRail's Smart Monitoring Room. Genetec Mission Control has three functions: filtering alerts, analyzing them and forwarding relevant images to an operator with suggested actions. Video analysis is used among other things to flag spoorlopers (people on the track). In that case the train dispatcher can warn drivers. In the article, SpoorPro quotes ProRail project lead Kristian Ruiter and Genetec's Bob van Keulen. On 10 September 2026 Genetec, the platform vendor, published a customer story titled “From incident to response in under a minute at ProRail”. ProRail and Genetec have reported no detection count, no stopped train and no fall in trespass due to the analytics.

record.title: 26 Indian banks use MuleHunter.AI to flag accounts that move money for fraudsters
record.summary: MuleHunter.AI, from the Reserve Bank Innovation Hub, flags likely mule accounts at 26 Indian banks. The Reserve Bank of India has withheld the number of accounts found.
record.account: The Reserve Bank Innovation Hub (RBIH) developed MuleHunter.AI. It analyzes patterns in transactions within each participating bank’s infrastructure to identify likely mule accounts. It analyzes patterns in accounts. RBIH’s technical documentation says that personally identifiable information is not exchanged with the hub. On 20 November 2025 the Economic Times reported that the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), Sanjay Malhotra, said that the tool showed a good success rate. In its summary, the paper attributed to him a figure of about 20,000 mule accounts detected each month. On 30 December 2025 Prabhanu Kumar Das reported in MediaNama on a Right to Information response. It showed that 23 banks had implemented MuleHunter.AI as of 10 December 2025. That was up from at least 15 banks in August 2025 and nearly 20 in November 2025. The report named Canara Bank, Punjab National Bank, Bank of India, Bank of Baroda, AU Small Finance Bank and Federal Bank. The RBI said that it cannot provide data on the number of mule accounts identified through MuleHunter.AI. It cannot provide the number acted upon. It said that it holds such information in a fiduciary capacity with banks. It said that disclosure could harm competitive interests. On 30 April 2026 Financial Services Secretary M Nagaraju asked banks to adopt the tool at the earliest. On 12 May 2026 the Ministry of Home Affairs announced a memorandum between its Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) and RBIH. They would combine identifiers of suspects with intelligence on mule accounts to improve the model. By August 2026 the RBI had told an inter-departmental committee in Supreme Court proceedings on digital-arrest frauds that 26 banks were using the tool. MediaNama reported that other banks used their own systems.

fields.account: The Reserve Bank Innovation Hub (RBIH) developed MuleHunter.AI. It analyzes patterns in transactions within each participating bank’s infrastructure to identify likely mule accounts. It analyzes patterns in accounts. RBIH’s technical documentation says that personally identifiable information is not exchanged with the hub. On 20 November 2025 the Economic Times reported that the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), Sanjay Malhotra, said that the tool showed a good success rate. In its summary, the paper attributed to him a figure of about 20,000 mule accounts detected each month. On 30 December 2025 Prabhanu Kumar Das reported in MediaNama on a Right to Information response. It showed that 23 banks had implemented MuleHunter.AI as of 10 December 2025. That was up from at least 15 banks in August 2025 and nearly 20 in November 2025. The report named Canara Bank, Punjab National Bank, Bank of India, Bank of Baroda, AU Small Finance Bank and Federal Bank. The RBI said that it cannot provide data on the number of mule accounts identified through MuleHunter.AI. It cannot provide the number acted upon. It said that it holds such information in a fiduciary capacity with banks. It said that disclosure could harm competitive interests. On 30 April 2026 Financial Services Secretary M Nagaraju asked banks to adopt the tool at the earliest. On 12 May 2026 the Ministry of Home Affairs announced a memorandum between its Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) and RBIH. They would combine identifiers of suspects with intelligence on mule accounts to improve the model. By August 2026 the RBI had told an inter-departmental committee in Supreme Court proceedings on digital-arrest frauds that 26 banks were using the tool. MediaNama reported that other banks used their own systems.

record.title: DARPA's AIxCC final: Autonomous systems find 54 of 63 synthetic vulnerabilities. They patch 43. They also find 18 real bugs in open-source code
record.summary: At DEF CON 33 on 8 August 2025, DARPA reported that seven teams' cyber reasoning systems found 54 synthetic vulnerabilities, patched 43, and found 18 real bugs for disclosure.
record.account: In its release of results, DARPA describes the Final Competition. The teams' cyber reasoning systems had to find and patch synthetic vulnerabilities across 54 million lines of real-world open-source code. They found 54 unique synthetic vulnerabilities in 63 challenges. They patched 43. They found 18 real, non-synthetic vulnerabilities (six in C codebases, 12 in Java). DARPA said that these were being responsibly disclosed. There were 11 patches for real bugs. The average cost was about $152 per task. Team Atlanta (Georgia Tech, Samsung Research, KAIST, POSTECH) won $4 million. Trail of Bits won $3 million. Theori won $1.5 million. Four of seven systems were released open source. The Record reported the same figures from Las Vegas with program manager Andrew Carney's remarks. On 22 October 2025 curl maintainer Daniel Stenberg, whose project was among the targets, examined the injected curl flaws. He judged that they were straightforward. He judged that they were not deeply hidden. In March 2026 Team Atlanta reported that the released systems were hard to run outside their teams. It reported that a ported Atlantis found 10 new bugs, three of high severity, in eight OSS-Fuzz projects. In September 2026 researchers at the University of Maryland tested the top three AIxCC systems on 213 transplanted vulnerabilities. Across 11 agents, they found that checks based only on the original crash input overstate patching success by 1.83 times on average. Atlantis passed 92.0% of the original crash checks. It solved 48.4% of tasks under full validation. The researchers found that the AIxCC systems solved fewer tasks than general-purpose coding agents on the same model.

fields.summary: At DEF CON 33 on 8 August 2025, DARPA reported that seven teams' cyber reasoning systems found 54 synthetic vulnerabilities, patched 43, and found 18 real bugs for disclosure.
fields.account: In its release of results, DARPA describes the Final Competition. The teams' cyber reasoning systems had to find and patch synthetic vulnerabilities across 54 million lines of real-world open-source code. They found 54 unique synthetic vulnerabilities in 63 challenges. They patched 43. They found 18 real, non-synthetic vulnerabilities (six in C codebases, 12 in Java). DARPA said that these were being responsibly disclosed. There were 11 patches for real bugs. The average cost was about $152 per task. Team Atlanta (Georgia Tech, Samsung Research, KAIST, POSTECH) won $4 million. Trail of Bits won $3 million. Theori won $1.5 million. Four of seven systems were released open source. The Record reported the same figures from Las Vegas with program manager Andrew Carney's remarks. On 22 October 2025 curl maintainer Daniel Stenberg, whose project was among the targets, examined the injected curl flaws. He judged that they were straightforward. He judged that they were not deeply hidden. In March 2026 Team Atlanta reported that the released systems were hard to run outside their teams. It reported that a ported Atlantis found 10 new bugs, three of high severity, in eight OSS-Fuzz projects. In September 2026 researchers at the University of Maryland tested the top three AIxCC systems on 213 transplanted vulnerabilities. Across 11 agents, they found that checks based only on the original crash input overstate patching success by 1.83 times on average. Atlantis passed 92.0% of the original crash checks. It solved 48.4% of tasks under full validation. The researchers found that the AIxCC systems solved fewer tasks than general-purpose coding agents on the same model.

value.text: The finalist systems autonomously searched for vulnerabilities and generated patches during the competition. Maintainers still controlled adoption outside it.

record.title: India's Department of Telecommunications disconnects more than 82 lakh mobile connections that its facial-recognition tool ASTR flagged
record.summary: The Department of Telecommunications' ASTR facial-recognition tool flags connections that one person took under different names. More than 82 lakh were disconnected after failed re-verification.
record.account: The Department of Telecommunications, Government of India, states that it designed and implemented ASTR. ASTR, the “AI and facial recognition powered Solution for Telecom SIM Subscriber Verification”, is to identify fake mobile connections. It covers forged connections. It covers non-bonafide connections. It is to weed them out. MediaNama reports that ASTR has run since 2021. In a release from Chennai of 8 May 2023, the Press Information Bureau reported that ASTR identified more than 50,000 non-bonafide connections in Tamil Nadu. It said that operators disconnected all of them. It said that they handed point-of-sale details to the Tamil Nadu Police Cyber Crime Wing. MediaNama reported on 9 May 2023 that the department refused its Right to Information request for the ASTR contract as confidential. The Hindu (Press Trust of India, 28 May 2023) quoted a senior official of the department in Patna. The official said that ASTR analysis found at least 21,800 connections exceeding the nine-per-subscriber limit in Bihar and Jharkhand. Around 17,000 of them were disconnected. Operators blacklisted 2,900 points of sale. Minister of State Dr Pemmasani Chandra Sekhar gave a Rajya Sabha written reply, which the Press Information Bureau posted on 7 August 2025. He said that the department disconnected more than 82 lakh connections through ASTR after they failed re-verification. The cumulative figure is dated to the posting of that reply. MediaNama reported on 24 July 2026 that a Rajya Sabha reply counted more than 88 lakh disconnections. The department's circular of 17 August 2026 orders operators to match subscriber photographs before issuing a SIM. MediaNama notes that the circular sets no limit on the retention of images. It notes that the circular offers no redress for a faulty facial match. On 9 October 2026 The Hans India reported the minister's statement that India had disconnected over 82 lakh fraudulent mobile connections through ASTR. None of the sources contains an independent evaluation of ASTR's accuracy.
