data.retained_case_account: The Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Government of India, states that it designed and implemented ASTR. ASTR, the “AI and facial recognition powered Solution for Telecom SIM Subscriber Verification”, is to identify and weed out fake, forged and non-bonafide mobile connections. A PIB Chennai release of 8 May 2023 reported that ASTR identified more than 50,000 non-bonafide connections in Tamil Nadu. All were disconnected by operators, with point-of-sale details handed to the Tamil Nadu Police Cyber Crime Wing. The Hindu (PTI, 28 May 2023) quoted a senior DoT official in Patna. The official said that ASTR analysis found at least 21,800 connections exceeding the nine-per-subscriber limit in Bihar and Jharkhand. Around 17,000 of them were disconnected, and operators blacklisted 2,900 points of sale. Minister of State Dr Pemmasani Chandra Sekhar gave a Rajya Sabha written reply, posted by PIB on 7 August 2025. He said that DoT disconnected more than 82 lakh connections through ASTR after they failed re-verification. The cumulative figure carries the reply's posting date. No independent accuracy evaluation was found.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: DoT describes ASTR as an indigenous AI and big-data analytic tool. It uses facial recognition to find connections taken by the same person under different names. Disconnection follows a failed re-verification step, so the tool flags connections rather than deciding. Developer and deployer are the same public body (DoT), which wrote the PIB releases.

ASTR, the “AI and facial recognition powered Solution for Telecom SIM Subscriber Verification”, is to identify fake mobile connections. It covers forged connections. It covers non-bonafide connections. It is to weed them out. MediaNama reports that ASTR has run since 2021. In a release from Chennai of 8 May 2023, the Press Information Bureau reported that ASTR identified more than 50,000 non-bonafide connections in Tamil Nadu. It said that operators disconnected all of them. It said that they handed point-of-sale details to the Tamil Nadu Police Cyber Crime Wing. MediaNama reported on 9 May 2023 that the department refused its Right to Information request for the ASTR contract as confidential. record.title: Northumberland County Council- FloodAI, using AI to detect flash floods
record.summary: Northumberland County Council's FloodAI machine-learning service is meant to forecast flash floods in six catchments. It was still a prototype in October 2025.
record.account: In October 2024 the Environment Agency reported that the Northumberland FloodAI project team was applying AI to a network of 43 smart sensors. The network includes river gauges. The team aimed to develop automated flood warnings by 2025. In June 2025 the council reported that the FloodAI research project was developing forecasts for six flash-flood-prone catchments. The council said that the system was at alpha stage. It said that the system was approaching limited piloting. In its national report of 13 August 2025, the Environment Agency still described the model as in development. It said that the model was being tested. On 24 October 2025 the Northumberland Gazette reported that a prototype warning system was being developed. No issued warning has been documented. No avoided flood impact has been documented.

fields.account: In October 2024 the Environment Agency reported that the Northumberland FloodAI project team was applying AI to a network of 43 smart sensors. The network includes river gauges. The team aimed to develop automated flood warnings by 2025. In June 2025 the council reported that the FloodAI research project was developing forecasts for six flash-flood-prone catchments. The council said that the system was at alpha stage. It said that the system was approaching limited piloting. In its national report of 13 August 2025, the Environment Agency still described the model as in development. It said that the model was being tested. On 24 October 2025 the Northumberland Gazette reported that a prototype warning system was being developed. No issued warning has been documented. No avoided flood impact has been documented.

record.title: Rafael's X-Guard towed decoy, labeled “AI-powered”, may have diverted Pakistani missiles from Indian Rafales in Operation Sindoor (7–10 May 2025). India's defense chief reports Indian aircraft losses. So does France's air force chief
record.summary: Commentators credit Rafael's X-Guard towed decoy, labeled “AI-powered”, with diverting Pakistani missiles from Indian Rafales. No official has confirmed its use. India admitted jet losses.
record.account: In its product brochure of March 2024, Rafael describes a reusable fiber-optic towed decoy. Rafael identifies no AI model in it. The company does not confirm deployment in Operation Sindoor. Operation Sindoor began on 7 May 2025. It lasted four days (India TV). At the Shangri-La Dialogue on 31 May 2025, India's Chief of Defence Staff, General Anil Chauhan, admitted that an unspecified number of Indian jets were shot down. He rejected Pakistan's claim of six (Al Jazeera, 1 June 2025, as well as Wikipedia citing Bloomberg). He placed India's air losses on the first day of fighting. The claim for the decoy first appears in an idrw.org post of 6 July 2025, credited to “AFI”, an outsourced content partner. In the post, idrw quotes Ryan Bodenheimer, a former US Air Force F-15E and F-16 pilot. Bodenheimer calls the Indian Air Force's tactics “the best spoofing and deception we've ever seen”. He credits “the Rafale's X-Guard AI-enhanced jamming decoy system”. idrw itself writes that the system “likely played a pivotal role”. It adds, citing Jane's Defence Weekly, that Pakistani claims of downed Rafales were “likely X-Guard decoys”. On the same day the Associated Press quoted General Jérôme Bellanger, chief of the French air force. Bellanger reported seeing evidence of three Indian aircraft losses, one of them a Rafale. The Economic Times writes on 8 July 2025 that the Indian Air Force “reportedly used artificial intelligence-powered technology”. On 9 July LatestLY says that it “allegedly used” it. India TV, on 9 July, attributes a finding that Pakistani kills were hits on towed decoys to “a recent Jane's Defence Weekly investigation”. No other outlet corroborates it. The Jane's Defence Weekly investigation itself is not among the sources. Oneindia (9 July) says that false claims of downed Rafales “may have been decoys”. TFIPOST (9 July) says that the Indian Air Force “reportedly deployed” the system. It names the maker correctly as Rafael Advanced Defense Systems. The Economic Times, India TV, LatestLY, Oneindia and idrw write “Rafale Advanced Defense Systems”. The Indian Air Force, the Ministry of Defence, Dassault and Rafael have not confirmed that X-Guard was carried. They have not confirmed that it was deployed. The claimed outcome of no losses is contradicted by India's Chief of Defence Staff.

data.answer:
Every account traces to ex-USAF pilot Ryan Bodenheimer via idrw.org (6 July 2025). No IAF, MoD, Dassault or Rafael confirmation; CDS Gen Anil Chauhan admitted on 31 May 2025 that India lost jets.

The deployment and AI label derive from a commentary chain, with no retained operator or manufacturer confirmation. The cited Jane's investigation is unavailable in the evidence list. Claims of no aircraft losses conflict with the retained report of India's acknowledgment of losses.

No source independent of the commentary chain describes X-Guard as an AI system. idrw writes “AI-enhanced jamming decoy” and “AI-enhanced algorithms dynamically adjust signals” without attribution. ET, India TV, LatestLY, Oneindia and TFIPOST repeat the label. The Week gives no source for “AI-enabled”. Rafael's own page was unreadable. Deployment itself is unconfirmed by the IAF, MoD, Dassault or Rafael. The no-loss outcome is contradicted by the CDS. Neither the system's AI character nor any contribution to the engagements can therefore be assessed.

data.retained_case_account: It says the Indian Air Force (IAF) used “the AI-powered X-Guard decoy system on Rafale jets”. It says this “prevented enemy missiles from hitting real aircraft”. The claim originates in an idrw.org post of 6 July 2025, sourced to “AFI”, an outsourced content partner. The post quotes Ryan Bodenheimer, a former US Air Force F-15E and F-16 pilot. He calls the IAF's tactics “the best spoofing and deception we've ever seen” and credits “the Rafale's X-Guard AI-enhanced jamming decoy system”. idrw itself writes that the system “likely played a pivotal role”. It writes that Pakistani claims of downed Rafales were “likely X-Guard decoys” according to Jane's Defence Weekly. The Economic Times (ET) writes on 8 July 2025 that the IAF “reportedly used artificial intelligence-powered technology”. LatestLY (9 Jul) says it “allegedly used” it. India TV (9 Jul) attributes a finding that Pakistani kills were hits on towed decoys to “a recent Jane's Defence Weekly investigation”. No other outlet on record corroborates it, and the Jane's Defence Weekly investigation itself is not among the sources. Oneindia (9 Jul) says false claims of downed Rafales “may have been decoys”. TFIPOST (9 Jul) says the IAF “reportedly deployed” the system and names the maker correctly as Rafael Advanced Defense Systems. ET, India TV, LatestLY, Oneindia and idrw write “Rafale Advanced Defense Systems”. The Week and Business Today are quoted from an earlier reading; their pages were not available afterward. The Week's headline says the IAF “may have used” X-Guard. It describes Bodenheimer as “a military tech digital creator”. Business Today writes “reportedly misdirected”. No IAF, Ministry of Defence (MoD), Dassault or Rafael statement confirms that X-Guard was carried or deployed. Rafael’s March 2024 product brochure describes a reusable fiber-optic towed decoy, but does not identify an AI model or confirm deployment in this operation. The claimed outcome (no losses) is contradicted by India's Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), General Anil Chauhan. At the Shangri-La Dialogue on 31 May 2025 he admitted that an unspecified number of Indian jets were shot down. He rejected Pakistan's claim of six (Al Jazeera, 1 June 2025; Wikipedia citing Bloomberg). Operation Sindoor began on 7 May 2025 and lasted four days (India TV).

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: Rafael’s original brochure establishes X-Guard’s electronic-decoy role and aircraft integration, but does not identify an AI model or confirm deployment in Operation Sindoor. The operation-specific AI and protection claims remain commentary, and the sweeping no-loss claim conflicts with India’s defense chief’s admission of losses.

fields.account: In its product brochure of March 2024, Rafael describes a reusable fiber-optic towed decoy. Rafael identifies no AI model in it. The company does not confirm deployment in Operation Sindoor. Operation Sindoor began on 7 May 2025. It lasted four days (India TV). At the Shangri-La Dialogue on 31 May 2025, India's Chief of Defence Staff, General Anil Chauhan, admitted that an unspecified number of Indian jets were shot down. He rejected Pakistan's claim of six (Al Jazeera, 1 June 2025, as well as Wikipedia citing Bloomberg). He placed India's air losses on the first day of fighting. The claim for the decoy first appears in an idrw.org post of 6 July 2025, credited to “AFI”, an outsourced content partner. In the post, idrw quotes Ryan Bodenheimer, a former US Air Force F-15E and F-16 pilot. Bodenheimer calls the Indian Air Force's tactics “the best spoofing and deception we've ever seen”. He credits “the Rafale's X-Guard AI-enhanced jamming decoy system”. idrw itself writes that the system “likely played a pivotal role”. It adds, citing Jane's Defence Weekly, that Pakistani claims of downed Rafales were “likely X-Guard decoys”. On the same day the Associated Press quoted General Jérôme Bellanger, chief of the French air force. Bellanger reported seeing evidence of three Indian aircraft losses, one of them a Rafale. The Economic Times writes on 8 July 2025 that the Indian Air Force “reportedly used artificial intelligence-powered technology”. On 9 July LatestLY says that it “allegedly used” it. India TV, on 9 July, attributes a finding that Pakistani kills were hits on towed decoys to “a recent Jane's Defence Weekly investigation”. No other outlet corroborates it. The Jane's Defence Weekly investigation itself is not among the sources. Oneindia (9 July) says that false claims of downed Rafales “may have been decoys”. TFIPOST (9 July) says that the Indian Air Force “reportedly deployed” the system. It names the maker correctly as Rafael Advanced Defense Systems. The Economic Times, India TV, LatestLY, Oneindia and idrw write “Rafale Advanced Defense Systems”. The Indian Air Force, the Ministry of Defence, Dassault and Rafael have not confirmed that X-Guard was carried. They have not confirmed that it was deployed. The claimed outcome of no losses is contradicted by India's Chief of Defence Staff.

fields.account: In its product brochure of March 2024, Rafael describes a reusable fiber-optic towed decoy. Rafael identifies no AI model in it. The company does not confirm deployment in Operation Sindoor. Operation Sindoor began on 7 May 2025. It lasted four days (India TV). At the Shangri-La Dialogue on 31 May 2025, India's Chief of Defence Staff, General Anil Chauhan, admitted that an unspecified number of Indian jets were shot down. He rejected Pakistan's claim of six (Al Jazeera, 1 June 2025, as well as Wikipedia citing Bloomberg). He placed India's air losses on the first day of fighting. The claim for the decoy first appears in an idrw.org post of 6 July 2025, credited to “AFI”, an outsourced content partner. In the post, idrw quotes Ryan Bodenheimer, a former US Air Force F-15E and F-16 pilot. Bodenheimer calls the Indian Air Force's tactics “the best spoofing and deception we've ever seen”. He credits “the Rafale's X-Guard AI-enhanced jamming decoy system”. idrw itself writes that the system “likely played a pivotal role”. It adds, citing Jane's Defence Weekly, that Pakistani claims of downed Rafales were “likely X-Guard decoys”. On the same day the Associated Press quoted General Jérôme Bellanger, chief of the French air force. Bellanger reported seeing evidence of three Indian aircraft losses, one of them a Rafale. The Economic Times writes on 8 July 2025 that the Indian Air Force “reportedly used artificial intelligence-powered technology”. On 9 July LatestLY says that it “allegedly used” it. India TV, on 9 July, attributes a finding that Pakistani kills were hits on towed decoys to “a recent Jane's Defence Weekly investigation”. No other outlet corroborates it. The Jane's Defence Weekly investigation itself is not among the sources. Oneindia (9 July) says that false claims of downed Rafales “may have been decoys”. TFIPOST (9 July) says that the Indian Air Force “reportedly deployed” the system. It names the maker correctly as Rafael Advanced Defense Systems. The Economic Times, India TV, LatestLY, Oneindia and idrw write “Rafale Advanced Defense Systems”. The Indian Air Force, the Ministry of Defence, Dassault and Rafael have not confirmed that X-Guard was carried. They have not confirmed that it was deployed. The claimed outcome of no losses is contradicted by India's Chief of Defence Staff.

record.title: RFI’s AlpEW seismic-warning system reportedly stops Rome–Naples trains during a magnitude 4.4 earthquake
record.summary: Rete Ferroviaria Italiana's AlpEW seismic early-warning system reportedly stopped Rome–Naples trains during a magnitude 4.4 earthquake. Its developers describe no learned AI model.
record.account: According to Euronews, Rete Ferroviaria Italiana's seismic early-warning system on the Rome-Naples high-speed line had been operational since 3 May 2025. Euronews reported that in the following weeks it was tested by a magnitude 4.4 earthquake, during which trains on the Rome-Naples line were stopped preventively. A magnitude 4.4 earthquake struck Campi Flegrei on 13 May 2025. Quotidiano Nazionale reported that high-speed trains in the Naples node were suspended that day. No source shows that the warning system made that stop. ANSA reported on 14 July 2025 that Ferrovie dello Stato's infrastructure company Rete Ferroviaria Italiana had activated Italy's first seismic early-warning system on the line. It was developed with the Physics Department of the University of Naples Federico II. Technical support came from the Railway Technical Research Institute of the Japanese railways. A network of latest-generation sensors detects the earliest seismic waves. Within seconds it automatically activates safety protocols to slow or stop trains. ANSA does not mention artificial intelligence. Euronews added on 15 July 2025 that the system comprises about 20 seismic stations along 200 km, on the surface and in deep boreholes. They are linked by a synchronous digital hierarchy (SDH) fiber network. According to Euronews, an advanced software intelligence instantly analyzes the data and assesses the danger of the quake. Euronews attributes the magnitude 4.4 episode to RailTech and places it within two weeks of the 3 May 2025 start. The two outlets give no exact date for that earthquake. In January 2026 the developers published a peer-reviewed study of the system in Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences. They describe signal processing with empirical prediction of ground motion. They describe probabilistic thresholds for alerts. They describe no learned AI model in the deployed system. Their operational observations cover March 2020 to January 2022. They do not verify the magnitude 4.4 stop. The developers wrote that Rete Ferroviaria Italiana had decided to extend the system to other high-speed lines. Wired Italia reported on 24 May 2026 that the system was still in use. It reported that its developers were studying machine learning to refine it. No report shows a second line in service by October 2026.

fields.summary: Rete Ferroviaria Italiana's AlpEW seismic early-warning system reportedly stopped Rome–Naples trains during a magnitude 4.4 earthquake. Its developers describe no learned AI model.
fields.account: According to Euronews, Rete Ferroviaria Italiana's seismic early-warning system on the Rome-Naples high-speed line had been operational since 3 May 2025. Euronews reported that in the following weeks it was tested by a magnitude 4.4 earthquake, during which trains on the Rome-Naples line were stopped preventively. A magnitude 4.4 earthquake struck Campi Flegrei on 13 May 2025. Quotidiano Nazionale reported that high-speed trains in the Naples node were suspended that day. No source shows that the warning system made that stop. ANSA reported on 14 July 2025 that Ferrovie dello Stato's infrastructure company Rete Ferroviaria Italiana had activated Italy's first seismic early-warning system on the line. It was developed with the Physics Department of the University of Naples Federico II. Technical support came from the Railway Technical Research Institute of the Japanese railways. A network of latest-generation sensors detects the earliest seismic waves. Within seconds it automatically activates safety protocols to slow or stop trains. ANSA does not mention artificial intelligence. Euronews added on 15 July 2025 that the system comprises about 20 seismic stations along 200 km, on the surface and in deep boreholes. They are linked by a synchronous digital hierarchy (SDH) fiber network. According to Euronews, an advanced software intelligence instantly analyzes the data and assesses the danger of the quake. Euronews attributes the magnitude 4.4 episode to RailTech and places it within two weeks of the 3 May 2025 start. The two outlets give no exact date for that earthquake. In January 2026 the developers published a peer-reviewed study of the system in Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences. They describe signal processing with empirical prediction of ground motion. They describe probabilistic thresholds for alerts. They describe no learned AI model in the deployed system. Their operational observations cover March 2020 to January 2022. They do not verify the magnitude 4.4 stop. The developers wrote that Rete Ferroviaria Italiana had decided to extend the system to other high-speed lines. Wired Italia reported on 24 May 2026 that the system was still in use. It reported that its developers were studying machine learning to refine it. No report shows a second line in service by October 2026.

record.title: CT algorithms from Rapiscan and Taronga/Macquarie detect marine wildlife, such as shark fins, at 86–96% in laboratory testing
record.summary: In laboratory tests on CT scans, some synthetic, Rapiscan's AI detected marine wildlife, such as shark fins, at rates of 86–96%, with 13% false alarms in all. No customs use is reported.
record.account: Pirotta and colleagues tested AI detection of marine wildlife in three-dimensional X-ray scans. In their paper of 8 June 2026, they state that the scans were collected from September 2024 to February 2025. They report 298 scans from 68 specimens. These include preserved specimens. Fresh shark material is among them. The researchers expanded the scans by inserting specimen images into baggage images. A 512-bag test set mixed original scans with these synthetic composites. All were drawn from the same specimen population. In Table 3, the authors report detection rates of 95% for shark fins, 96% for seahorses, and 86% for sea cucumbers. The false-alarm rate across all classes was 13%. The rates for single classes were 2%, 9% and 1%. Rapiscan supplied equipment. It funded staff to take part in the analysis. Its funding covered their part in the writing. The authors report laboratory detection only. They report no operational seizure. Nor do they report an evaluation by customs. Mongabay reported on 16 June 2026 that outside researchers, along with a spokesperson for the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC), welcomed the study as a complementary tool. Toby Breckon of Durham University told Mongabay that major airports already have 3D scanners for hold luggage. Michelle Anagnostou of Oxford noted that the study left out sea freight. Pirotta told Mongabay that the next step is to share the method so that other species can be detected in other regions.

fields.account: Pirotta and colleagues tested AI detection of marine wildlife in three-dimensional X-ray scans. In their paper of 8 June 2026, they state that the scans were collected from September 2024 to February 2025. They report 298 scans from 68 specimens. These include preserved specimens. Fresh shark material is among them. The researchers expanded the scans by inserting specimen images into baggage images. A 512-bag test set mixed original scans with these synthetic composites. All were drawn from the same specimen population. In Table 3, the authors report detection rates of 95% for shark fins, 96% for seahorses, and 86% for sea cucumbers. The false-alarm rate across all classes was 13%. The rates for single classes were 2%, 9% and 1%. Rapiscan supplied equipment. It funded staff to take part in the analysis. Its funding covered their part in the writing. The authors report laboratory detection only. They report no operational seizure. Nor do they report an evaluation by customs. Mongabay reported on 16 June 2026 that outside researchers, along with a spokesperson for the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC), welcomed the study as a complementary tool. Toby Breckon of Durham University told Mongabay that major airports already have 3D scanners for hold luggage. Michelle Anagnostou of Oxford noted that the study left out sea freight. Pirotta told Mongabay that the next step is to share the method so that other species can be detected in other regions.

record.title: Kenya Wildlife Service installs AI-enabled FLIR thermal cameras at Solio, Lake Nakuru and Ol Pejeta to send intrusion alerts to rhino rangers
record.summary: The Kenya Wildlife Service installed FLIR thermal cameras whose built-in AI alerts rangers to intruders at three black rhino sites. The service has linked no outcome, such as an arrest, to them.
record.account: Citizen Digital reported on 21 September 2024 that the Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) had installed FLIR thermal cameras at three black rhino sites. The sites are Lake Nakuru National Park, Ol Pejeta Conservancy and Solio Game Reserve, which was the latest of the three. Meru National Park was named as the next site. The US Department of State Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs and WWF supported the installations. details.value: Meta built its pipeline to find posts that indicate a risk of suicide or self-injury and route them to trained reviewers, who contact local authorities in imminent cases. The Kota arrangement routes those flags to police.

details.label: Contribution of the AI
details.value: PTI reports that the chain starts with a red-flag tag on Meta's system when a student posts suicide or self-harm content. Account information is then shared with police. PTI does not say whether Meta's classifier or a user report raised the flag in the Jhunjhunu case, or what happened on arrival. In its own description (2018, updated 2021), Meta says that machine-learning detection is followed by human review before authorities are contacted. The intervention itself was police work. PTI also notes that no red-flag tags had been reported in Kota city since the launch.

record.title: Within a week of tying up with Meta to route flags of self-harm from Facebook and Instagram to Abhay Command Centre, Kota police say that they prevented a possible suicide by a Jhunjhunu student
record.summary: Kota police receive Meta's red-flag tags for posts about self-harm on Facebook and Instagram. Within a week, police said that they had prevented a possible suicide by a Jhunjhunu student.
record.account: In its newsroom, Meta describes machine-learning detection of posts about suicide. The detection covers posts about self-injury. Human review comes before authorities are contacted (Card, 2018). PTI reported from Kota on 28 May 2024 that city police under Superintendent Amrita Duhan had tied up with Meta. Its aim is to identify students exhibiting suicidal tendencies on Facebook and Instagram. When a student posts content about suicide, a red-flag tag appears on Meta's system. A student's post about self-harm triggers a red-flag tag. Account information is then shared with Kota police. For students outside Kota it goes to Abhay Command Centre. It may instead go to the district control room. There a dedicated team works round the clock in eight-hour shifts. By PTI's account, the tie-up started about a week before 28 May 2024. Within a week of the launch, police said that they had prevented a possible suicide by a student from Jhunjhunu district. The intervention therefore took place in May 2024, on a date that PTI does not give. No red-flag tags had yet been reported in the city. PTI counted nine suicides among coaching students in 2024 to date. It counted 26 in 2023. Duhan planned to extend the arrangement to Jaipur (PTI via LatestLY). No later report covers the Kota arrangement. None covers its planned extension to Jaipur. The same chain of a Meta alert routed to police has been reported in Uttar Pradesh, in Raebareli on 29 March 2026 and in Meerut on 7 June 2026.
record.purpose: Meta built its pipeline to find posts that indicate a risk of suicide or self-injury and route them to trained reviewers, who contact local authorities in imminent cases. The Kota arrangement routes those flags to police.

data.retained_case_account: PTI reported from Kota on 28 May 2024 that city police under Superintendent Amrita Duhan had tied up with Meta. It aims to identify students exhibiting suicidal tendencies on Facebook and Instagram. When a student posts suicide or self-harm content, a red-flag tag appears on Meta's system and account information is shared with Kota police. For students outside Kota it goes to Abhay Command Centre or the district control room. There a dedicated team works round the clock in eight-hour shifts. Within a week of the launch, police said they had prevented a possible suicide by a student from Jhunjhunu district. No red-flag tags had yet been reported in the city. PTI counted nine coaching-student suicides in 2024 to date and 26 in 2023. Duhan planned to extend the arrangement to Jaipur (PTI via LatestLY). Meta's newsroom describes machine-learning detection with human review before authorities are contacted (Card, 2018). The intervention date is not given.

It may instead go to the district control room. There a dedicated team works round the clock in eight-hour shifts. By PTI's account, the tie-up started about a week before 28 May 2024. Within a week of the launch, police said that they had prevented a possible suicide by a student from Jhunjhunu district. The intervention therefore took place in May 2024, on a date that PTI does not give. No red-flag tags had yet been reported in the city. PTI counted nine suicides among coaching students in 2024 to date. It counted 26 in 2023. Duhan planned to extend the arrangement to Jaipur (PTI via LatestLY). No later report covers the Kota arrangement. None covers its planned extension to Jaipur. The same chain of a Meta alert routed to police has been reported in Uttar Pradesh, in Raebareli on 29 March 2026 and in Meerut on 7 June 2026.

record.title: Researchers at Colorado State University find that four AI weather models, GraphCast among them, matched the best operational models of cyclone tracks in 2023
record.summary: Researchers at Colorado State University, who ran the models, found that four AI weather models matched the best operational models on 2023 cyclone tracks. DeepMind's GraphCast was one.
record.account: Google DeepMind's GraphCast was run live on the public charts of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) from 2023. In its blog of 14 November 2023, DeepMind says that the live model predicted Hurricane Lee's landfall in Nova Scotia in September 2023 about nine days in advance. DeepMind wrote only “In September”, so the year comes from the date of the post, 14 November 2023. This benefit does not appear in ECMWF's newsletters 177 and 178. It does not appear in the center's science blog. It does not appear in its Severe Event Catalog. MIT Technology Review quoted ECMWF's Peter Dueben: “It showed that these models are so good that we cannot avoid them anymore.” Researchers at CIRA, Colorado State University, who have no tie to DeepMind, applied the verification procedure of the National Hurricane Center (NHC) to cyclones from May to November 2023. They found that the track errors of GraphCast-operational, like those of three other AI models, were comparable to those of the best operational models. In their experiment, adding all four improved the NHC track consensus by 11% at 120 h. NHC did not use the AI models in its 2023 operations. The evaluation appeared as a preprint on 8 September 2024. After peer review it appeared in Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems on 20 October 2025. Both versions report the same 11% gain in the consensus at 120 h. The authors found that the AI models' intensity forecasts had no skill against the simplest statistical models, because the models almost always weakened the storms. In its verification report of 30 March 2026, NHC states that the 2025 season marked the first time that it incorporated AI-based models into real-time operations. It reports that the Google DeepMind ensemble mean slightly outperformed NHC at lead times from 12 to 72 h.

fields.account: Google DeepMind's GraphCast was run live on the public charts of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) from 2023. In its blog of 14 November 2023, DeepMind says that the live model predicted Hurricane Lee's landfall in Nova Scotia in September 2023 about nine days in advance. DeepMind wrote only “In September”, so the year comes from the date of the post, 14 November 2023. This benefit does not appear in ECMWF's newsletters 177 and 178. It does not appear in the center's science blog. It does not appear in its Severe Event Catalog. MIT Technology Review quoted ECMWF's Peter Dueben: “It showed that these models are so good that we cannot avoid them anymore.” Researchers at CIRA, Colorado State University, who have no tie to DeepMind, applied the verification procedure of the National Hurricane Center (NHC) to cyclones from May to November 2023. They found that the track errors of GraphCast-operational, like those of three other AI models, were comparable to those of the best operational models. In their experiment, adding all four improved the NHC track consensus by 11% at 120 h. NHC did not use the AI models in its 2023 operations. The evaluation appeared as a preprint on 8 September 2024. After peer review it appeared in Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems on 20 October 2025. Both versions report the same 11% gain in the consensus at 120 h. The authors found that the AI models' intensity forecasts had no skill against the simplest statistical models, because the models almost always weakened the storms. In its verification report of 30 March 2026, NHC states that the 2025 season marked the first time that it incorporated AI-based models into real-time operations. It reports that the Google DeepMind ensemble mean slightly outperformed NHC at lead times from 12 to 72 h.

record.title: Seibu Railway puts AI detection of people left in level crossings into full operation from 14 November 2022, while a 3D-camera system covers one crossing
record.summary: An AI system from OKI and Marubeni Network Solutions detects people left in Seibu Railway crossings. One crossing uses a 3D stereo-camera system. Both light lamps that warn train drivers.
record.account: In April 2021 a man in his 60s who was left inside the Ikebukuro No. 9 crossing was killed by a train. A trial of a crossing anomaly detection system (“踏切異常検知システム”) began in December 2021. Response.jp reported on 11 November 2022 that Seibu Railway would begin full operation of the system on 14 November 2022. The report was based on press releases. Seibu said that the system had run stably in the trial. The rollout used two alternative technologies at different crossings. One is an AI monitoring system developed by OKI and Marubeni Network Solutions. It uses skeleton recognition to detect people left in crossings. It detects objects. The other is a 3D image-analysis system from Computer Systems Laboratory that uses stereo-camera depth. When a detection occurs, the special signal lamps that warn drivers of danger operate. Live video of the site is sent to the operations control center. Full operation was announced for three crossings on the Ikebukuro and Shinjuku lines, with two more planned within fiscal 2022. Asahi reported on 16 November 2022 that the AI system covers the Ikebukuro No. 9 and Tokorozawa No. 3 crossings. It reported that the 3D system covers the Igusa No. 2 crossing. According to the transport ministry, the 3D system was the first of its kind in Japan. Yomiuri reported on 19 September 2026 that Seibu had installed AI cameras at seven crossings in all, starting with Ikebukuro No. 9. No detection figures for Seibu appear in the sources. They give no figures on accidents.

data.retained_case_account: Response.jp reported on 11 Nov 2022 that Seibu Railway would begin full operation of a “踏切異常検知システム” on 14 Nov 2022. The rollout used two alternative technologies at different crossings. One is an AI monitoring system developed by OKI and Marubeni Network Solutions. It uses skeleton recognition to detect people and objects left in crossings. The other is a 3D image-analysis system from Computer Systems Laboratory that uses stereo-camera depth. When a detection occurs, the special signal lamps that warn drivers of danger operate. Live video of the site is sent to the operations control center. Full operation was announced for three crossings on the Ikebukuro and Shinjuku lines, with two more planned within fiscal 2022. The trial that began in December 2021 was reported to have confirmed stable operation. The sources are press-release based. No detection event or accident outcome is documented.

fields.account: In April 2021 a man in his 60s who was left inside the Ikebukuro No. 9 crossing was killed by a train. A trial of a crossing anomaly detection system (“踏切異常検知システム”) began in December 2021. Response.jp reported on 11 November 2022 that Seibu Railway would begin full operation of the system on 14 November 2022. The report was based on press releases. Seibu said that the system had run stably in the trial. The rollout used two alternative technologies at different crossings. One is an AI monitoring system developed by OKI and Marubeni Network Solutions. It uses skeleton recognition to detect people left in crossings. It detects objects. The other is a 3D image-analysis system from Computer Systems Laboratory that uses stereo-camera depth. When a detection occurs, the special signal lamps that warn drivers of danger operate. Live video of the site is sent to the operations control center. Full operation was announced for three crossings on the Ikebukuro and Shinjuku lines, with two more planned within fiscal 2022. Asahi reported on 16 November 2022 that the AI system covers the Ikebukuro No. 9 and Tokorozawa No. 3 crossings. It reported that the 3D system covers the Igusa No. 2 crossing. According to the transport ministry, the 3D system was the first of its kind in Japan. Yomiuri reported on 19 September 2026 that Seibu had installed AI cameras at seven crossings in all, starting with Ikebukuro No. 9. No detection figures for Seibu appear in the sources. They give no figures on accidents.

details.value: Boulder Imaging built IdentiFlight to detect eagles and curtail turbines. In Germany it is meant to protect lesser spotted eagles at wind farms.

details.label: Contribution of the AI
details.value: The camera software detects and classifies birds and sends the shutdown signal. Validation reports measure that step against ornithologists' observations, with 97.8% correct classification of lesser spotted eagles in 2025. No study in the sources measures whether the shutdowns reduced bird deaths in Germany.

record.title: German test sites check IdentiFlight cameras that signal wind turbines to slow when they detect eagles
record.summary: IdentiFlight V5 classified lesser spotted eagles correctly in 97.8% of checked images at a German test site in 2025. No measured drop in bird deaths in Germany appears in the sources.
record.account: OekoFor and ARSU compare camera detections with observations by ornithologists at German test sites. In its dated updates, OekoFor reports that the validation for red kites was completed in October 2021. The OECD says that Germany is deploying AI-powered camera systems developed by IdentiFlight. They detect endangered lesser spotted eagles near wind turbines. They slow the blades to prevent collisions. In its updates, OekoFor reports the publication of an assessment for white-tailed eagles in May 2023. It gives no estimate of any reduction in bird deaths in Germany. It gives no start date for the tests on lesser spotted eagles. Two U.S. Geological Survey scientists argued in 2023 that the Wyoming data show little evidence of fewer eagle deaths. The Bavarian state environment office reported 31 dangerous red kite flights through rotors at a forest site since spring 2024. It reported no observed collisions. On 27 August 2026, OekoFor and ARSU reported for Boulder Imaging that IdentiFlight V5 classified lesser spotted eagles correctly in 97.8% of checked images at Kublank in 2025. On 27 October 2026, the competence center KNE (Kompetenzzentrum Naturschutz und Energiewende) listed basic recognition of V5 for the red kite. It listed the black kite. It listed the white-tailed eagle. It listed classification of the lesser spotted eagle.

fields.summary: IdentiFlight V5 classified lesser spotted eagles correctly in 97.8% of checked images at a German test site in 2025. No measured drop in bird deaths in Germany appears in the sources.
fields.account: OekoFor and ARSU compare camera detections with observations by ornithologists at German test sites. In its dated updates, OekoFor reports that the validation for red kites was completed in October 2021. The OECD says that Germany is deploying AI-powered camera systems developed by IdentiFlight. They detect endangered lesser spotted eagles near wind turbines. They slow the blades to prevent collisions. In its updates, OekoFor reports the publication of an assessment for white-tailed eagles in May 2023. It gives no estimate of any reduction in bird deaths in Germany. It gives no start date for the tests on lesser spotted eagles. Two U.S. Geological Survey scientists argued in 2023 that the Wyoming data show little evidence of fewer eagle deaths. The Bavarian state environment office reported 31 dangerous red kite flights through rotors at a forest site since spring 2024. It reported no observed collisions. On 27 August 2026, OekoFor and ARSU reported for Boulder Imaging that IdentiFlight V5 classified lesser spotted eagles correctly in 97.8% of checked images at Kublank in 2025. On 27 October 2026, the competence center KNE (Kompetenzzentrum Naturschutz und Energiewende) listed basic recognition of V5 for the red kite. It listed the black kite. It listed the white-tailed eagle. It listed classification of the lesser spotted eagle.

record.title: A threat alert from Meta, relayed through the FBI, brings Paraguayan police with psychologists to a bullied 17-year-old who praised the Uvalde shooter
record.summary: Meta flagged a post in which a Paraguayan teenager praised the Uvalde shooter. After the FBI relayed the alert, police visited him with psychologists.
record.account: On Thursday 26 May 2022, two days after the Uvalde school shooting, Paraguay's Policía Nacional and Ministerio Público received an alert. It came from Meta's platform and the FBI office in Buenos Aires. A user in Paraguay had tagged the shooter. He called himself his “fan”. He said that something similar could happen in Paraguay with more victims. Comisario Diosnel Alarcón's cybercrime department identified the owner of the Instagram profile as a 17-year-old in the “zona central”. He lived with a relative. Officials treated him as a victim of bullying. Police visited the home. Prosecutors went with them. The children's defender went. Psychologists went. They recommended urgent psychological support. They visited a friend who knew of the posts. No weapon was reported. No plan was reported.

fields.account: On Thursday 26 May 2022, two days after the Uvalde school shooting, Paraguay's Policía Nacional and Ministerio Público received an alert. It came from Meta's platform and the FBI office in Buenos Aires. A user in Paraguay had tagged the shooter. He called himself his “fan”. He said that something similar could happen in Paraguay with more victims. Comisario Diosnel Alarcón's cybercrime department identified the owner of the Instagram profile as a 17-year-old in the “zona central”. He lived with a relative. Officials treated him as a victim of bullying. Police visited the home. Prosecutors went with them. The children's defender went. Psychologists went. They recommended urgent psychological support. They visited a friend who knew of the posts. No weapon was reported. No plan was reported.

record.title: Singapore's ScamShield app flags about 5 million suspected scam text messages
record.summary: Singapore's ScamShield app filters text messages with a machine-learning model on the phone. From March 2022 to November 2023 it flagged about 5 million to users as potential scams.
record.account: ScamShield is a Singapore government app by Open Government Products, a unit of GovTech. It was developed with the National Crime Prevention Council and the Singapore Police Force. In June 2021 GovInsider described an on-device machine-learning model that files suspected scam text messages into a junk folder. The app blocks calls from numbers on a police blocklist. GovInsider reported that users had reported 722,865 text messages. It reported that 5,537 numbers had been blocked since launch. It relayed a claim of 95% detection accuracy. It quoted the product manager, Lennard Lim, on the model's need to adapt as scammers change their attacks. According to The Straits Times, the police had counted 300,500 downloads on iOS in August 2022. On 22 November 2023 the Minister of State Sun Xueling gave an oral reply to parliamentary questions. She said that ScamShield had about 750,000 downloads as of October 2023. She said that about 80,000 unique scam-tainted phone numbers had been blacklisted. She said that they had been blocked. In the reply, she states that about 5 million text messages had been flagged to users as potential scams. The ministry counts both figures from March 2022. She said that ScamShield had been effective in protecting users. She cited about 180 million suspected scam calls blocked at network level in the first half of 2023. That figure is a measure by the telecommunications operators. It is separate from the app. The Straits Times reported on the same day that the minister said that the app cannot work well unless users set its permissions. On a page updated on 18 August 2026, the Ministry of Digital Development and Information reported growth in the enhanced app, launched in August 2024. It had recorded 1.61 million installations, up from 944,000. The police have not published an evaluation of the losses that victims avoided.

fields.account: ScamShield is a Singapore government app by Open Government Products, a unit of GovTech. It was developed with the National Crime Prevention Council and the Singapore Police Force. In June 2021 GovInsider described an on-device machine-learning model that files suspected scam text messages into a junk folder. The app blocks calls from numbers on a police blocklist. It quoted the product manager, Lennard Lim, on the model's need to adapt as scammers change their attacks. According to The Straits Times, the police had counted 300,500 downloads on iOS in August 2022. On 22 November 2023 the Minister of State Sun Xueling gave an oral reply to parliamentary questions. She said that ScamShield had about 750,000 downloads as of October 2023. She said that about 80,000 unique scam-tainted phone numbers had been blacklisted. She said that they had been blocked. In the reply, she states that about 5 million text messages had been flagged to users as potential scams. The ministry counts both figures from March 2022. She said that ScamShield had been effective in protecting users. She cited about 180 million suspected scam calls blocked at network level in the first half of 2023. That figure is a measure by the telecommunications operators. It is separate from the app. The Straits Times reported on the same day that the minister said that the app cannot work well unless users set its permissions. On a page updated on 18 August 2026, the Ministry of Digital Development and Information reported growth in the enhanced app, launched in August 2024. It had recorded 1.61 million installations, up from 944,000. The police have not published an evaluation of the losses that victims avoided.

details.label: Purpose
details.value: Google built the system to detect earthquakes with the accelerometers in Android phones and to warn users where shaking is expected, seconds before the slower destructive waves arrive. It covers quakes of magnitude 4.5 and above.

details.label: Contribution of the AI
details.value: Google's system produced the alert from start to finish. Its servers combined signals from the accelerometers of many phones to detect the quake and estimate its size. They then pushed alerts to phones where shaking was expected, ahead of the slower S-waves. Google does not use the words AI or machine learning when it describes this process. In a paper in Science in 2025, the authors describe it as algorithms that detect earthquakes with smartphones. Reporters give different lead times (seconds, about 10 seconds, about one minute), and Google promises seconds.

record.title: Google's Android Earthquake Alerts reached phones in Alanya seconds before a quake of magnitude 5.1 in the Mediterranean on 5 January 2022
record.summary: Google's Android Earthquake Alerts System sent Android users near Alanya, Turkey, a warning seconds before a magnitude 5.1 offshore quake on 5 January 2022.
record.account: At 06:21 local time on 5 January 2022 an earthquake struck the Mediterranean about 57 km off Alanya, Antalya, Turkey, at a depth of roughly 40 km. The U.S. Geological Survey put its magnitude at 5.1. AFAD, Turkey's disaster and emergency agency, put it at 5.3. Google had introduced its Android Earthquake Alerts System in Turkey in June 2021. Yeni Şafak and DonanımHaber reported the same day that the system sent Android users an alert for a magnitude 5.3 quake seconds before the shaking. The alert was a visual message with a sound. AFAD and the Alanya district governor reported no damage. They reported no injuries. İndigo Dergisi claimed on 5 January that the alert came about a minute ahead. On 7 January 2022 Hürriyet put the lead at about 10 seconds. It reported that most users who posted about the alert said that they panicked. On 18 January 2022 NTV repeated the figure of about a minute. On 3 February 2022 Google said that the system had alerted users to two January quakes centered on Alanya and Balıkesir. In July 2023 BBC Newsnight reported that its reporters had spoken with hundreds of Android users in Adana, Iskenderun and Osmaniye. They found no one who received a warning from the same system before the main shock of 6 February 2023. Google's product lead told the BBC that he was confident that the system fired and sent alerts. Google staff published a study on 11 August 2026. They report that the system sent alerts to more than 16 million users for the magnitude 6.2 earthquake at Marmara Ereğlisi on 23 April 2025.

produced_by: A magnitude 5.1 (AFAD 5.3) quake above the 4.5 alert threshold, centered about 57 km offshore and roughly 40 km deep. So the push alert could outrun the slower S-waves to the coast.

Enough Android phones near the epicenter with Earthquake Alerts on to trigger Google's server-side detection. Per Google's 3 February 2022 presentation it runs on Android 5.0 and later and users can switch it off.
Crowdsourced phone detection was the only input: Google partners with the ShakeAlert seismic network only in California, Oregon and Washington
must_hold: The server's magnitude and location estimate must be right and early. The 2025 Science paper reports only 36% of alert recipients got the alert before shaking.
Recipients must know what to do with seconds of notice. Hürriyet reported on 7 January 2022 that most users who posted about the Alanya alert said they panicked
The phone must have location and the Earthquake Alerts setting enabled

data.retained_case_account: At 06:21 local time on 5 January 2022 a magnitude 5.1 (USGS; AFAD 5.3) earthquake struck the Mediterranean about 57 km off Alanya, Antalya, Turkey. Depth: roughly 40 km. Yeni Şafak and DonanımHaber reported the same day on Google's Android Earthquake Alerts System, introduced in Turkey in June 2021. It sent an audible and visual alert for a magnitude 5.3 quake to Android users seconds before the shaking. Hürriyet put the lead at about 10 seconds, while NTV and İndigo Dergisi claimed about a minute. AFAD and the Alanya district governor reported no damage or injuries. On 3 February 2022 Google said the system had alerted users to two January quakes centered on Alanya and Balıkesir.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: The alert was produced end to end by Google's system. Accelerometer triggers from many phones were combined on Google's servers to detect the quake and estimate its size. Alerts were pushed to phones in the expected shaking zone ahead of the slower S-waves. Google's own descriptions of this process do not use the words AI or machine learning. The reported lead time varies by outlet (seconds, about 10 seconds, about one minute); Google promises seconds.

fields.account: At 06:21 local time on 5 January 2022 an earthquake struck the Mediterranean about 57 km off Alanya, Antalya, Turkey, at a depth of roughly 40 km. The U.S. Geological Survey put its magnitude at 5.1. AFAD, Turkey's disaster and emergency agency, put it at 5.3. Google had introduced its Android Earthquake Alerts System in Turkey in June 2021. Yeni Şafak and DonanımHaber reported the same day that the system sent Android users an alert for a magnitude 5.3 quake seconds before the shaking. The alert was a visual message with a sound. AFAD and the Alanya district governor reported no damage. They reported no injuries. İndigo Dergisi claimed on 5 January that the alert came about a minute ahead. On 7 January 2022 Hürriyet put the lead at about 10 seconds. It reported that most users who posted about the alert said that they panicked. On 18 January 2022 NTV repeated the figure of about a minute. On 3 February 2022 Google said that the system had alerted users to two January quakes centered on Alanya and Balıkesir. In July 2023 BBC Newsnight reported that its reporters had spoken with hundreds of Android users in Adana, Iskenderun and Osmaniye. They found no one who received a warning from the same system before the main shock of 6 February 2023. Google's product lead told the BBC that he was confident that the system fired and sent alerts. Google staff published a study on 11 August 2026. They report that the system sent alerts to more than 16 million users for the magnitude 6.2 earthquake at Marmara Ereğlisi on 23 April 2025.

value.text: The alert was a single warning before one quake. The recorded follow-up is a BBC Newsnight investigation of July 2023. Its reporters found no one in three Turkish cities who received a warning from the same system before the main shock of 6 February 2023.

fields.purpose: Google built the system to detect earthquakes with the accelerometers in Android phones and to warn users where shaking is expected, seconds before the slower destructive waves arrive. It covers quakes of magnitude 4.5 and above.

Google built the system to detect earthquakes with the accelerometers in Android phones and to warn users where shaking is expected, seconds before the slower destructive waves arrive. It covers quakes of magnitude 4.5 and above.

display.answer: Observed 5 January 2022. AFAD's statement, quoted on the day, gives the time of the earthquake, and the reports say that the alert arrived seconds before the shaking on that morning.

produced_by: A magnitude 5.1 (AFAD 5.3) quake above the 4.5 alert threshold, centered about 57 km offshore and roughly 40 km deep. So the push alert could outrun the slower S-waves to the coast.

Enough Android phones near the epicenter with Earthquake Alerts on to trigger Google's server-side detection. Per Google's 3 February 2022 presentation it runs on Android 5.0 and later and users can switch it off.
Crowdsourced phone detection was the only input: Google partners with the ShakeAlert seismic network only in California, Oregon and Washington
must_hold: The server's magnitude and location estimate must be right and early. The 2025 Science paper reports only 36% of alert recipients got the alert before shaking.
Recipients must know what to do with seconds of notice. Hürriyet reported on 7 January 2022 that most users who posted about the Alanya alert said they panicked
The phone must have location and the Earthquake Alerts setting enabled

echoes.setting: Kahramanmaraş (Pazarcık) M7.8 earthquake, southern Turkey: BBC reporters found no Android user who received a warning before the main shock
Mw 6.2 Marmara Ereğlisi earthquake near Istanbul: a study by Google staff reports that the system alerted more than 16 million users, with a median warning of 56 seconds for weak shaking

evidence.citation: Stogaitis M (2020). Earthquake detection and early alerts, now on your Android phone. Google, The Keyword, 11 August 2020.
evidence.title: Earthquake detection and early alerts, now on your Android phone
evidence.quote: The server then combines information from many phones to figure out if an earthquake is happening.

evidence.citation: Yeni Şafak (2022). Google depremi önceden bildi: Antalya depremi hissedilmeden kullanıcılarını uyardı. Yeni Şafak, 5 January 2022.
evidence.title: Google depremi önceden bildi: Antalya depremi hissedilmeden kullanıcılarını uyardı
evidence.quote: Depremden saniyeler önce bazı Android kullanıcıları, Google Android’in deprem erken uyarı sisteminden depreme dair telefonlarına 5.3 büyüklüğünde bir depremin olacağına dair sesli ve görsel bir uyarı mesajı gönderildi.
evidence.quote_translation: Seconds before the earthquake, an audible and visual warning message about the earthquake, saying that an earthquake of magnitude 5.3 would occur, was sent from Google Android's earthquake early warning system to the phones of some Android users.

evidence.citation: DonanımHaber (2022). Google erken uyarı sistemi, Alanya depremini saniyeler öncesinden bildi. DonanımHaber, 5 January 2022.
evidence.title: Google erken uyarı sistemi, Alanya depremini saniyeler öncesinden bildi
evidence.quote: Google deprem uyarı sistemi, erken saatlerde meydana gelen depremden saniyeler önce, o bölgede oturan kullanıcılara deprem uyarı sistemi aracılığıyla bir uyarı mesajı gönderdi.
evidence.quote_translation: Google's earthquake warning system, seconds before the earthquake that occurred in the early hours, sent a warning message through the earthquake warning system to users living in that region.

evidence.citation: Öztürk T (2022). Erken uyarı sistemi tartışması! Depremin olacağını 10 saniye önceden bilmek güvenli mi? Hürriyet, 7 January 2022.
evidence.title: Erken uyarı sistemi tartışması! Depremin olacağını 10 saniye önceden bilmek güvenli mi?
evidence.quote: Depremden yaklaşık 10 saniye önce, cep telefonlarına 'deprem olacak' bildirimi gitti.
evidence.quote_translation: About 10 seconds before the earthquake, a 'there will be an earthquake' notification went out to cell phones.

evidence.citation: Hürriyet (2022). Google, Android Deprem Uyarı Sistemi’ni tanıttı. Hürriyet, 3 February 2022.
evidence.title: Google, Android Deprem Uyarı Sistemi’ni tanıttı
evidence.quote: Ocak ayında ülkemizde merkezi Alanya ve Balıkesir olmak üzere 4.5 büyüklüğü üzeri iki depreme dair Android kullanıcılarına uyarı bildirisi gönderen Android Deprem Uyarı Sistemi
evidence.quote_translation: The Android Earthquake Alerts System, which in January sent warning notifications to Android users about two earthquakes above magnitude 4.5 in our country, centered in Alanya and Balıkesir

evidence.citation: İndigo Dergisi (2022). Google Deprem Uyarı Sistemi nasıl açılır? Alanya depremini 1 dakika önceden nasıl haber verdi? İndigo Dergisi, 5 January 2022.
evidence.title: Google Deprem Uyarı Sistemi nasıl açılır? Alanya depremini 1 dakika önceden nasıl haber verdi?
evidence.quote: AFAD’dan yapılan açıklamada “Akdeniz’de Antalya’nın Alanya ilçesi açıklarında saat 06.21’de 5,3 büyüklüğünde bir deprem meydana geldi. Gelişmeleri takip ediyoruz” denildi.
evidence.quote_translation: The statement from AFAD said, "An earthquake of magnitude 5.3 occurred at 06:21 in the Mediterranean off Antalya's Alanya district. We are following developments."

evidence.citation: NTV (2022). Deprem uyarı sistemi nedir, nasıl çalışır? NTV, 18 January 2022.
evidence.title: Deprem uyarı sistemi nedir, nasıl çalışır?
evidence.quote: Geçtiğimiz haftalarda Google'ın sunduğu deprem uyarı sistemi, Alanya açıklarında meydana gelen 5.3'lük depremi 1 dakika öncesinden tahmin ederek kullanıcılarına sesli uyarı göndermişti.
evidence.quote_translation: In recent weeks, the earthquake warning system offered by Google had predicted the 5.3 earthquake that occurred off the coast of Alanya 1 minute in advance and sent its users an audible warning.

evidence.citation: Yeni Akit (2022). Android deprem uyarı sistemi nedir, nasıl yapılır, nasıl kullanılır? Yeni Akit, 18 January 2022.
evidence.title: Android deprem uyarı sistemi nedir, nasıl yapılır, nasıl kullanılır?
evidence.quote: Android deprem uyarı sistemi sayesinde 5 Ocak 2022 sabahı Antalya’da meydana gelen depremin kısa süre öncesinde vatandaşlara uyarı yollandı.
evidence.quote_translation: Thanks to the Android Earthquake Alerts System, a warning was sent to citizens shortly before the earthquake that occurred in Antalya on the morning of January 5, 2022.

evidence.citation: Hürriyet (2022). Deprem uyarı sistemi nasıl yapılır, nedir? Android erken deprem uyarı sistemi kullanım detayları. Hürriyet, 18 January 2022.
evidence.title: Deprem uyarı sistemi nasıl yapılır, nedir? Android erken deprem uyarı sistemi kullanım detayları
evidence.quote: Olası bir depremi 10 saniye önceden haber verebilen deprem uyarı sistemi Alanya'da yaşanan depremi gerçekleşmeden 1 dakika kadar önce bölgede oturanlara Google tarafından bildirilmişti.
evidence.quote_translation: Through the earthquake warning system, which can give notice of a possible earthquake 10 seconds in advance, Google had notified those living in the region of the earthquake in Alanya about 1 minute before it happened.

evidence.citation: U.S. Geological Survey (2022). M 5.1 - 67 km SSW of Okurcalar, Turkey (event us7000g94d). USGS Earthquake Hazards Program.
evidence.title: M 5.1 - 67 km SSW of Okurcalar, Turkey
evidence.quote: M 5.1 - 67 km SSW of Okurcalar, Turkey

evidence.citation: Duckett C (2021). Android opens up earthquake alerts and end-to-end encrypted messages. ZDNet, 16 June 2021. The story only relays the makers' account. The story predates the earthquake.
evidence.title: Android opens up earthquake alerts and end-to-end encrypted messages
evidence.quote: The system is already live in New Zealand and Greece, with Turkey, the Philippines, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyz Republic, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan coming on board.

evidence.citation: Lee F (2021). 6 new features on Android this summer. Google, The Keyword, 15 June 2021.
evidence.title: 6 new features on Android this summer
evidence.quote: Today, we're introducing the Android Earthquake Alerts System in Turkey, the Philippines, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyz Republic, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan.

evidence.citation: Google (n.d.). Android early earthquake warnings. Google Crisis Resilience.
evidence.title: Android early earthquake warnings
evidence.quote: These alerts are only sent for earthquakes of magnitude 4.5 or greater.

evidence.citation: Allen RM, Barski A, Berman M, et al. (2025). Global earthquake detection and warning using Android phones. Science 389(6757):254-259.
evidence.title: Global earthquake detection and warning using Android phones
evidence.quote: User feedback shows that 85% of people receiving an alert felt shaking, and 36, 28, and 23% received the alert before, during, and after shaking, respectively.

evidence.citation: Clayton J, Derico B, Foster A, Google alert failed to warn people of Turkey earthquake, BBC News, 27 July 2023. BBC Newsnight reporters with no stake in the system interviewed hundreds of Android users in Adana, Iskenderun and Osmaniye. They found no one who received a warning before the 6 February 2023 main shock, while Google maintained that alerts were sent.
evidence.title: Google alert failed to warn people of Turkey earthquake
evidence.quote: we couldn't find anyone who got a warning ahead of the first, most powerful quake

evidence.citation: Nature Communications (Springer Nature), Performance and user response of android's smartphone-based alerts in the 2025 Marmara Ereğlisi earthquake, 11 August 2026.
evidence.title: Performance and user response of android's smartphone-based alerts in the 2025 Marmara Ereğlisi earthquake
evidence.quote: This study presents a comprehensive evaluation of Google's Android Earthquake Alert (AEA) system during the Mw 6.2 Marmara Ereğlisi, Türkiye earthquake. AEA detected the event 5.31 seconds after its initiation, alerting over 16 million users.

fields.summary: Google's Android Earthquake Alerts System sent Android users near Alanya, Turkey, a warning seconds before a magnitude 5.1 offshore quake on 5 January 2022.
fields.account: At 06:21 local time on 5 January 2022 an earthquake struck the Mediterranean about 57 km off Alanya, Antalya, Turkey, at a depth of roughly 40 km. The U.S. Geological Survey put its magnitude at 5.1. AFAD, Turkey's disaster and emergency agency, put it at 5.3. Google had introduced its Android Earthquake Alerts System in Turkey in June 2021. Yeni Şafak and DonanımHaber reported the same day that the system sent Android users an alert for a magnitude 5.3 quake seconds before the shaking. The alert was a visual message with a sound. AFAD and the Alanya district governor reported no damage. They reported no injuries. İndigo Dergisi claimed on 5 January that the alert came about a minute ahead. On 7 January 2022 Hürriyet put the lead at about 10 seconds. It reported that most users who posted about the alert said that they panicked. On 18 January 2022 NTV repeated the figure of about a minute. On 3 February 2022 Google said that the system had alerted users to two January quakes centered on Alanya and Balıkesir. In July 2023 BBC Newsnight reported that its reporters had spoken with hundreds of Android users in Adana, Iskenderun and Osmaniye. They found no one who received a warning from the same system before the main shock of 6 February 2023. Google's product lead told the BBC that he was confident that the system fired and sent alerts. Google staff published a study on 11 August 2026. They report that the system sent alerts to more than 16 million users for the magnitude 6.2 earthquake at Marmara Ereğlisi on 23 April 2025.

record.title: Sanyo Electric Railway puts Optage's AI cameras into use at two crossings in July 2021 after a trial at three crossings
record.summary: In July 2021 Sanyo Electric Railway began to use Optage's AI analysis of video from crossing cameras. It detects people left inside two crossings to warn train drivers.
record.account: On 11 August 2020 Optage announced a field trial of AI image analysis of crossing surveillance cameras. Mynavi News reported on 12 August 2020, from the press release, that Optage, Sanyo Electric Railway and the Sanyo Electric Railway Information Center had begun the trial. It ran from early August to mid-October 2020 at three crossings on Sanyo Electric Railway lines. Edge devices analyze the video in real time to detect people, including those with prams. Detection covers people in wheelchairs. The aim is to stop trains safely by signaling the driver through a special signal lamp. The system notifies the operations center over an IP-VPN. Accuracy in rain and at night was to be verified with K4Digital. Full deployment was targeted for spring 2021. Optage reported on 29 June 2021 that Sanyo had adopted the system after the trial. Optage reports that the system offers comparable function at lower cost than laser radar. It supplies no numerical results of detection. It gives no measured reduction in accidents. Kobe Shimbun reported on 3 August 2021 that Sanyo had put the system into use from July 2021 at two busy crossings. They are the Shikama depot crossing in Himeji and the Tsukimiyama crossing in Suma, Kobe. Kobe Shimbun notes that 137 of Sanyo's 165 crossings already had automatic detectors that have difficulty detecting people. Sanyo's electrical systems section manager told the paper that the company hoped to add sites after reviewing the results. It reports no detections or measured safety results after the rollout.

fields.summary: In July 2021 Sanyo Electric Railway began to use Optage's AI analysis of video from crossing cameras. It detects people left inside two crossings to warn train drivers.
fields.account: On 11 August 2020 Optage announced a field trial of AI image analysis of crossing surveillance cameras. Mynavi News reported on 12 August 2020, from the press release, that Optage, Sanyo Electric Railway and the Sanyo Electric Railway Information Center had begun the trial. It ran from early August to mid-October 2020 at three crossings on Sanyo Electric Railway lines. Edge devices analyze the video in real time to detect people, including those with prams. Detection covers people in wheelchairs. The aim is to stop trains safely by signaling the driver through a special signal lamp. The system notifies the operations center over an IP-VPN. Accuracy in rain and at night was to be verified with K4Digital. Full deployment was targeted for spring 2021. Optage reported on 29 June 2021 that Sanyo had adopted the system after the trial. Optage reports that the system offers comparable function at lower cost than laser radar. It supplies no numerical results of detection. It gives no measured reduction in accidents. Kobe Shimbun reported on 3 August 2021 that Sanyo had put the system into use from July 2021 at two busy crossings. They are the Shikama depot crossing in Himeji and the Tsukimiyama crossing in Suma, Kobe. Kobe Shimbun notes that 137 of Sanyo's 165 crossings already had automatic detectors that have difficulty detecting people. Sanyo's electrical systems section manager told the paper that the company hoped to add sites after reviewing the results. It reports no detections or measured safety results after the rollout.

record.title: In a trial, Delhi Police facial recognition matches 2,930 children in care homes, but the Delhi High Court records that it has not helped solve any missing-child case
record.summary: The Wire identifies Delhi Police's facial recognition as Innefu Labs' AI Vision. It produced 2,930 matches among children in care. The High Court later recorded that it solved no case.
record.account: In Sadhan Haldar v NCT of Delhi, the Delhi High Court had pressed the police to test facial recognition. The Ministry of Women and Child Development then supplied data on about seven lakh missing children from the Track Child portal. The Wire cites the Bureau of Police Research and Development's Compendium of Equipment. It lists two facial recognition systems that the police bought on 28 March 2018. Innefu Labs manufactured them. Pelorus Technologies supplied them. On 22 April 2018 the Press Trust of India (PTI) reported in Business Standard on an affidavit from the ministry to the Delhi High Court. In the affidavit, the ministry said that the Delhi Police, “on a trial basis, used the FRS on 45,000 children living in different children's homes”. The ministry added that 2,930 children “could be recognised between April 6 and April 10”. The ministry's secretary Rakesh Srivastava said that the police shared the outcome on 10 April. PTI also reported that identities “have been established and efforts are on to help them reunite with their families”. On 23 August 2018 Delhi Police counsel Rahul Mehra told the High Court: “The software is not good. There is only two per cent match” (NDTV). That was in a habeas corpus matter about women missing from a placement agency. On 22 January 2019 the High Court (Hima Kohli and Manoj Kumar Ohri JJ) recorded in Sadhan Haldar what it was told. The software “has not helped in cracking any case of missing children so far”, against 5,160 children untraced out of 19,916 reported missing in 2016–2018. On 23 August 2019 the ministry's counsel told the Delhi High Court that the software sometimes matched photographs of missing boys with girls. The court had asked why fewer than 1 percent of children were matched. It ordered the ministry to chart each identified child (PTI, 24 August 2019). The chart was also to show the status of the child's return home. The Delhi High Court's order of 26 April 2019 records 10,617 probable matches from the ministry's data. Of these, 3,202 identities were verified. The report gives no count of reunifications. On 2 and 3 July 2025 the Pulitzer Center republished The Wire's investigations. They quote a blog post in which Innefu claims that its AI Vision product “helped in identifying 3000 missing children” in its first four days. No reunification has been documented.

data.retained_case_account: PTI reported on 22 April 2018 (Business Standard) on an affidavit from the Ministry of Women and Child Development to the Delhi High Court. It said that the Delhi Police, “on a trial basis, used the FRS on 45,000 children living in different children's homes”. Also, 2,930 children “could be recognized between April 6 and April 10”. The ministry's secretary Rakesh Srivastava said that the police shared the outcome on 10 April. In Sadhan Haldar v NCT of Delhi, the court had pressed the police to test-run facial recognition. The ministry had then supplied data on about seven lakh missing children from the Track Child portal. The same report says that identities “have been established and efforts are on to help them reunite with their families”. No reunification is documented in any cited source. The Wire (republished by the Pulitzer Center, 2–3 July 2025) cites the Bureau of Police Research and Development's Compendium of Equipment. It says that the police bought two facial recognition systems on 28 March 2018, manufactured by Innefu Labs and supplied by Pelorus Technologies. It quotes an Innefu blog claiming its AI Vision product “helped in identifying 3000 missing children” in its first four days. On 23 August 2018 Delhi Police counsel Rahul Mehra told the High Court: “The software is not good. There is only two percent match” (NDTV). That was in a habeas corpus matter about women missing from a placement agency. On 22 January 2019 the High Court (Hima Kohli and Manoj Kumar Ohri JJ) recorded in Sadhan Haldar what it was told. The software “has not helped in cracking any case of missing children so far”, against 5,160 children untraced out of 19,916 reported missing in 2016–2018. A Centre for Internet and Society (CIS India) report gives 10,617 matches, of which 3,202 identities were verified, and no reunification count.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: The software produced the 2,930 matches reported in the ministry's affidavit. The claim rests on the police's report of raw output, relayed by PTI, and on the vendor's blog. No cited source verifies a single match to a reunification. The police counsel described the match rate as two percent in August 2018. The Delhi High Court recorded in January 2019 that the software had not helped crack any case. The CIS India figures (10,617 matches, 3,202 identities verified) come from a report that is not among the sources.

fields.account: In Sadhan Haldar v NCT of Delhi, the Delhi High Court had pressed the police to test facial recognition. The Ministry of Women and Child Development then supplied data on about seven lakh missing children from the Track Child portal. The Wire cites the Bureau of Police Research and Development's Compendium of Equipment. It lists two facial recognition systems that the police bought on 28 March 2018. Innefu Labs manufactured them. Pelorus Technologies supplied them. On 22 April 2018 the Press Trust of India (PTI) reported in Business Standard on an affidavit from the ministry to the Delhi High Court. In the affidavit, the ministry said that the Delhi Police, “on a trial basis, used the FRS on 45,000 children living in different children's homes”. The ministry added that 2,930 children “could be recognised between April 6 and April 10”. The ministry's secretary Rakesh Srivastava said that the police shared the outcome on 10 April. PTI also reported that identities “have been established and efforts are on to help them reunite with their families”. On 23 August 2018 Delhi Police counsel Rahul Mehra told the High Court: “The software is not good. There is only two per cent match” (NDTV). That was in a habeas corpus matter about women missing from a placement agency. On 22 January 2019 the High Court (Hima Kohli and Manoj Kumar Ohri JJ) recorded in Sadhan Haldar what it was told. The software “has not helped in cracking any case of missing children so far”, against 5,160 children untraced out of 19,916 reported missing in 2016–2018. On 23 August 2019 the ministry's counsel told the Delhi High Court that the software sometimes matched photographs of missing boys with girls. The court had asked why fewer than 1 percent of children were matched. It ordered the ministry to chart each identified child (PTI, 24 August 2019). The chart was also to show the status of the child's return home. The Delhi High Court's order of 26 April 2019 records 10,617 probable matches from the ministry's data. Of these, 3,202 identities were verified. The report gives no count of reunifications. On 2 and 3 July 2025 the Pulitzer Center republished The Wire's investigations. They quote a blog post in which Innefu claims that its AI Vision product “helped in identifying 3000 missing children” in its first four days. No reunification has been documented.

The court had asked why fewer than 1 percent of children were matched. It ordered the ministry to chart each identified child (PTI, 24 August 2019). The chart was also to show the status of the child's return home. The Delhi High Court's order of 26 April 2019 records 10,617 probable matches from the ministry's data. Of these, 3,202 identities were verified. The report gives no count of reunifications. On 2 and 3 July 2025 the Pulitzer Center republished The Wire's investigations. They quote a blog post in which Innefu claims that its AI Vision product “helped in identifying 3000 missing children” in its first four days. No reunification has been documented.

record.account: In a Forbes piece of 8 March 2026, Sastry Durvasula describes AI alerts that send suspected scams to customer care staff. The fraud department receives the alerts. Durvasula is TIAA's chief operating, information and digital officer. He does not mention the 76-year-old participant. On 17 June 2026 TIAA's CEO, Thasunda Brown Duckett, spoke on Fortune's podcast Fortune 500: Titans and Disruptors of Industry. She told Fortune that an AI alert helped staff stop a scam involving a 76-year-old participant’s retirement savings. Fortune's first article on the podcast, published the same day, reports that the participant was trying to withdraw his entire $3 million portfolio. It quotes Duckett as saying that AI by itself would not necessarily have protected him. Fortune published a lightly edited transcript of the interview on 22 June 2026. In the interview, Duckett says that a portfolio manager referred the concern to the fraud team, which spent hours with the participant and contacted his daughter. She says that the money did not move. In the transcript, she describes retirement holdings above $3 million and does not itemize an attempted transfer. No statement from the participant is supplied. No record of a transaction is supplied. No separate investigation is supplied.
