fields.summary: TIAA's CEO said that an unnamed AI tool flagged a 76-year-old's unusual withdrawal. Staff then kept his retirement savings of more than $3 million from moving.
fields.account: In a Forbes piece of 8 March 2026, Sastry Durvasula describes AI alerts that send suspected scams to customer care staff. The fraud department receives the alerts. Durvasula is TIAA's chief operating, information and digital officer. He does not mention the 76-year-old participant. On 17 June 2026 TIAA's CEO, Thasunda Brown Duckett, spoke on Fortune's podcast Fortune 500: Titans and Disruptors of Industry. She told Fortune that an AI alert helped staff stop a scam involving a 76-year-old participant’s retirement savings. Fortune's first article on the podcast, published the same day, reports that the participant was trying to withdraw his entire $3 million portfolio. It quotes Duckett as saying that AI by itself would not necessarily have protected him. Fortune published a lightly edited transcript of the interview on 22 June 2026. In the interview, Duckett says that a portfolio manager referred the concern to the fraud team, which spent hours with the participant and contacted his daughter. She says that the money did not move. In the transcript, she describes retirement holdings above $3 million and does not itemize an attempted transfer. No statement from the participant is supplied. No record of a transaction is supplied. No separate investigation is supplied.

record.title: Federal analysts detect anomalous Medicare billing. $4.41 billion in claims is held in escrow
record.summary: Justice Department analysts found anomalous Medicare billing through proactive data analytics. $4.41 billion was held in escrow. The software is unnamed. The department has not said that it used AI.
record.account: In June 2024 the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services called the 2023 billing volume for two types of intermittent urinary catheter codes significant. The agency called it a highly suspect anomaly. The American Hospital Association said that accountable care organizations had reported the suspect billing. On 18 June 2025 a federal indictment in the Eastern District of New York, United States v. Nakhmatullaev et al., set out the alleged scheme. On 30 June 2025 the Department of Justice reported that its analysts had detected the anomalous billing in Operation Gold Rush. The Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General and the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services held $4.41 billion in escrow from about $4.45 billion scheduled for payment. Medicare paid about $41 million. Supplemental insurers paid about $900 million. The Department of Justice stated that the health agencies intended to seek the return of the escrow to the Medicare trust fund. In the same announcement the Department of Justice proposed an AI-enabled Data Fusion Center. The announcement does not establish that AI was used in the Gold Rush detection. On 3 February 2026 the Department of Justice announced that a Brooklyn banker had pleaded guilty to laundering proceeds of the Medicare fraud for the transnational criminal organization. It reported on 14 August 2026 that 35 people had been charged. It reported that 16 had been convicted, after a money-laundering guilty plea the previous day. These later announcements do not establish the final disposition of the $4.41 billion in escrow.

record.brief: The Department of Justice reported on 30 June 2025 that its analysts and their collaborators had detected anomalous Medicare billing in Operation Gold Rush. According to the department, health agencies stopped all but about $41 million of about $4.45 billion scheduled for payment. The agencies were the Office of Inspector General of the Department of Health and Human Services and the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services. The $4.41 billion that was stopped went into escrow. The Justice Department said that the health agencies intended to seek its return to the Medicare trust fund. In its later announcements, the department does not say what finally became of that money.[1] Medicare supplemental insurers still paid about $900 million. The Justice Department credits the detection to proactive data analytics. In the same release, it announced plans for an AI-enabled Data Fusion Center. According to the American Hospital Association, accountable care organizations had also reported the suspect billing for intermittent urinary catheters. In June 2024 the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services called the 2023 volume of that billing highly suspect.[2] No source shows that AI flagged these claims. None says what share of the hold came from the analytics.[3]

record.title: Vyntra's (formerly NetGuardians) AI risk models may have blocked fraudulent payments at unnamed banks, including a USD 500,000 ATM scheme
record.summary: Vyntra credits its AI risk models with blocking payments of USD 7,500 to CHF 1,000,000. It credits them with stopping a USD 500,000 (KSh 58 million) ATM fraud that ended in arrests.
record.account: The metadata of Vyntra's “Fraud Cases” page dates it to 4 April 2022. The cases themselves are undated. On the page, Vyntra states that “Our solutions stop the fraud before the money leaves the bank”. It lists about two dozen short case studies at unnamed banks. In one, an account takeover after pharming was stopped before a CHF 19,990 payment. In another, an impersonation led a bank employee to validate a CHF 1,000,000 transaction, which was blocked because the beneficiary was unusual at bank level. Other cases involve voice phishing, fake technical support, impersonation of a chief executive, business email compromise, romance scams and redirected invoices. On the page, Vyntra says that payments of EUR 22,114, EUR 33,170, USD 7,500, GBP 21,000, EUR 125,000, EUR 170,000, USD 100,000, USD 170,000 and USD 850,000 were stopped in these cases. In each, variables of the e-banking payment (beneficiary, country, amount, currency, browser, screen resolution, language) did not match a usual profile. In some cases the profile was the customer's. In others it was the bank's. There are two internal-fraud cases. In one case “fraudsters were arrested while attempting to withdraw USD 500,000 (KSh 58 million) from the second bank's ATMs”. The models had flagged the unusual timing of withdrawals. They had flagged their unusual frequency. NetGuardians, a Swiss company, merged with Belgium's Intix to form Vyntra in June 2025 (FinTech Global, 19 June 2025). “NetGuardians solution” still appears in one entry on the page. On the current page, the CHF 19,990 example is placed in Switzerland. No customer on the page is identified. No bank on the page is identified. The page supplies no dated event, no finding by a regulator and no court record. The page is the vendor's own account. In a separate, undated case study, Vyntra names Sidian Bank in Nairobi as a client from April 2019. In it, Sidian's head of internal audit, Peter Karichu, says that the software flagged rapid ATM withdrawals one weekend in mid-December 2019. He says that the fraudsters were arrested at another bank. Vyntra gives no amount for that case. The Sidian case may or may not be the KSh 58 million case.

The part that its models played is therefore not established.[3]

It also says that fraudsters were arrested while attempting to withdraw USD 500,000 (KSh 58 million). Others describe blocked payments of up to CHF 1,000,000. The page names no customer or bank, and the cases are undated. A separate case study from Vyntra names Sidian Bank in Nairobi as a client and describes an ATM fraud that the software flagged in mid-December 2019. It gives no amount, so the Sidian case may or may not be the KSh 58 million case.[2] The “Fraud Cases” page supplies no finding by a regulator and no court record. Every account of the cases comes from Vyntra, so the part that its models played is not established.[3]

data.retained_case_account: Vyntra's “Fraud Cases” page was published 4 April 2022 per its page metadata; the cases themselves are undated. It states that “Our solutions stop the fraud before the money leaves the bank” and lists about two dozen short case studies at unnamed banks. One is an account takeover after pharming stopped before a CHF 19,990 payment. Another is an impersonation that led a bank employee to validate a CHF 1,000,000 transaction, blocked because the beneficiary was unusual at bank level. There are vishing, tech-support, CEO-fraud, business-email-compromise, romance and invoice-redirection cases. Their payments of EUR 22,114, EUR 33,170, USD 7,500, GBP 21,000, EUR 125,000, EUR 170,000, USD 100,000, USD 170,000 and USD 850,000 were stopped. Transaction or e-banking session variables (beneficiary, country, amount, currency, browser, screen resolution, language) did not match the customer's or bank's usual profile. There are two internal-fraud cases. In one case “fraudsters were arrested while attempting to withdraw USD 500,000 (KSh 58 million) from the second bank's ATMs”. The models had flagged unusual timing and frequency of withdrawals. One entry still names “NetGuardians solution”, the Swiss company that merged with Belgium's Intix to form Vyntra in June 2025 (FinTech Global, 19 June 2025). No customer or bank is identified, and no dated event, regulator finding or court record is supplied. The current page labels the CHF 19,990 example as Switzerland. The page is the vendor's own account.

fields.account: The metadata of Vyntra's “Fraud Cases” page dates it to 4 April 2022. The cases themselves are undated. On the page, Vyntra states that “Our solutions stop the fraud before the money leaves the bank”. It lists about two dozen short case studies at unnamed banks. In one, an account takeover after pharming was stopped before a CHF 19,990 payment. In another, an impersonation led a bank employee to validate a CHF 1,000,000 transaction, which was blocked because the beneficiary was unusual at bank level. Other cases involve voice phishing, fake technical support, impersonation of a chief executive, business email compromise, romance scams and redirected invoices. On the page, Vyntra says that payments of EUR 22,114, EUR 33,170, USD 7,500, GBP 21,000, EUR 125,000, EUR 170,000, USD 100,000, USD 170,000 and USD 850,000 were stopped in these cases. In each, variables of the e-banking payment (beneficiary, country, amount, currency, browser, screen resolution, language) did not match a usual profile. In some cases the profile was the customer's. In others it was the bank's. There are two internal-fraud cases. In one case “fraudsters were arrested while attempting to withdraw USD 500,000 (KSh 58 million) from the second bank's ATMs”. The models had flagged the unusual timing of withdrawals. They had flagged their unusual frequency. NetGuardians, a Swiss company, merged with Belgium's Intix to form Vyntra in June 2025 (FinTech Global, 19 June 2025). “NetGuardians solution” still appears in one entry on the page. On the current page, the CHF 19,990 example is placed in Switzerland. No customer on the page is identified. No bank on the page is identified. The page supplies no dated event, no finding by a regulator and no court record. The page is the vendor's own account. In a separate, undated case study, Vyntra names Sidian Bank in Nairobi as a client from April 2019. In it, Sidian's head of internal audit, Peter Karichu, says that the software flagged rapid ATM withdrawals one weekend in mid-December 2019. He says that the fraudsters were arrested at another bank. Vyntra gives no amount for that case. The Sidian case may or may not be the KSh 58 million case.

record.title: A Yunnan man cancels a transfer of 190,000 yuan to a suspected romance scammer after WeChat Pay's “anti-fraud customer service reminder” interrupts it (reported 14 December 2021)
record.summary: WeChat says that its WeChat Pay anti-fraud reminder put a Yunnan man in touch with customer service. An agent advised him to cancel a 190,000 yuan transfer to a “goddess” whom he had met online.
record.account: On 14 December 2021 WeChat announced that WeChat Pay had launched an “anti-fraud customer service reminder” (IT之家 and ChinaZ, 14 December 2021). ZOL reported it on 16 December 2021. When a payment is flagged as a risky transaction, the screen shows an “answer the reminder” button. The system connects automatically. Tencent Cloud Zhifu then provides online customer service to help judge the risk. The Yunnan story is WeChat's own example in that announcement. ChinaZ reports that a man in Yunnan had met a woman on a video platform. Within a week she asked to borrow 190,000 yuan for medical treatment. As he initiated the transfer, a WeChat Pay voice reminder appeared. In the announcement relayed by IT之家, WeChat says that the man received a call from WeChat Pay customer service while making the transfer. Customer service judged from experience that this looked like a dating scam. It explained the pattern to him. It advised him to cancel. He avoided a loss of 190,000 yuan. In September 2022 Xinhua reported that the reminder was still part of WeChat Pay's risk warnings.

record.brief: On 14 December 2021 WeChat announced an “anti-fraud customer service reminder” for WeChat Pay. WeChat's example was a man in Yunnan, identified only by his surname.[1] ChinaZ reported that the man had met a woman on a video platform. Within a week she asked to borrow 190,000 yuan for medical treatment. As he began the transfer, a voice reminder from WeChat Pay appeared. He then received a call from its customer service. The agent on the call judged from experience that this looked like a dating scam and advised him to cancel.[2] He canceled the payment. The automated step in these accounts is the flagging of a risky transaction. Neither WeChat nor ChinaZ says how this transfer was flagged or whether any model was involved. WeChat and ChinaZ credit the agent's advice with his decision to cancel. No confirmation from the police or a bank is reported. No date is given for the transfer. In September 2022 Xinhua listed the reminder among WeChat Pay's risk warnings. It gave no figures on the reminder's effect.[3]

data.retained_case_account: According to WeChat (ChinaZ, 14 December 2021; ZOL, 16 December 2021), WeChat Pay launched an “anti-fraud customer service reminder”. When a payment is flagged as a risky transaction, the screen shows an “answer the reminder” button and the system connects automatically. Tencent Cloud Zhifu then provides online customer service to help judge the risk. ChinaZ reports that a man in Yunnan had met a woman on a video platform. Within a week she asked to borrow 190,000 yuan for medical treatment. As he initiated the transfer, a WeChat Pay voice reminder appeared. The customer service, judging from experience that this looked like a dating scam, explained the pattern and advised him to cancel. He avoided a loss of 190,000 yuan. The Monitor bundles this with Shanghai police figures for 2021 (115,000 scam calls blocked daily; 510 million yuan directly recovered). Xinmin attributes those to police, the communications administration and carriers without naming AI.

fields.summary: WeChat says that its WeChat Pay anti-fraud reminder put a Yunnan man in touch with customer service. An agent advised him to cancel a 190,000 yuan transfer to a “goddess” whom he had met online.
fields.account: On 14 December 2021 WeChat announced that WeChat Pay had launched an “anti-fraud customer service reminder” (IT之家 and ChinaZ, 14 December 2021). ZOL reported it on 16 December 2021. When a payment is flagged as a risky transaction, the screen shows an “answer the reminder” button. The system connects automatically. Tencent Cloud Zhifu then provides online customer service to help judge the risk. The Yunnan story is WeChat's own example in that announcement. ChinaZ reports that a man in Yunnan had met a woman on a video platform. Within a week she asked to borrow 190,000 yuan for medical treatment. As he initiated the transfer, a WeChat Pay voice reminder appeared. In the announcement relayed by IT之家, WeChat says that the man received a call from WeChat Pay customer service while making the transfer. Customer service judged from experience that this looked like a dating scam. It explained the pattern to him. It advised him to cancel. He avoided a loss of 190,000 yuan. In September 2022 Xinhua reported that the reminder was still part of WeChat Pay's risk warnings.

record.title: UNEP MARS alert led to repair of a decades-old methane source at Hassi Messaoud, Algeria, verified by satellite from 15 October 2024
record.summary: An alert from the UN Environment Programme's Methane Alert and Response System led an Algerian operator to fix an unlit flare at Hassi Messaoud. Satellites show no emissions since 15 October 2024.
record.account: UNEP's Methane Alert and Response System (MARS) combines data from more than 30 satellite instruments with expert analysis. It uses AI models. In its document on Hassi Messaoud, Algeria, UNEP records a Landsat 5 detection of methane at the site dated 1 July 1987. It counts 113 plumes since 1987. It estimates total emissions at 960,000 tonnes. In its public catalog, Carbon Mapper independently records that NASA's EMIT instrument saw methane plumes at the site on 17 dates from 17 August 2022 to 29 September 2024. The plumes carried about 2,100 to 3,600 kilograms per hour. UNEP attributes the emissions to an unlit flare caused by a passing valve on the flare line. The operator corrected the valve. It restored normal operations. In October 2024 UNEP's International Methane Emissions Observatory confirmed mitigation of the source through MARS. UNEP states that no further emissions have been detected at the location since 15 October 2024. Carbon Mapper lists no later plume at that point. UNEP issued the document in November 2024, according to the repository record. The PDF's last-updated field reads 15 October 2024. UN News reported on 23 July 2026 that the Algerian alert led to the repair of a leak that had persisted for decades. On 31 August 2026 The Guardian reported that the leak, which had run for almost 40 years, was stemmed. The Guardian gave no data of its own on the site.

data.retained_case_account: UNEP's Methane Alert and Response System (MARS) combines data from more than 30 satellite instruments with expert analysis and AI models. It confirmed mitigation of a methane source at Hassi Messaoud, Algeria, in October 2024. UNEP's case document was issued in November 2024 per the repository record. The PDF's last-updated field reads 15 October 2024. It records a Landsat 5 detection dated 1 July 1987. It attributes the emissions to an unlit flare caused by a passing valve on the flare line. The operator corrected the valve and restored normal operations. UNEP states no further emissions have been detected at the location since 15 October 2024. UN News reported on 23 July 2026 that the Algerian alert led to the repair of a leak that had persisted for decades.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: UNEP IMEO both developed and operates MARS (developer and deployer are the same body). UNEP's MARS page describes detection using more than 30 satellite instruments coupled with expertise and advanced AI models. The MARS FAQ says deep learning models monitor high-resolution satellite data for further emissions. The case document's boilerplate says MARS combines 30+ satellite instruments with expert analysis and AI models. None of these states which step in this case was AI-driven. The repair was carried out by the operator. The two case-document items are treated as a public body's official reports rather than vendor material.

fields.account: UNEP's Methane Alert and Response System (MARS) combines data from more than 30 satellite instruments with expert analysis. It uses AI models. In its document on Hassi Messaoud, Algeria, UNEP records a Landsat 5 detection of methane at the site dated 1 July 1987. It counts 113 plumes since 1987. It estimates total emissions at 960,000 tonnes. In its public catalog, Carbon Mapper independently records that NASA's EMIT instrument saw methane plumes at the site on 17 dates from 17 August 2022 to 29 September 2024. The plumes carried about 2,100 to 3,600 kilograms per hour. UNEP attributes the emissions to an unlit flare caused by a passing valve on the flare line. The operator corrected the valve. It restored normal operations. In October 2024 UNEP's International Methane Emissions Observatory confirmed mitigation of the source through MARS. UNEP states that no further emissions have been detected at the location since 15 October 2024. Carbon Mapper lists no later plume at that point. UNEP issued the document in November 2024, according to the repository record. The PDF's last-updated field reads 15 October 2024. UN News reported on 23 July 2026 that the Algerian alert led to the repair of a leak that had persisted for decades. On 31 August 2026 The Guardian reported that the leak, which had run for almost 40 years, was stemmed. The Guardian gave no data of its own on the site.

fields.summary: An alert from the UN Environment Programme's Methane Alert and Response System led an Algerian operator to fix an unlit flare at Hassi Messaoud. Satellites show no emissions since 15 October 2024.
fields.account: UNEP's Methane Alert and Response System (MARS) combines data from more than 30 satellite instruments with expert analysis. It uses AI models. In its document on Hassi Messaoud, Algeria, UNEP records a Landsat 5 detection of methane at the site dated 1 July 1987. It counts 113 plumes since 1987. It estimates total emissions at 960,000 tonnes. In its public catalog, Carbon Mapper independently records that NASA's EMIT instrument saw methane plumes at the site on 17 dates from 17 August 2022 to 29 September 2024. The plumes carried about 2,100 to 3,600 kilograms per hour. UNEP attributes the emissions to an unlit flare caused by a passing valve on the flare line. The operator corrected the valve. It restored normal operations. In October 2024 UNEP's International Methane Emissions Observatory confirmed mitigation of the source through MARS. UNEP states that no further emissions have been detected at the location since 15 October 2024. Carbon Mapper lists no later plume at that point. UNEP issued the document in November 2024, according to the repository record. The PDF's last-updated field reads 15 October 2024. UN News reported on 23 July 2026 that the Algerian alert led to the repair of a leak that had persisted for decades. On 31 August 2026 The Guardian reported that the leak, which had run for almost 40 years, was stemmed. The Guardian gave no data of its own on the site.

record.title: ALERTCalifornia's AI cameras may have helped crews hold Kern County's Trotter Fire to 52 acres through rapid detection (August 2023)
record.summary: Microsoft, which funds ALERTCalifornia, says that the network's AI cameras helped crews hold Kern County's Trotter Fire to 52 acres in August 2023 by early detection. The software has not been named.
record.account: On 14 August 2023 KBAK (Bakersfield) reported a mandatory evacuation for Skyline Drive between Saddleback Drive and Cumberland Road in Bear Valley Springs. It gave an estimated 40 acres, forward progress stopped by 2:17 p.m. and the evacuation lifted by 3:12 p.m. The Kern County Fire Department said that the fire “was started by an electrical strike”. KBAK illustrated its report with photos credited to ALERTCalifornia. In the text, KBAK does not say how the fire was first reported. KGET blamed lightning in a headline the same day. In the same headline, KGET said that no homes were damaged. Cal Fire's archived incident record lists the Trotter Fire at Trotter Drive and Skyline Drive, west of Tehachapi, Kern County. It lists the Kern County Fire Department as the agency in charge. The fire was therefore not a Cal Fire incident. The record gives the start as 11:10 a.m. on 14 August 2023, which is 18:10 in Coordinated Universal Time. The fire burned 52 acres. In universal time the record dates its 100% containment to 17 August 2023. It gives the same date for its extinguishment. In local time it gives containment as 5:00 p.m. on 16 August 2023. The record lists the cause as under investigation. It holds nothing on how the fire was detected. It does not show how the fire was reported. Microsoft made a $5 million contribution to ALERTCalifornia that included a $3 million Azure grant, which ALERTCalifornia announced on 3 February 2026. Since February 2026 Microsoft has worked with ALERTCalifornia's research team through the Microsoft AI for Good Lab. In Microsoft's “Unlocked” feature “The first five minutes” (27 August 2026), Bruna Mori writes that in 2023 ALERTCalifornia's cameras with AI helped crews rapidly detect the fire. She writes that they then helped the crews contain the Trotter Fire at 52 acres. ALERTCalifornia founder Neal Driscoll estimates that without AI-powered imaging the fire may have spread to nearly 4,000 acres. Mori quotes Zachary Wells, deputy chief of the Kern County Fire Department. He holds a second post as deputy director of operations at ALERTCalifornia. The claim of AI detection is found only in Microsoft and ALERTCalifornia material. Fire agencies, regulators and independent news outlets have not mentioned AI detection in their accounts of the fire. None of them has said which agency received the alert. None has said when the alert came relative to 911 calls.

fields.account: On 14 August 2023 KBAK (Bakersfield) reported a mandatory evacuation for Skyline Drive between Saddleback Drive and Cumberland Road in Bear Valley Springs. It gave an estimated 40 acres, forward progress stopped by 2:17 p.m. and the evacuation lifted by 3:12 p.m. The Kern County Fire Department said that the fire “was started by an electrical strike”. KBAK illustrated its report with photos credited to ALERTCalifornia. In the text, KBAK does not say how the fire was first reported. KGET blamed lightning in a headline the same day. In the same headline, KGET said that no homes were damaged. Cal Fire's archived incident record lists the Trotter Fire at Trotter Drive and Skyline Drive, west of Tehachapi, Kern County. It lists the Kern County Fire Department as the agency in charge. The fire was therefore not a Cal Fire incident. The record gives the start as 11:10 a.m. on 14 August 2023, which is 18:10 in Coordinated Universal Time. The fire burned 52 acres. In universal time the record dates its 100% containment to 17 August 2023. It gives the same date for its extinguishment. In local time it gives containment as 5:00 p.m. on 16 August 2023. The record lists the cause as under investigation. It holds nothing on how the fire was detected. It does not show how the fire was reported. Microsoft made a $5 million contribution to ALERTCalifornia that included a $3 million Azure grant, which ALERTCalifornia announced on 3 February 2026. Since February 2026 Microsoft has worked with ALERTCalifornia's research team through the Microsoft AI for Good Lab. In Microsoft's “Unlocked” feature “The first five minutes” (27 August 2026), Bruna Mori writes that in 2023 ALERTCalifornia's cameras with AI helped crews rapidly detect the fire. She writes that they then helped the crews contain the Trotter Fire at 52 acres. ALERTCalifornia founder Neal Driscoll estimates that without AI-powered imaging the fire may have spread to nearly 4,000 acres. Mori quotes Zachary Wells, deputy chief of the Kern County Fire Department. He holds a second post as deputy director of operations at ALERTCalifornia. The claim of AI detection is found only in Microsoft and ALERTCalifornia material. Fire agencies, regulators and independent news outlets have not mentioned AI detection in their accounts of the fire. None of them has said which agency received the alert. None has said when the alert came relative to 911 calls.

record.title: West Yorkshire Police's first deployment of live facial recognition in Huddersfield leads to three arrests over three days, including a domestic stalking suspect. It also leads to six Sexual Harm Prevention Order checks
record.summary: West Yorkshire Police reported three arrests and six Sexual Harm Prevention Order checks after NEC NeoFace live facial recognition issued nine alerts in Huddersfield on 12 to 14 August 2026.
record.account: The National Physical Laboratory tested NEC NeoFace V4 for the Metropolitan Police and South Wales Police in 2022. It reported in March 2023. It found that at a face-match threshold of 0.64 the system produced no false positives, with a true recognition rate of 79 percent. West Yorkshire Police records the same threshold of 0.64 for its deployments. The force identifies NEC NeoFace as the matching system. It states that trained officers review alerts before intervention. West Yorkshire Police used live facial recognition in Huddersfield from 12 to 14 August 2026. The force reported the arrests of three people: a domestic stalking suspect, a person wanted on a warrant and a shoplifting suspect. It reported six Sexual Harm Prevention Order checks. Its deployment register records five alerts on 12 August. It records two on each following day. All nine were recorded as confirmed true alerts. The estimated numbers of faces seen were 5,824, 2,951 and 4,100, which total 12,875. These figures come from the force's own operational records. No independent study of these deployments has been found. The absence of recorded false alerts does not establish that the system missed no matches. The reported results do not establish a conviction. They do not establish a specific harm that was prevented. The force's register shows that the vans returned to Huddersfield town center on 8, 9 and 10 September 2026, with 16 alerts, all confirmed true. On a further return on 10 October 2026 they recorded no alerts.

data.retained_case_account: West Yorkshire Police used live facial recognition in Huddersfield on August 12–14, 2026. The force reported three arrests, involving a domestic stalking suspect, a person wanted on a warrant, and a shoplifting suspect, along with six Sexual Harm Prevention Order checks. Its deployment register records five alerts on August 12 and two on each subsequent day. All nine were recorded as confirmed true alerts. The estimated numbers of faces seen were 5,824, 2,951, and 4,100, totaling 12,875. These are the force’s operational records, not an independent accuracy study. Zero recorded false alerts does not establish that there were no missed matches. The force identifies NEC NeoFace as the matching system and states that trained officers review alerts before intervention. The reported arrests and checks do not establish a conviction or a specific harm that was prevented.

fields.account: The National Physical Laboratory tested NEC NeoFace V4 for the Metropolitan Police and South Wales Police in 2022. It reported in March 2023. It found that at a face-match threshold of 0.64 the system produced no false positives, with a true recognition rate of 79 percent. West Yorkshire Police records the same threshold of 0.64 for its deployments. The force identifies NEC NeoFace as the matching system. It states that trained officers review alerts before intervention. West Yorkshire Police used live facial recognition in Huddersfield from 12 to 14 August 2026. The force reported the arrests of three people: a domestic stalking suspect, a person wanted on a warrant and a shoplifting suspect. It reported six Sexual Harm Prevention Order checks. Its deployment register records five alerts on 12 August. It records two on each following day. All nine were recorded as confirmed true alerts. The estimated numbers of faces seen were 5,824, 2,951 and 4,100, which total 12,875. These figures come from the force's own operational records. No independent study of these deployments has been found. The absence of recorded false alerts does not establish that the system missed no matches. The reported results do not establish a conviction. They do not establish a specific harm that was prevented. The force's register shows that the vans returned to Huddersfield town center on 8, 9 and 10 September 2026, with 16 alerts, all confirmed true. On a further return on 10 October 2026 they recorded no alerts.

record.title: Southern Water's sewer monitors flag a forming fatberg in Rowner, Gosport, so a crew clears it before any spill into the River Alver
record.summary: Southern Water's machine-learning sewer monitors flagged a forming fatberg in Rowner, Gosport. A crew cleared it before any overflow into the River Alver.
record.account: Southern Water runs around 34,000 sewer level monitors with machine learning. Its proactive operations control manager Daniel McElhinney says that the system learns the normal behavior of sewers. He says that it can tell a forming blockage from daily rushes. He says that it can tell one from rain. Shortly before 22 April 2026 the sensors detected an abnormal flow in Rowner, Gosport. They alerted the control room. A crew cleared the sewer with a jet. They found a fatberg of wet wipes and other unflushable items. The company said that, left unchecked, the sewer could have overflowed from a manhole into a surface water drain leading to the River Alver. The blockage was reported on 22 April 2026. A second blockage that the sensors found, at Warlands Lane, Shalfleet, Isle of Wight, was reported on 23 April. BBC Future reported on 12 May 2026 that the sensors use radar to measure sewer levels. It reported that a model compares them with rainfall and weather data. The BBC reported that Southern Water had cleared 700 blockages with AI so far that year. It noted that the company still had more than 15,500 sewage spills in 2025, a drop of 47 percent from 2024. The BBC did not mention the blockage at Rowner. In October 2026 the same sensor network flagged a blockage of wet wipes before it overflowed into the Lymington River in the New Forest, by the company's account.
record.purpose: Southern Water installed the monitors and the anomaly model to spot blockages and leaks forming in sewers, so that crews can clear them before they cause pollution or flooding.

ratings.reason: The company says that a sewage overflow into the River Alver was averted. The Andover Advertiser says that the river is home to herons, water voles and kingfishers. No source shows what would have happened without the alert, and no pollution occurred. This is a specific avoided harm of unmeasured size.

Southern Water cleared one blockage before it became a pollution incident or a customer flooding. The company says that blocked sewers are the leading cause of its pollution incidents. This is one of the more than 4,000 interventions that it reports in a year.

data.retained_case_account: Southern Water runs around 34,000 sewer level monitors with machine learning. Its proactive operations control manager Daniel McElhinney says the system learns the normal behavior of sewers. He says it can tell a forming blockage from daily rushes or rain. Shortly before 22 April 2026 the sensors detected an abnormal flow in Rowner, Gosport, and alerted the control room. A crew jetted the sewer and found a fatberg of wet wipes and other unflushable items. The company said that, left unchecked, the sewer could have overflowed from a manhole into a surface water drain leading to the River Alver. The case was reported on 22 April 2026. A second flagged blockage at Warlands Lane, Shalfleet, Isle of Wight, was reported on 23 April.

fields.account: Southern Water runs around 34,000 sewer level monitors with machine learning. Its proactive operations control manager Daniel McElhinney says that the system learns the normal behavior of sewers. He says that it can tell a forming blockage from daily rushes. details.value: South Wales Police and Gwent Police brought in the app for people who cannot or will not give their details. It confirms the identity of a person whom an officer suspects to be missing, at risk or wanted.

details.label: Contribution of the AI
details.value: The app compared a photograph taken on a police phone with a reference database and returned the match that identified the man. Officers then confirmed the warrant and detained him. The National Physical Laboratory tested the NEC NeoFace V4 algorithm used for OIFR in 2022, for the Metropolitan Police and South Wales Police. It found that the algorithm returned the correct match first for every probe image of a person in the database. record.summary: South Wales Police's Operator Initiated Facial Recognition phone app matched a man in Cardiff to a European arrest warrant issued in Poland in 2012. He was remanded in custody (July 2025).
record.account: South Wales Police and Gwent Police are the first UK forces with the Operator Initiated Facial Recognition (OIFR) app. It lets an officer photograph a person on a police phone. The officer can then compare the image with a reference database. It is for when a person will not give true details. In 2022 the National Physical Laboratory tested the NEC NeoFace V4 algorithm that the app uses, under contract to the Metropolitan Police and South Wales Police. The app launched in December 2024. In one use, an officer in Cardiff identified a 38-year-old man wanted on a European arrest warrant since 2012. The warrant was for drug dealing in Poland. It covered an armed assault there on a police officer. He was remanded in custody to Westminster magistrates' court (Wales Online, 14 July 2025). The arrest date is not given. The forces report 50 searches in South Wales, which produced 10 arrests. They report six uses in Gwent, with three matches. One arrest followed. They cite the National Physical Laboratory testing, in which the correct match came top for people in the database (Wales Online). The accuracy claim rests on those 2022 tests. More than 500 officers had been trained by July 2025 (Emergency Services Times, 15 July 2025). In an audit report of August 2025, the Information Commissioner's Office said that it had observed the app at the two forces. It called the app a pilot in its infancy. In August 2026 the Information Commissioner's Office still described the app as a pilot in a limited number of forces. The extradition proceedings have no reported outcome.

fields.summary: South Wales Police's Operator Initiated Facial Recognition phone app matched a man in Cardiff to a European arrest warrant issued in Poland in 2012. He was remanded in custody (July 2025).
fields.account: South Wales Police and Gwent Police are the first UK forces with the Operator Initiated Facial Recognition (OIFR) app. It lets an officer photograph a person on a police phone. The officer can then compare the image with a reference database. It is for when a person will not give true details. In 2022 the National Physical Laboratory tested the NEC NeoFace V4 algorithm that the app uses, under contract to the Metropolitan Police and South Wales Police. The app launched in December 2024. In one use, an officer in Cardiff identified a 38-year-old man wanted on a European arrest warrant since 2012. The warrant was for drug dealing in Poland. It covered an armed assault there on a police officer. He was remanded in custody to Westminster magistrates' court (Wales Online, 14 July 2025). The arrest date is not given. The forces report 50 searches in South Wales, which produced 10 arrests. They report six uses in Gwent, with three matches. One arrest followed. They cite the National Physical Laboratory testing, in which the correct match came top for people in the database (Wales Online). The accuracy claim rests on those 2022 tests. More than 500 officers had been trained by July 2025 (Emergency Services Times, 15 July 2025). In an audit report of August 2025, the Information Commissioner's Office said that it had observed the app at the two forces. It called the app a pilot in its infancy. In August 2026 the Information Commissioner's Office still described the app as a pilot in a limited number of forces. The extradition proceedings have no reported outcome.

record.title: The 1st Military Police Battalion arrests a woman wanted for drug trafficking after Vigia Mais MT facial recognition identifies her in downtown Cuiabá
record.summary: Mato Grosso's security secretariat reports that Vigia Mais MT facial recognition matched a woman wanted for drug trafficking in central Cuiabá on 12 July 2025. Police arrested her.
record.account: On 19 June 2024 the 9th Criminal Court Specialized in Drug Offenses issued a warrant for a woman for drug trafficking. On Saturday 12 July 2025 the video-monitoring system of Mato Grosso's State Secretariat of Public Security (Sesp) helped arrest her in downtown Cuiabá. It acted through the Vigia Mais MT program. Cameras in the city center identified her by facial recognition. After the system confirmed her identity, the monitoring center of the Integrated Public Security Operations Center (Ciosp) tracked her movements in real time. The center passed them to a team of the 1st Military Police Battalion, which made the approach. She was taken to a Civil Judicial Police unit. On 14 July 2025 Maria Klara Duque wrote a release about the arrest for the secretariat. Diário de Cuiabá and O Documento carried the text of that release on 14 July. CliqueF5 carried it on 15 July 2025. Diário de Cuiabá and CliqueF5 credit it to the secretariat. The secretariat adds that from April to July 2025 about 60 fugitives were located by state security forces. They were then arrested. By its account, the Vigia Mais MT program then covered 128 municipalities.

fields.account: On 19 June 2024 the 9th Criminal Court Specialized in Drug Offenses issued a warrant for a woman for drug trafficking. On Saturday 12 July 2025 the video-monitoring system of Mato Grosso's State Secretariat of Public Security (Sesp) helped arrest her in downtown Cuiabá. It acted through the Vigia Mais MT program. Cameras in the city center identified her by facial recognition. After the system confirmed her identity, the monitoring center of the Integrated Public Security Operations Center (Ciosp) tracked her movements in real time. The center passed them to a team of the 1st Military Police Battalion, which made the approach. She was taken to a Civil Judicial Police unit. On 14 July 2025 Maria Klara Duque wrote a release about the arrest for the secretariat. Diário de Cuiabá and O Documento carried the text of that release on 14 July. CliqueF5 carried it on 15 July 2025. Diário de Cuiabá and CliqueF5 credit it to the secretariat. The secretariat adds that from April to July 2025 about 60 fugitives were located by state security forces. They were then arrested. By its account, the Vigia Mais MT program then covered 128 municipalities.

record.title: From clues in threat intelligence, Google's Big Sleep may have isolated the SQLite flaw CVE-2025-6965, which SQLite fixed in version 3.50.2 before any reported exploitation
record.summary: Google says that its Big Sleep agent isolated SQLite flaw CVE-2025-6965 from signs that attackers were preparing to exploit an unknown flaw. SQLite fixed it in version 3.50.2 on 28 June 2025.
record.account: The SQLite developers state that the flaw was fixed on 27 June 2025. They state that it needs an attacker who can inject arbitrary SQL into an application. The SQLite 3.50.2 release carrying the fix is dated 28 June 2025. SQLite's release log lists the corresponding fix. The Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures record for the flaw, CVE-2025-6965, was published on 15 July 2025. In the CVE record, which it assigned, Google credits Vlad Stolyarov of Google's Threat Analysis Group with assistance from Google Big Sleep. In a post of the same day, Google says that, based on intelligence from Google Threat Intelligence, the Big Sleep agent discovered an SQLite vulnerability known only to threat actors. Google says that it was at risk of being exploited. A Google spokesperson told The Record that its threat intelligence group found artifacts indicating that a zero-day was being staged but could not identify the vulnerability. The spokesperson said that Big Sleep was used to isolate it. Google declined to name the actors. It declined to describe the indicators. The sources hold no independent confirmation that exploitation was imminent. The claim rests on Google. On 11 August 2025 the Big Sleep team reported a curl vulnerability, later published as CVE-2025-9086, which curl's maintainer confirmed. As of 28 October 2026 the CVE is not in the catalog of known exploited vulnerabilities kept by the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency.

record.title: Large models working with small models for safety at ports
record.summary: ZTE reports that its Nebula vision system at Taicang Port eliminated 92% of false fire alarms. It detected unsafe behavior. No injuries prevented have been reported.
record.account: ZTE reports that it deployed its Nebula vision system at Taicang Port. An edge detector flags possible fire. It flags possible smoke. A larger cloud vision model checks the context to reject false positives. ZTE reports that the system eliminated 92% of false fire alarms. It reports that the system detected unsafe behavior. ZTE reports that it tested the system at Taicang Port on 65 videos. Of these, 30 had smoke. The other 35 did not. It states that accuracy exceeded 90%. It states that the false alarm rate stayed below 5%. These gains rest on ZTE's own reports. Prevented injuries remain unestablished.

record.summary: Huawei reports that operations aided by a telecom foundation model, a transformer with 38 billion parameters, lowered packet loss and delay at MTN. It does not isolate the model's share.
record.account: In the ITU entry, current to June 2025, Huawei describes a telecom foundation model, a transformer with 38 billion parameters. The model supports diagnosis, queries in natural language and optimization recommendations. It works within a system that uses conventional network maps. The system's routing methods are conventional. The entry lists a Huawei employee as a contact. It lists Huawei as the only partner. Huawei states that with the AI-based system “the packet loss rate and network delay are significantly reduced” at MTN. It does not separate the contribution of the model. It gives no effect size. The deployment setting is unclear, because Huawei describes an MTN deployment alongside an internal testbed. On 13 November 2025 TechAfrica News relayed a joint announcement in which Huawei and MTN said that TM Forum had certified MTN South Africa's IP network at autonomous network Level 4. The assessment covered the handling of congestion along with path interruption. The network received the highest grade in every dimension of the standard. The network runs Huawei's network digital map with its network agent. The two companies gave no figures for packet loss. They gave no figures for delay.

details.value: In its own account, Skylight describes a contribution in two stages. A rule-based Speed Range Event flagged the vessel at under 6 knots inside an area of interest. A Fishing Event from its machine-learning model, which detects longlining, trawling and squid jigging, reinforced the suspicion 40 minutes later. PNA analysts then redirected a coastguard vessel. Skylight quotes a retired PNA captain who says that Skylight contributed directly to the decision. So this is the maker's account, with the deployer's officers quoted inside it. Agenda Malvinas, an independent outlet citing Pescare and official information, credits the detection to the PNA's Sistema Guardacostas and does not name Skylight or AI. So the credit to the AI output is not independently confirmed.

record.title: On 5 January 2025, Skylight alerts may have led Argentina's Prefectura Naval to stop the Vanuatu-flagged XINRUN 579, which may have paid a fine
record.summary: Skylight says that its speed alert led Argentina's coast guard to intercept a trawler on 5 January 2025. Its machine-learning fishing alert did too. Skylight also says that the vessel paid a fine.
record.account: On Sunday 5 January 2025 the Prefectura Naval Argentina (PNA), Argentina's coast guard, detected the Vanuatu-flagged trawler XinRun 579. It was in Argentina's exclusive economic zone off Caleta Olivia, Santa Cruz, sailing at under 6 knots. Under local rules, that speed is a sign of trawling. The coast guard vessel GC-25 Azopardo intercepted it. The captain was formally notified of an infraction under Law 24.922, which opened administrative proceedings (Agenda Malvinas, 8 January 2025, citing official information). Agenda Malvinas credits the detection to the PNA's Sistema Guardacostas. It does not mention Skylight. AI does not appear in its account. On 3 March 2025 NVIDIA wrote in a Developer blog post that the coast guard interdicted the vessel after Skylight alerted it. NVIDIA wrote that the coast guard later fined the vessel. Skylight, the free AI maritime-monitoring platform of the Allen Institute for AI, published its own account on 31 March 2025. A rule-based Speed Range Event first alerted the authorities. A Fishing Event alert from its machine-learning model came 40 minutes later. PNA analysts redirected a nearby coast guard vessel. Skylight says that the interception led to Argentina's first international electronic fine using AI-powered evidence. It says that the vessel paid the fine along with the operational costs. Skylight quotes a retired PNA captain who coordinates EICEMAR, an interdisciplinary team for the control of maritime spaces and their resources. It quotes the lead of the PNA's geographic information systems division. Both credit Skylight. The PNA release that Skylight links to cannot be found online. No archived copy has been found.

data.retained_case_account: On Sunday 5 January 2025 the Prefectura Naval Argentina (PNA) detected the Vanuatu-flagged trawler XinRun 579. It was in Argentina's exclusive economic zone off Caleta Olivia, Santa Cruz, sailing at under 6 knots. Local rules treat that as indicating trawling. Coastguard vessel GC-25 Azopardo intercepted it. The captain was formally notified of an infraction under Law 24.922, opening administrative proceedings (Agenda Malvinas, 8 January 2025, citing official information). Skylight, the free AI maritime-monitoring platform of the Allen Institute for AI, published its own account on 31 March 2025. A rule-based Speed Range Event first alerted the authorities. A Fishing Event alert from its machine-learning model came 40 minutes later. PNA analysts redirected a nearby coastguard vessel. It led to Argentina's first international electronic fine using AI-powered evidence, with the fine and operational costs paid. It quotes the EICEMAR coordinator and the PNA GIS division lead crediting Skylight. The independent news report attributes the detection to the PNA's Sistema Guardacostas and does not mention Skylight or AI. The PNA release Skylight links to is not found live or in the Internet Archive. An NVIDIA Developer blog (3 March 2025) also reports the interdiction and fine.

This is the maker's account, with the deployer's officers quoted inside it. The independent report (Agenda Malvinas, citing Pescare and official information) attributes the detection to the PNA's Sistema Guardacostas and does not name Skylight or AI. chronology_source.title: Prefectura detectó un buque asiático pescando ilegalmente en aguas argentinas

display.answer: Skylight's own account of 31 March 2025 is the source of the AI's part and of the paid fine. It quotes two members of the Argentine coast guard. The NVIDIA Developer blog post of 3 March 2025 comes from a technology partner of Skylight. Agenda Malvinas cites Pescare and official information in its report of 8 January 2025 and does not mention Skylight. In its impact report for June 2025 to May 2026, Skylight gives aggregated results for its partners and does not attribute them to single cases.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: Skylight says that its speed alert led Argentina's coast guard to intercept a trawler on 5 January 2025. Its machine-learning fishing alert did too. Skylight also says that the vessel paid a fine.
fields.account: On Sunday 5 January 2025 the Prefectura Naval Argentina (PNA), Argentina's coast guard, detected the Vanuatu-flagged trawler XinRun 579. It was in Argentina's exclusive economic zone off Caleta Olivia, Santa Cruz, sailing at under 6 knots. Under local rules, that speed is a sign of trawling. The coast guard vessel GC-25 Azopardo intercepted it. The captain was formally notified of an infraction under Law 24.922, which opened administrative proceedings (Agenda Malvinas, 8 January 2025, citing official information). Agenda Malvinas credits the detection to the PNA's Sistema Guardacostas. It does not mention Skylight. AI does not appear in its account. On 3 March 2025 NVIDIA wrote in a Developer blog post that the coast guard interdicted the vessel after Skylight alerted it. NVIDIA wrote that the coast guard later fined the vessel. Skylight, the free AI maritime-monitoring platform of the Allen Institute for AI, published its own account on 31 March 2025. A rule-based Speed Range Event first alerted the authorities. A Fishing Event alert from its machine-learning model came 40 minutes later. PNA analysts redirected a nearby coast guard vessel. Skylight says that the interception led to Argentina's first international electronic fine using AI-powered evidence. It says that the vessel paid the fine along with the operational costs. Skylight quotes a retired PNA captain who coordinates EICEMAR, an interdisciplinary team for the control of maritime spaces and their resources. It quotes the lead of the PNA's geographic information systems division. Both credit Skylight. The PNA release that Skylight links to cannot be found online. No archived copy has been found.

record.title: Code Intelligence's Spark agent found a heap use-after-free in wolfSSL's pem_read_bio_key() during its beta test. WolfSSL merged a fix within days. It shipped the fix in 5.7.6
record.summary: Code Intelligence's Spark is an AI agent that runs fuzz tests that it writes. In late October 2024 it found a heap use-after-free in wolfSSL. wolfSSL shipped the fix in 5.7.6 on 31 December 2024.
record.account: Spark is the AI test agent in Code Intelligence GmbH's CI Fuzz product. In its final beta test in late October 2024, the vendor ran it on wolfSSL, an open-source cryptography library for embedded devices. The library serves devices on the Internet of Things. By the vendor's account, after one command the agent chose the target. It generated a fuzz test. It ran the test. It exposed a heap use-after-free in pem_read_bio_key(). There a BIO write-back could reallocate a buffer that a pointer still referenced. The vendor reported it to wolfSSL, which merged a fix in pull request 8139 on 1 November 2024. The fix shipped in release 5.7.6 on 31 December 2024. The maintainers credit “Peter” in the release notes. On 3 January 2025 the vendor's engineer Peter Samarin described the find on the company blog.

fields.account: Spark is the AI test agent in Code Intelligence GmbH's CI Fuzz product. In its final beta test in late October 2024, the vendor ran it on wolfSSL, an open-source cryptography library for embedded devices. The library serves devices on the Internet of Things. By the vendor's account, after one command the agent chose the target. It generated a fuzz test. It ran the test. It exposed a heap use-after-free in pem_read_bio_key(). There a BIO write-back could reallocate a buffer that a pointer still referenced. The vendor reported it to wolfSSL, which merged a fix in pull request 8139 on 1 November 2024. The fix shipped in release 5.7.6 on 31 December 2024. The maintainers credit “Peter” in the release notes. On 3 January 2025 the vendor's engineer Peter Samarin described the find on the company blog.

ratings.reason: wolfSSL received a reproducible report of a heap use-after-free in a path that parses private keys. It merged the fix within days, in pull request 8139 on 1 November 2024, and shipped it in 5.7.6 on 31 December 2024. The maintainers listed it among bug fixes, and the release's Vulnerabilities section does not include it. wolfSSL lists no Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures identifier for it on its page of vulnerabilities. The vendor itself says that the exploit conditions “don't seem easy to meet”, so the benefit is material and bounded.

record.title: Kunshan police “AI police” models flag a mobile gambling ring at Zhouzhuang, 20-plus arrested on 10 September 2024. They trace a telecom fraud's card transfers to freeze 500,000 yuan within 10 minutes
record.summary: Kunshan police say that their “AI police” models found a mobile gambling ring that police broke up on 10 September 2024. The models traced a telecom fraud. 500,000 yuan was frozen within 10 minutes.
record.account: The “Kunpeng Squad”, 35 officers assembled in May 2024, built the “AI police” models for the Kunshan Public Security Bureau in Jiangsu. On 10 September 2024, the bureau broke up a gang running a mobile open-air casino in Zhouzhuang town. It arrested over 20 suspects. Modern Express reported that the “AI police” had found the ring (NetEase reprint, 6 October 2024). These are models that detect outdoor gambling from behavioral patterns in bulk data. In a telecom fraud handled by the Lujia police station, a victim lost 980,000 yuan. Suzhou Daily reports that the fraud case came earlier in 2024. The models traced three tiers of card transfers and froze 500,000 yuan within 10 minutes. They identified 87 suspect accounts within 8 hours. Nine suspects were arrested on the third day with 200,000 yuan recovered (Suzhou Daily via suzhou.gov.cn, 7 October 2024). The police say that the same work would once have taken five or six officers two weeks before the first arrests. The squad reports over 220 models. It reports 609 fraud cases solved over six months. It reports 32.47 million yuan recovered in the same period (both sources). All figures are the police's own.

data.retained_case_account: On 10 September 2024, the Kunshan Public Security Bureau in Jiangsu broke up a gang running a mobile open-air casino in Zhouzhuang town. It arrested over 20 suspects. Modern Express reported that the “AI police” had found the ring (NetEase reprint, 6 October 2024). These are models that detect outdoor gambling from behavioral patterns in bulk data. In a telecom fraud handled by the Lujia police station, a victim lost 980,000 yuan. The models traced three tiers of card transfers and froze 500,000 yuan within 10 minutes. They identified 87 suspect accounts within 8 hours. Nine suspects were arrested on the third day with 200,000 yuan recovered (Suzhou Daily via suzhou.gov.cn, 7 October 2024). The models were built by the “Kunpeng Squad”, 35 officers assembled in May 2024. They report over 220 models and, over six months, 609 fraud cases solved and 32.47 million yuan recovered (both sources). All figures are the police's own.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: Both accounts are the police's. They credit the models with flagging the outdoor casino from behavioral features in bulk data and mapping the ring's structure “with one click”. They also traced card-tier fund flows in parallel, so a freeze came within 10 minutes. Officers made the arrests and freeze requests. Deputy criminal-investigation chief He Yongliang describes the gain as 24-hour, parallel rather than serial casework. Neither source separates the models' share from ordinary investigation.

record.title: An agent framework for running networks, in which large models work with small ones
record.summary: China Telecom reports that large AI models working with small ones raised configuration compliance above 95%. They cut anomaly detection from ten minutes to one.
record.account: The China Academy of Information and Communications Technology and the research institutes of China Telecom, China Mobile and China Unicom published a blue book in September 2024. They reported that the Jiangsu branch's configuration audit reached 94% recall for abnormal configurations in production. Its precision was 85%. They name the branch's own operations center as the source of those figures. In a use case that the International Telecommunication Union published on 29 October 2025, China Telecom describes a framework that coordinates large models with small ones for network operations. It reports the same two figures. It reports that compliance of network device configurations improved to over 95%. It reports that anomaly detection fell from 10 minutes to 1 minute, with an average accuracy above 90%. China Telecom reports large savings in staff time. It reports that digital employees cut operations staff by 30%. It makes claims about customer satisfaction. The operational figures show no particular outage prevented. They show no benefit to employees from the staffing changes. No independent evaluation of the figures had appeared by October 2026.

record.title: Austin Energy deploys 13 Pano AI cameras to detect wildfires across its 437-square-mile territory
record.summary: Austin Energy announced on 29 August 2024 that 13 Pano AI cameras for detecting wildfires cover its service territory. It later said that they had located car, house and recycling-center fires.
record.account: The Austin City Council approved Austin Energy's Pano AI wildfire detection program on 5 October 2023. Austin Energy budgeted $500,000 a year for a five-year contract. Austin Energy, the City of Austin's electric utility, announced the full deployment of the Pano AI system on 29 August 2024. The system combines 13 ultra-high-definition 360-degree cameras with artificial intelligence. It adds real-time monitoring across the utility's 437-square-mile service territory. The territory covers most of Travis County and parts of Hays, Bastrop, Williamson and Burnet counties. Once a fire is identified, the system alerts Austin Energy and local fire departments with location data and imagery. The utility says that the system supports decisions such as power shut-offs. In the release, the utility quotes wildfire program manager Chris Vetromile and Austin Fire Department wildfire mitigation officer Justice Jones. It quotes Arvind Satyam of Pano AI. In its Electric System Resiliency Plan of November 2025, the utility lists the Pano AI cameras among the wildfire tools that it uses. In none of its three documents does the utility report a fire that the cameras detected or contained. It told The Daily Texan in September 2024 that the system had located car fires, house fires and a large fire at a recycling center since its launch in March 2024. All three come from Austin Energy, a public body. The 2024 release carries the vendor's statement. No independent report has been found.

record.title: An AI model that forecasts the weather with high precision
record.summary: Alibaba DAMO Academy reports that its Baguan weather model had 57.8% lower regional forecast error on average than ECMWF-IFS, the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts' system.
record.account: Alibaba's news site, Alizila, reported on 6 November 2024 that Baguan forecast a 20% drop in electricity demand in Shandong with 98.1% load-forecast accuracy. Alizila gives no date for the forecast. It gives no measure of grid savings. In a paper posted on 20 May 2025, the makers report a test on the last half of 2023. They compared Baguan with the Integrated Forecasting System of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF-IFS). In that test, Baguan-Regional achieved an average improvement of 57.8% on the main regional variables. They state that the system serves the power sector in an eastern Chinese province. In their submission to the International Telecommunication Union, current as of June 2025, the makers report improvements over ECMWF-IFS on selected forecast variables in regional comparisons. Their global comparisons show improvements. They name State Grid Shandong among the test settings. A version of the paper appeared in the proceedings of the 31st ACM SIGKDD Conference on 3 August 2025. Better forecasting of renewable power is an intended application. The makers aim for better grid operations. Alibaba and State Grid Shandong have quantified no resulting change in any of three measures (dispatch, reliability, emissions).

fields.account: Alibaba's news site, Alizila, reported on 6 November 2024 that Baguan forecast a 20% drop in electricity demand in Shandong with 98.1% load-forecast accuracy. Alizila gives no date for the forecast. It gives no measure of grid savings. In a paper posted on 20 May 2025, the makers report a test on the last half of 2023. They compared Baguan with the Integrated Forecasting System of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF-IFS). In that test, Baguan-Regional achieved an average improvement of 57.8% on the main regional variables. They state that the system serves the power sector in an eastern Chinese province. In their submission to the International Telecommunication Union, current as of June 2025, the makers report improvements over ECMWF-IFS on selected forecast variables in regional comparisons. Their global comparisons show improvements. They name State Grid Shandong among the test settings. A version of the paper appeared in the proceedings of the 31st ACM SIGKDD Conference on 3 August 2025. Better forecasting of renewable power is an intended application. The makers aim for better grid operations. Alibaba and State Grid Shandong have quantified no resulting change in any of three measures (dispatch, reliability, emissions).

record.summary: Hertfordshire County Council reports that the Robotiz3d ARRES Prevent robot, which uses AI to detect road defects, filled a small number of cracks in a public-road pilot.
record.account: Hertfordshire County Council and Robotiz3d trialed the ARRES Prevent robot, which uses AI to detect road defects. The robot fills cracks. The first public-road test took place in Potters Bar on 6 March 2024. The council reports that the pilot repaired a small number of cracks. The partners report that detection accuracy increased from 66% to 100% in testing. In February 2025 the BBC reported that the council had moved the ARRES Eye scanner into a months-long test on a trial route. The BBC gave no results on the durability of the robot's repairs. Long-term repair performance remains unmeasured. Pothole prevention remains unmeasured. Cost savings are unmeasured. Effects on safety are unmeasured.

record.title: An LLM builds a geodatabase of natural hazards from digital mass media
record.summary: HSE University reports that a language-model pipeline turned 8.3 million Russian-language articles into a database of 21,000 unique natural-hazard events.
record.account: HSE University uses a language model to identify reports of natural hazards. The model structures them. It geocodes them. The team registered the database with Rospatent in 2024. In its submission of June 2025, the team reports that the first phase processed eight million articles. It reports that the phase produced 38,000 event entries covering Russia in 2018–2024. The team's 2026 paper counts nearly 49,000 hazard-relevant texts on 21,000 unique events. On its own page, the team reports that the language model filled the database fields with an average accuracy of 0.65 to 0.97. Specialists checked the entries against other public hazard databases. The user version holds 11.7 thousand messages on 8.3 thousand events. The team notes that the database maps where people write about hazards more than where hazards occur. The database exists as a research resource. Transfer to additional users remains prospective. Any resulting benefits for emergency management remain prospective.

record.title: Intelligent Transmission Section Flow Control Agent in Power Systems
record.summary: China Southern Power Grid's AI company reports that its Intelligent Transmission Section Flow Control Agent outperformed human dispatchers in control evaluations on a regional grid.
record.account: China Southern Power Grid Artificial Intelligence Technology Co., Ltd. developed a flow-control agent for power dispatch. Human dispatchers adjust generation by experience, with decisions taken at the scale of minutes. The developer reports that the agent is deployed in the southwestern Chinese regional power grid, where it adjusts generation outputs in real time. It reports that the agent outperformed human dispatchers in full control evaluations. People's Daily reported in September 2025 that its control ability was close to that of human dispatchers. It states that decisions can move to the scale of seconds. Development of the agent continues. This gain is not verified in any source independent of the developer. Energy benefits remain unquantified. Benefits for emissions remain unquantified.

Human dispatchers adjust generation by experience, with decisions taken at the scale of minutes. The developer reports that the agent is deployed in the southwestern Chinese regional power grid, where it adjusts generation outputs in real time. Energy benefits remain unquantified. Benefits for emissions remain unquantified.

evidence.citation: Dai Zhen, 广西电网公司发布断面调控智能体 (Guangxi Power Grid releases a grid-section control agent), China Energy News, 16 June 2025, p. 11. Dai Zhen is China Southern Power Grid's contact for the project. In the article, Dai Zhen writes that the agent went online at the end of 2024 and made the control of grid sections faster and safer.
evidence.title: 广西电网公司发布断面调控智能体
evidence.quote: 该智能体是广西电网公司联合南网数字集团、基于大瓦特-天璇大模型开发的调度运行融合智能体，融合强化学习算法，实现对电网断面状态的秒级感知、智能预测与自主调控。自2024年底上线以来，显著提升了正常态与极端故障场景下的电网断面控制及时性及安全水平。
evidence.quote_translation: The agent is a dispatch-operation integrated agent developed by Guangxi Power Grid Company together with Southern Grid Digital Group, based on the Dawate-Tianxuan large model; it incorporates reinforcement learning algorithms to achieve second-level perception, intelligent prediction and autonomous regulation of grid section states. Since going live at the end of 2024, it has significantly improved the timeliness and safety level of grid section control in both normal-state and extreme-fault scenarios.

evidence.citation: China Energy News, 南方电网AI成果亮相“人工智能向善全球峰会”并获奖 (China Southern Power Grid's AI results win an award at the AI for Good Global Summit), ifeng.com, 14 July 2025. China Energy News relays China Southern Power Grid's own account: The agent won an Innovate for Impact award at the summit.
evidence.title: 南方电网AI成果亮相“人工智能向善全球峰会”并获奖
evidence.quote: 南方电网公司获奖案例“新型电力系统断面控制智能体”，由南方总调、广西电网公司与南网数字集团联合研发并落地实施，可毫秒级完成上千机组策略推演，将传统15分钟推算压缩至秒级，已在省中调调度台上线使用
evidence.quote_translation: China Southern Power Grid's award-winning case, the “New-Type Power System Section Control Agent,” jointly developed and implemented by the Southern Grid General Dispatch, Guangxi Power Grid Company and Southern Grid Digital Group, can complete strategy simulations for more than a thousand generating units at the millisecond level, compressing the traditional 15-minute calculation to seconds, and has gone live at the provincial central dispatch desk

evidence.citation: Wei Lu, Chen Qinrong and Lu Dongqi, 人工智能开启广西电网数智变革新图景 (AI opens a new picture of digital change at Guangxi Power Grid), China Energy News, 22 September 2025, p. 11. The three writers report for Guangxi Power Grid, which built and runs the agent. They write that it had run at the Guangxi dispatch desk for more than eight months and that it controls the grid nearly as well as human dispatchers.
evidence.title: 人工智能开启广西电网数智变革新图景
evidence.quote: 为此，广西电网公司基于南方电网“大瓦特-天璇”电力调度AI大模型和边缘计算集群系统开发了电网断面调控智能体，运用AI大模型强化学习技术，通过百万次训练，实现接近人类调度员调控能力，以应对高比例新能源给电网带来的冲击。 电网断面调控智能体已在广西电网调度台上线使用8个多月，监控范围包括全区600余个厂站、90多个断面
evidence.quote_translation: To this end, Guangxi Power Grid Company developed a grid section regulation agent based on China Southern Power Grid's “Dawate-Tianxuan” power dispatch AI large model and an edge computing cluster system; using AI large-model reinforcement learning technology, through a million training runs, it achieves regulation capability close to that of human dispatchers, in order to cope with the impact that a high share of new energy has on the grid. The grid section regulation agent has been in use at the Guangxi Power Grid dispatch desk for more than 8 months, with a monitoring scope that includes more than 600 plants and substations and more than 90 sections across the region

record.title: Morphing-BOT: AI inspection of infrastructure to predict maintenance
record.summary: Morphing I reports that its Morphing-BOT robot inspected more than 30 km of water mains in four South Korean municipal pilots. It produced validated inspection data.
record.account: Morphing I led a government-funded data project on AI Hub, run by the National Information Society Agency. The dataset, opened on 28 June 2024, shows that the robot gathered 109,350 labeled records from water mains in Jeju, Siheung, Jeonju and Jindo in 2023. A project partner handled inspection. It handled the response to the quality check by the Telecommunications Technology Association. According to the dataset's notes, external sound recordings did not differ much between types of anomaly. In its account for the International Telecommunication Union, current as of June 2025, Morphing I reports that municipal pilots inspected more than 30 km of pipelines. It reports that the pilots produced validated inspection data. The developer states that the system is in early commercialization. The sources include no independent verification of the reported gains. Avoided leaks remain unmeasured. Avoided failures remain unmeasured.

The dataset, opened on 28 June 2024, shows that the robot gathered 109,350 labeled records from water mains in Jeju, Siheung, Jeonju and Jindo in 2023. A project partner handled inspection. It handled the response to the quality check by the Telecommunications Technology Association. According to the dataset's notes, external sound recordings did not differ much between types of anomaly. In its account for the International Telecommunication Union, current as of June 2025, Morphing I reports that municipal pilots inspected more than 30 km of pipelines. It reports that the pilots produced validated inspection data. The developer states that the system is in early commercialization. The sources include no independent verification of the reported gains. Avoided leaks remain unmeasured. Avoided failures remain unmeasured.

record.title: Philippine Red Cross activated its typhoon Early Action Protocol on a machine-learning forecast of impact from 510 before Storm Nalgae (October 2022)
record.summary: A machine-learning damage forecast from 510 met the early-action trigger on 27 October 2022. The Philippine Red Cross installed shelter kits for 78 Aurora households before Storm Nalgae.
record.account: The Philippine Red Cross approved its Early Action Protocol for typhoons in December 2019. Its model forecasts by impact. The Philippine Red Cross developed it with 510, an initiative of the Netherlands Red Cross. It applies machine learning to predict damage to housing in each municipality from typhoon forecasts. In 2021 the 510 model became the trigger model for the anticipatory action pilot of the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) in the Philippines. The Central Emergency Response Fund funded the OCHA pilot with $7.5 million for the 2023 typhoon season. Under the protocol, early actions start when the forecast shows at least 10 percent of houses totally damaged in more than three municipalities 72 hours before landfall. As Tropical Storm Paeng (Nalgae) approached on 27 October 2022, the 510 forecast projected up to 10 percent shelter damage in priority municipalities. That met the trigger at 56 hours' lead time. According to the final report, the 56-hour lead time was granted as an exception. With anticipatory funds from the Disaster Response Emergency Fund of the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies, the Philippine Red Cross activated the protocol in Aurora Province. From 27 to 29 October, 40 workers distributed kits for strengthening shelters to 78 of 100 planned households in Dipaculao before landfall. They installed them. According to the same report, strong winds limited the distribution to 78 households. The onset of rain limited it. In its survey after the storm, the Philippine Red Cross reports that all 78 kits were installed. It reports that 390 people were reached. The operation spent CHF 7,002 of its CHF 117,555 budget. The final report of 30 June 2023 records a workshop on lessons learned. Its participants judged the trigger high. They recommended a review of the protocol.

This was the first completed activation of the Philippine typhoon protocol. In the final report, the Red Cross records lessons about lead time and the limits that the weather set.
The 390 people reached are the members of the reinforced households. The Philippine Red Cross reports no outcome beyond them.

data.retained_case_account: The Philippine Red Cross (PRC) approved its Early Action Protocol (EAP) for typhoons in December 2019. Its impact-based forecasting (IBF) model, developed with 510 (Netherlands Red Cross), applies machine learning (ML) to predict housing damage per municipality from typhoon forecasts. As Tropical Storm Paeng (Nalgae) approached on 27 October 2022, the 510/IBF forecast projected up to 10 percent shelter damage in priority municipalities. That hit the trigger at 56 hours' lead time. With IFRC anticipatory DREF funds, PRC activated it in Aurora Province. On 27 to 29 October, 40 workers distributed and installed shelter strengthening kits for 78 of 100 planned households in Dipaculao before landfall. PRC's post-storm survey reports all 78 kits installed, 390 people reached. CHF 7,002 of the CHF 117,555 budget was spent.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: The ML impact forecast was the trigger. Under the EAP, early actions fire on the forecast wind impact on housing 72 hours before landfall. The trigger: at least 10% of houses totally damaged in more than three municipalities. The notification records the Aurora municipalities as “Met (More than 10%)”. The 72-hour lead-time condition was not met. The final report says the 56-hour lead time was exceptionally granted. The notification says the projection came from the 510/IBF forecast incorporating PAGASA data. PRC staff confirmed chapter capacity and chose municipalities. The outcome claim is PRC's own post-storm survey. The NHESS paper and EGU abstract on the model have 510 staff as co-authors, not lead authors.
