fields.account: The Philippine Red Cross approved its Early Action Protocol for typhoons in December 2019. Its model forecasts by impact. The Philippine Red Cross developed it with 510, an initiative of the Netherlands Red Cross. It applies machine learning to predict damage to housing in each municipality from typhoon forecasts. In 2021 the 510 model became the trigger model for the anticipatory action pilot of the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) in the Philippines. The Central Emergency Response Fund funded the OCHA pilot with $7.5 million for the 2023 typhoon season. Under the protocol, early actions start when the forecast shows at least 10 percent of houses totally damaged in more than three municipalities 72 hours before landfall. As Tropical Storm Paeng (Nalgae) approached on 27 October 2022, the 510 forecast projected up to 10 percent shelter damage in priority municipalities. That met the trigger at 56 hours' lead time. According to the final report, the 56-hour lead time was granted as an exception. With anticipatory funds from the Disaster Response Emergency Fund of the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies, the Philippine Red Cross activated the protocol in Aurora Province. From 27 to 29 October, 40 workers distributed kits for strengthening shelters to 78 of 100 planned households in Dipaculao before landfall. They installed them. According to the same report, strong winds limited the distribution to 78 households. The onset of rain limited it. In its survey after the storm, the Philippine Red Cross reports that all 78 kits were installed. It reports that 390 people were reached. The operation spent CHF 7,002 of its CHF 117,555 budget. The final report of 30 June 2023 records a workshop on lessons learned. Its participants judged the trigger high. They recommended a review of the protocol.

record.account: The International Fund for Animal Welfare (IFAW) and Baidu launched AI Guardian, an image-recognition tool that supports monitoring of online wildlife trade, on 22 April 2020. In a five-month test it flagged 3,348 images of illegal wildlife products among about 250,000 picture messages, at a reported accuracy of 75%. IFAW reports that by June 2024 the tool had screened over 360,000 images. It reports that the tool detected 21,271 images of targeted species. The screening led to the removal of 7,853 illegal postings. Version 2.0, a broader species-detection version, followed on 21 November 2024. The number of prevented transactions is not established. How many animals the tool protected is not established.

details.value: The Taoyuan environmental bureau places mobile AI sound cameras on main roads and residential streets to collect data on noise. Its staff combine the data with complaints to find when and where illegally modified, noisy vehicles appear.

details.label: Contribution of the AI
details.value: The bureau's own description is the only account of what the system contributed. The task force placed AI sound cameras at the relevant spots on the night of the complaint. By analyzing the noise data against the complaints, staff worked out where and when the car appeared. Environmental and police officers then found it near Daxing Road on 23 April. The bureau does not say how the cameras link a noise to a vehicle, and it reports no decibel reading. The bureau has not estimated how long a conventional patrol would have taken. The stop, the referral and the pending penalty were the officers' work.

record.title: Taoyuan's AI sound cameras locate a white BMW that had been roaring down Jieshou Road at night, within a day of residents' complaint
record.summary: Mobile AI sound cameras of Taoyuan's environmental department located a loud white BMW within a day of a complaint from residents. Officers stopped it on 23 April 2025.
record.account: Residents of Bade District, Taoyuan, complained in the Facebook group 記憶八德. A white BMW with a loud exhaust kept roaring down Jieshou Road late at night. The Taoyuan City Department of Environmental Protection received the complaint on the night of 22 April 2025. Its Quiet Taoyuan (靜桃) task force immediately set up sound cameras that use AI at the relevant spots. By analyzing the noise data against the complaints, it worked out where the car appeared. It worked out when. On 23 April environmental and police officers stopped it near Daxing Road. The car was referred to the motor vehicle office for a modification review. The bureau said that a fine of up to NT$3,600 under the Noise Control Act would follow. It said that an order to fix the car would follow. All five cited reports reproduce statements from the Taoyuan City Department of Environmental Protection. None adds reporting of its own. In January 2026 the bureau said that noise complaints had fallen 38 percent since the Quiet Taoyuan project began. The bureau reported that 50 sets of sound cameras were installed across the city.
record.purpose: The Taoyuan environmental bureau places mobile AI sound cameras on main roads and residential streets to collect data on noise. Its staff combine the data with complaints to find when and where illegally modified, noisy vehicles appear.
record.system: AI sound camera equipment (AI聲音照相) of the Quiet Taoyuan (靜桃) project, part of the bureau's network of 'improved mobile sound cameras' (改良式移動聲音照相)
record.deployer: Taoyuan City Department of Environmental Protection (桃園市政府環境保護局), with the Taoyuan City Police Department for the stop

ratings.reason: Residents on Jieshou Road had written that the car's passes late at night seriously affected their quality of life and sleep. The car was identified and referred for a review of its modifications. Whether the noise stopped afterwards is not documented, so no outcome for the residents is reported.

The bureau closed one complaint in 24 hours and used the case to publicize its enforcement with sound cameras. It gives no figures for its claim that the cameras “greatly raise the success rate” of tracking noisy vehicles.

ai_role.statement: The bureau's own description is the only account of what the system contributed. The task force placed AI sound cameras at the relevant spots on the night of the complaint. By analyzing the noise data against the complaints, staff worked out where and when the car appeared. Environmental and police officers then found it near Daxing Road on 23 April. The bureau does not say how the cameras link a noise to a vehicle, and it reports no decibel reading. The bureau has not estimated how long a conventional patrol would have taken. The stop, the referral and the pending penalty were the officers' work.

produced_by: A complaint that named the road and the time window (late night on Jieshou Road). This told the task force where to place the cameras the same night.
Mobile AI sound cameras already in the bureau's inventory under the Quiet Taoyuan project. Deployment did not wait on procurement.

must_hold: The target must be a repeat offender with a pattern. The method matches noise data against complaint times and places, and cannot catch a one-off pass.
Officers must be free to intercept on the night the analysis points to. The cameras locate. They do not stop.
A legal basis for the follow-up: here the Noise Control Act (fine up to NT$3,600 and an improvement order). Also the Road Traffic Management and Penalty Act (up to NT$24,000 for a removed muffler).

fields.account: Residents of Bade District, Taoyuan, complained in the Facebook group 記憶八德. A white BMW with a loud exhaust kept roaring down Jieshou Road late at night. The Taoyuan City Department of Environmental Protection received the complaint on the night of 22 April 2025. Its Quiet Taoyuan (靜桃) task force immediately set up sound cameras that use AI at the relevant spots. By analyzing the noise data against the complaints, it worked out where the car appeared. It worked out when. On 23 April environmental and police officers stopped it near Daxing Road. The car was referred to the motor vehicle office for a modification review. The bureau said that a fine of up to NT$3,600 under the Noise Control Act would follow. It said that an order to fix the car would follow. All five cited reports reproduce statements from the Taoyuan City Department of Environmental Protection. None adds reporting of its own. In January 2026 the bureau said that noise complaints had fallen 38 percent since the Quiet Taoyuan project began. The bureau reported that 50 sets of sound cameras were installed across the city.

value.text: The car was located and stopped within 24 hours of the complaint, and the sources leave open whether its noise stopped afterward. In January 2026 the bureau reported 50 sound-camera sets installed citywide and noise complaints down 38 percent since the Quiet Taoyuan project began.

record.title: Hydrology aided by an LLM
record.summary: ZTE reports that Jiupai cut the time spent writing reports by approximately 30%. ZTE released this hydrology model with the Changjiang Hydrological Bureau.
record.account: The Changjiang Water Resources Commission's Hydrology Bureau released a hydrology model named Jiupai on 6 December 2024 at a basin hydrology meeting in Yunnan. China Water Resources News reported that the bureau had developed the model itself. It reported that the model was still in a founding stage. Its platform was at that stage. On 13 December 2024, ZTE described itself as a main technical support unit that released the model jointly with the bureau. In its later ITU account, ZTE describes an operational hydrology model with the Changjiang Hydrological Bureau as a partner. It reports shorter report writing. It reports faster thalweg drawing. It gives figures for the accuracy of predictions. It gives separate figures for the accuracy of queries. The system is intended to support water management. It is meant to support flood planning. Specific flood interventions remain undocumented. No prevented loss has been documented.

China Water Resources News reported that the bureau had developed the model itself. It reported that the model was still in a founding stage. Its platform was at that stage. On 13 December 2024, ZTE described itself as a main technical support unit that released the model jointly with the bureau. In its later ITU account, ZTE describes an operational hydrology model with the Changjiang Hydrological Bureau as a partner. It reports shorter report writing. It reports faster thalweg drawing. It gives figures for the accuracy of predictions. It gives separate figures for the accuracy of queries. The system is intended to support water management. It is meant to support flood planning. record.title: AI that uses the weather to forecast power from new energy sources
record.summary: Huadian and Huawei report that power forecasts from a fine-tuned Huawei Pangu weather model cut costs at a Jiangsu pilot. In the first half of 2024 one assessment penalty fell by 27%, another by 15%.
record.account: Huadian and Huawei describe AI-based meteorological power forecasting that runs on dedicated computing hardware. Beijing Jiutian Meteorological Technology supplied weather data. It supported the modeling. According to the contributors, the Jiangsu pilot reduced assessment penalties by 27% and 15% during the first half of 2024. The contributors report that the forecasts were computed faster. They report that the forecasts were more accurate. Huawei reported on 9 July 2025 that the pilot station belonged to China Huadian Jiangsu New Energy Company. By Huawei's figures, forecast accuracy at the station reached 97.24% at 15 minutes. At four hours it reached 91.72%. Wider adoption of renewable power, with its benefits for the climate, is an intended downstream effect. No independent account of the penalty reductions had appeared by October 2026.

record.title: The Metropolitan Police explores AI to sort child sexual abuse imagery so that officers can find unknown victims faster
record.summary: The Metropolitan Police said on 13 April 2026 that it is testing AI tools from unnamed companies. They grade abuse imagery. They flag unknown victims. No use on live cases has been reported.
record.account: On 12 July 2019 the Home Office announced an image categorization algorithm for the national Child Abuse Image Database. On 13 April 2026 the Metropolitan Police Service announced that it is exploring a similar use of artificial intelligence. It would grade child sexual abuse imagery quickly. It would triage it. Material possibly relating to unknown victims could then be marked so that safeguarding comes first. The force wants to reduce officers' manual review of distressing material. It said that it is in conversations with multiple companies. It said that it is testing how this could work. It described a separate tool that reviews 641,000 messages in 35 minutes. Its announcement covered a £10 million investment in suites for interviewing victims. It cited more than 5,400 child sexual abuse offenses investigated in the past year. It cited over 1,300 children safeguarded. Deputy Commissioner Matt Jukes said that speed matters for safeguarding. He said that human judgment would remain central. He said that oversight would remain central. As of 29 October 2026 the Metropolitan Police had not reported any use of the grading tools on live cases. It had not reported any result.

record.summary: South Korea's transport ministry plans AI cameras from an unnamed supplier that alert train drivers to road users trapped at crossings, with pilots at Nonsan and Boseong.
record.account: Kyunghyang Shinmun's 최미랑 reported on 11 February 2026 that the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport had drawn up a full plan to prevent accidents at railway crossings. It was to take effect from March 2026. It includes an AI-based intelligent closed-circuit television (CCTV) system, to be installed in railway protection zones nationwide. The system immediately detects a vehicle trapped inside a crossing. It detects a trapped pedestrian. It then transmits the information to the driver of an approaching train. Pilot installations were planned within the first quarter at Nonsan in Chungnam and at Boseong, where accidents occurred in 2025. Installation at the 543 national crossings would follow in sequence, depending on the results. The ministry set fines of up to 70,000 won, after a six-month grace period, for vehicles that fail to stop. Vehicles that enter while barriers operate face the same fines. The ministry cited 36 crossing accidents over five years with 14 deaths. There were 7 injuries. Driver carelessness caused 27 of the accidents. No developer has been named. Newspim reported on 10 July 2026 that the ministry still planned to install the AI cameras at the Nonsan and Boseong crossings, after the first-quarter target had passed. On 23 September 2026 the ministry and Korail said that crossing cameras were in pilot operation and that they would consider a phased expansion. No results have been reported.

fields.summary: South Korea's transport ministry plans AI cameras from an unnamed supplier that alert train drivers to road users trapped at crossings, with pilots at Nonsan and Boseong.
fields.account: Kyunghyang Shinmun's 최미랑 reported on 11 February 2026 that the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport had drawn up a full plan to prevent accidents at railway crossings. It was to take effect from March 2026. It includes an AI-based intelligent closed-circuit television (CCTV) system, to be installed in railway protection zones nationwide. The system immediately detects a vehicle trapped inside a crossing. It detects a trapped pedestrian. It then transmits the information to the driver of an approaching train. Pilot installations were planned within the first quarter at Nonsan in Chungnam and at Boseong, where accidents occurred in 2025. Installation at the 543 national crossings would follow in sequence, depending on the results. The ministry set fines of up to 70,000 won, after a six-month grace period, for vehicles that fail to stop. Vehicles that enter while barriers operate face the same fines. The ministry cited 36 crossing accidents over five years with 14 deaths. There were 7 injuries. Driver carelessness caused 27 of the accidents. No developer has been named. Newspim reported on 10 July 2026 that the ministry still planned to install the AI cameras at the Nonsan and Boseong crossings, after the first-quarter target had passed. On 23 September 2026 the ministry and Korail said that crossing cameras were in pilot operation and that they would consider a phased expansion. No results have been reported.

record.title: Detecting anomalies across 5G slices with federated learning
record.summary: An Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad team reports that its cross-slice federated learning model reached a macro F1 score of 93.83% on a test dataset with new anomalous traffic.
record.account: A team at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Hyderabad develops the system with open-source network tools. It uses network emulators. It is intended to identify anomalies across 5G network slices while the data stay distributed. In October 2025 the IIT Hyderabad team presented its results at the MSWiM conference in Barcelona. Its cross-slice federated model reached a macro F1 score of 93.83% on a test dataset with new anomalous traffic. The authors are the developers. No use in an operator network has been reported. No intercepted attack has been reported. No prevented loss has been reported. No measured service improvement has been reported.

fields.account: A team at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Hyderabad develops the system with open-source network tools. It uses network emulators. It is intended to identify anomalies across 5G network slices while the data stay distributed. In October 2025 the IIT Hyderabad team presented its results at the MSWiM conference in Barcelona. Its cross-slice federated model reached a macro F1 score of 93.83% on a test dataset with new anomalous traffic. The authors are the developers. No use in an operator network has been reported. No intercepted attack has been reported. No prevented loss has been reported. No measured service improvement has been reported.

record.title: WINGS says, quoting the mayor, that wi.breathe cameras alert authorities to a Troizina wildfire
record.summary: WINGS says that the AI fire detector on its wi.breathe cameras alerted authorities to a wildfire at Troizina on 28 August 2025. The municipality did not mention them in its statement that day.
record.account: ERT, Greece's public broadcaster, reported on 28 August 2025 that 45 firefighters, 13 vehicles, two planes and four helicopters had been sent to the fire at Diavologefyro near Troizina. It reported that footage showed the fire close to houses. Saronic Magazine quoted the municipality, which said that the fire was put out quickly, before it grew out of control. In its statement that evening, the municipality credits a coordinated response. More than 80 firefighters took part, with six aircraft. The municipality thanks the fire service, the police and volunteers. It credits cooperation among agencies. It does not mention the cameras. Reporters and the municipality set out how large the fire was. They give the scale of the response. None of them verifies the AI's contribution. WINGS reported on 2 September 2025 that its wi.breathe cameras in Methana had detected the wildfire in Troizina on 28 August. It reported that the cameras had alerted authorities. The company quoted Mayor Tasos Ath. Mougios crediting the system with preventing a larger disaster. The mayor's credit to wi.breathe appears only in this WINGS release. That account comes with no alert log, no detection time, no chronology of the response and no estimate of avoided damage. WINGS later announced completion of the wider camera installation on 12 May 2026. Detection within one minute is claimed in publicity for the completed installation. That figure concerns the system's capability. WINGS gives no measurement of it for the August fire.

fields.summary: WINGS says that the AI fire detector on its wi.breathe cameras alerted authorities to a wildfire at Troizina on 28 August 2025. The municipality did not mention them in its statement that day.
fields.account: ERT, Greece's public broadcaster, reported on 28 August 2025 that 45 firefighters, 13 vehicles, two planes and four helicopters had been sent to the fire at Diavologefyro near Troizina. It reported that footage showed the fire close to houses. Saronic Magazine quoted the municipality, which said that the fire was put out quickly, before it grew out of control. In its statement that evening, the municipality credits a coordinated response. More than 80 firefighters took part, with six aircraft. The municipality thanks the fire service, the police and volunteers. It credits cooperation among agencies. It does not mention the cameras. Reporters and the municipality set out how large the fire was. They give the scale of the response. None of them verifies the AI's contribution. WINGS reported on 2 September 2025 that its wi.breathe cameras in Methana had detected the wildfire in Troizina on 28 August. It reported that the cameras had alerted authorities. The company quoted Mayor Tasos Ath. Mougios crediting the system with preventing a larger disaster. The mayor's credit to wi.breathe appears only in this WINGS release. That account comes with no alert log, no detection time, no chronology of the response and no estimate of avoided damage. WINGS later announced completion of the wider camera installation on 12 May 2026. Detection within one minute is claimed in publicity for the completed installation. That figure concerns the system's capability. WINGS gives no measurement of it for the August fire.

record.title: UNDP hands SESU the Ukrainian “Mines Eye” AI aerial detection system after a pilot that scanned over 360 hectares in Kharkiv and Mykolaiv oblasts
record.summary: Mines Eye, an aerial system whose AI detects explosive remnants of war, scanned over 360 hectares in a five-month pilot by Ukraine's emergency service. No detection counts have been published.
record.account: Mines Eye is an aerial detection system. It combines three methods: magnetometry, visual aerial imaging and infrared aerial imaging. In a press release of 21 June 2025, the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in Ukraine calls the system “Developed in Ukraine” but does not name the developer. UNDP states that “Using artificial intelligence, it detects explosive remnants of war (ERW), including anti-tank mines, even beneath vegetation”. The system produces maps for operators before clearance, with reports of anomalies. UNDP-trained teams of the State Emergency Service of Ukraine (SESU) ran a five-month pilot. They “used the system to scan over 360 hectares of confirmed and suspected hazardous areas in Kharkiv and Mykolaiv oblasts”. The release is datelined Mykolaiv. UNDP writes that it “officially handed over the Mines Eye aerial detection system to the State Emergency Service of Ukraine (SESU)”. Financial support came from the Government of Luxembourg. The handover took place at the base of SESU's Main Department in Mykolaiv oblast, with UNDP Acting Administrator Haoliang Xu present. SESU First Deputy Head Vitalii Myroniuk is quoted as saying that the technology “enables us to detect threats in areas that are too dangerous for manual inspection”. UNDP gives no number of items detected, no number confirmed, no figure for hectares released and no accuracy figure. UNDP's release of 26 June 2025 concerned a testing exhibition with mock devices. No source independent of UNDP or SESU has been found.

data.retained_case_account: UNDP Ukraine's press release of 21 June 2025 is datelined Mykolaiv. It says UNDP “officially handed over the Mines Eye aerial detection system to the State Emergency Service of Ukraine (SESU)”. Financial support came from the Government of Luxembourg. The base of SESU's Main Department in Mykolaiv oblast hosted it, with UNDP Acting Administrator Haoliang Xu present. The release calls the system “Developed in Ukraine” but does not name the developer. It combines magnetometry with visual and infrared aerial imaging. It states that “Using artificial intelligence, it detects explosive remnants of war (ERW), including anti-tank mines, even beneath vegetation”. It produces maps and anomaly reports for operators before manual or mechanical clearance. UNDP-trained SESU teams ran a five-month pilot. They “used the system to scan over 360 hectares of confirmed and suspected hazardous areas in Kharkiv and Mykolaiv oblasts”. SESU First Deputy Head Vitalii Myroniuk is quoted that the technology “enables us to detect threats in areas that are too dangerous for manual inspection”. The release gives no number of items detected or confirmed, no hectares released, and no accuracy figure. UNDP's 26 June 2025 release concerned a testing exhibition with mock devices. No source independent of UNDP or SESU was found.

record.title: Remote visual tracking in disasters using GenAI-based predictive rendering
record.summary: Tata Consultancy Services proposes a system that would let disaster responders share visual information over limited bandwidth. It uses semantic scene understanding. It uses generative rendering.
record.account: Three researchers at Tata Consultancy Services described the disaster-tracking scenario in a paper at the 17th International Conference on Communication Systems and Networks in Bengaluru on 6 January 2025. The authors present disaster tracking as one of two application scenarios. They report lessons from an initial proof of concept for one of them. The concept seeks to reconstruct useful visual scenes from compact transmitted information. In the International Telecommunication Union entry, current as of June 2025, the team states that the concept is not fully deployed. The team reports that existing datasets do not suit the purpose. It reports that it needs to develop its own. Faster response to disasters is an intended benefit. Reduced consequences are an intended benefit. No observed response has been reported. No rescue outcome has been reported.

record.title: AI-Driven Early Warning System for Oceanic Dead Zones
record.summary: Vellore Institute of Technology is developing an AI system to forecast low-oxygen ocean dead zones two to four weeks ahead, with regional pilots planned.
record.account: In the International Telecommunication Union entry, the developer is the Vellore Institute of Technology, Chennai campus. The prototype combines environmental data with neural models to predict low-oxygen conditions. The makers report no forecast accuracy for the prototype. Under testbeds, the team lists the National Institute of Oceanography and the Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services. Proposed pilots cover hypoxia-prone seas. One intended response is nutrient management. Fishing restrictions are a second. No intervention driven by an alert has been documented. No avoided fish death has been documented. No preserved fishing income has been documented.

In an International Telecommunication Union (ITU) report that is current as of June 2025, the authors report that they trained models on a cleaned version of the public CICIoT2023 dataset. They ran only a simulated edge deployment. A lab test in a smart home network is still planned. They report no accuracy figures. Detection performance remains unreported. No security benefit has been reported. The code repository is listed as coming soon. No paper from the team appeared after June 2025. No code release appeared. No report of a deployment appeared.

record.title: OpenAI o3 finds CVE-2025-37899, a remote use-after-free in the Linux kernel's ksmbd, fixed in mainline in April 2025 before the 6.1 and 6.6 longterm branches get the fix on 6 December 2025
record.summary: The researcher Sean Heelan ran OpenAI's o3 through the plain application programming interface. It flagged a previously unknown use-after-free in the Linux kernel's SMB server, now CVE-2025-37899.
record.account: Sean Heelan is an independent vulnerability researcher who was auditing ksmbd, the Linux kernel's in-kernel server for the SMB3 file-sharing protocol. He used a known bug (CVE-2025-37778) to benchmark OpenAI's o3 through the plain application programming interface. He used no scaffolding. He used no agents. He used no tools. Given about 12,000 lines covering all SMB command handlers, o3 reported a previously unknown use-after-free in the handler for the SMB “logoff” command. In that flaw, sess->user can be freed while another connection bound to the same session still uses it. Heelan wrote the fix on 21 April 2025. The SMB maintainer Steve French committed it to the ksmbd tree on 25 April 2025 with the acknowledgment of the ksmbd maintainer, Namjae Jeon. It reached mainline on 28 April 2025. The fix reached the 6.12 and 6.14 branches on 9 May 2025. The Linux kernel's CVE Numbering Authority published CVE-2025-37899 on 20 May 2025. Heelan's write-up followed on 22 May 2025. He calls it, to his knowledge, the first public case of a large language model finding a vulnerability of that nature. Linuxiac reported on 29 May 2025 that the upstream response was fast. It reported that patches had been merged for every maintained branch. The fix reached the 6.1 and 6.6 longterm branches later, on 6 December 2025. In the CVE record, the fix now appears as “ksmbd: fix use-after-free in session logoff”. It lists the mainline commit, which is in 6.15, with backports to four stable branches. The 6.1 branch is fixed from 6.1.159 and the 6.6 branch from 6.6.119. The 6.12 branch is fixed from 6.12.28 and the 6.14 branch from 6.14.6. It lists the 5.15 branch as affected with no fixed version.

fields.account: Sean Heelan is an independent vulnerability researcher who was auditing ksmbd, the Linux kernel's in-kernel server for the SMB3 file-sharing protocol. He used a known bug (CVE-2025-37778) to benchmark OpenAI's o3 through the plain application programming interface. He used no scaffolding. He used no agents. He used no tools. Given about 12,000 lines covering all SMB command handlers, o3 reported a previously unknown use-after-free in the handler for the SMB “logoff” command. In that flaw, sess->user can be freed while another connection bound to the same session still uses it. Heelan wrote the fix on 21 April 2025. The SMB maintainer Steve French committed it to the ksmbd tree on 25 April 2025 with the acknowledgment of the ksmbd maintainer, Namjae Jeon. It reached mainline on 28 April 2025. The fix reached the 6.12 and 6.14 branches on 9 May 2025. The Linux kernel's CVE Numbering Authority published CVE-2025-37899 on 20 May 2025. Heelan's write-up followed on 22 May 2025. He calls it, to his knowledge, the first public case of a large language model finding a vulnerability of that nature. Linuxiac reported on 29 May 2025 that the upstream response was fast. It reported that patches had been merged for every maintained branch. The fix reached the 6.1 and 6.6 longterm branches later, on 6 December 2025. In the CVE record, the fix now appears as “ksmbd: fix use-after-free in session logoff”. It lists the mainline commit, which is in 6.15, with backports to four stable branches. The 6.1 branch is fixed from 6.1.159 and the 6.6 branch from 6.6.119. The 6.12 branch is fixed from 6.12.28 and the 6.14 branch from 6.14.6. It lists the 5.15 branch as affected with no fixed version.

fields.account: Sean Heelan is an independent vulnerability researcher who was auditing ksmbd, the Linux kernel's in-kernel server for the SMB3 file-sharing protocol. He used a known bug (CVE-2025-37778) to benchmark OpenAI's o3 through the plain application programming interface. He used no scaffolding. He used no agents. He used no tools. Given about 12,000 lines covering all SMB command handlers, o3 reported a previously unknown use-after-free in the handler for the SMB “logoff” command. In that flaw, sess->user can be freed while another connection bound to the same session still uses it. Heelan wrote the fix on 21 April 2025. The SMB maintainer Steve French committed it to the ksmbd tree on 25 April 2025 with the acknowledgment of the ksmbd maintainer, Namjae Jeon. It reached mainline on 28 April 2025. The fix reached the 6.12 and 6.14 branches on 9 May 2025. The Linux kernel's CVE Numbering Authority published CVE-2025-37899 on 20 May 2025. Heelan's write-up followed on 22 May 2025. He calls it, to his knowledge, the first public case of a large language model finding a vulnerability of that nature. Linuxiac reported on 29 May 2025 that the upstream response was fast. It reported that patches had been merged for every maintained branch. The fix reached the 6.1 and 6.6 longterm branches later, on 6 December 2025. In the CVE record, the fix now appears as “ksmbd: fix use-after-free in session logoff”. It lists the mainline commit, which is in 6.15, with backports to four stable branches. The 6.1 branch is fixed from 6.1.159 and the 6.6 branch from 6.6.119. The 6.12 branch is fixed from 6.12.28 and the 6.14 branch from 6.14.6. It lists the 5.15 branch as affected with no fixed version.

record.account: The project models relationships between weather and power-line data transmission. On 25 April 2025, the project team at Universiti Putra Malaysia published its results in Transactions on Engineering and Computing Sciences. The authors report that their model predicts a regional throughput performance of 71.62% for Peninsular Malaysia. Across six Nigerian regions it predicts between 74.46% and 99.97%. Universiti Putra Malaysia and the Nigerian Meteorological Agency supplied the historical weather data. In June 2025, the project had collected data for Malaysia and Nigeria. It had developed models for both. It was still in research. Prototyping was also under way. No network improvement has been credited to the AI, as distinct from replacement of infrastructure. The authors do not report that a utility used these predictions.

record.title: Authors of a study suggest that Google Flood Hub and GloFAS forecasts could extend some flood early-action plans in Mali from four to seven days, though Flood Hub gave frequent false alarms
record.summary: Authors of a retrospective study suggest that Google Flood Hub could extend some early-action plans in Mali from four to seven days, with frequent false alarms. No early action was measured.
record.account: Researchers evaluated forecasts from Google Flood Hub and the Global Flood Awareness System (GloFAS) against observations of river flow in Mali. They checked them against records of the impacts of floods. Four of the seven authors work for the Netherlands Red Cross data and digital team 510. The researchers are independent of Google, although one coauthor works at the Joint Research Centre, which contributes to GloFAS. The authors first presented the result in a European Geosciences Union abstract dated 14 March 2025. They posted a preprint on 7 January 2026. The journal article appeared on 16 September 2026. Their results show that some early-action plans could extend from four to seven days without much loss of forecast skill. Performance varied across districts. It varied across thresholds. No correctly predicted floods were found in the northern districts that were evaluated. At a seven-day lead time, Google Flood Hub’s false-alarm ratio was around 0.8 across discharge thresholds, compared with around 0.5 for GloFAS. The authors describe GloFAS as more balanced in several comparisons. They used a ten-day matching window to compare forecasts with reported impacts, which affects the interpretation of performance. This was a retrospective evaluation of forecasts. It did not measure benefits from an early action that was carried out. The Mali Red Cross has not reported that its protocol has adopted these forecasts. It has not reported that the protocol has adopted a lead time of seven days.

Their results suggest that some early-action plans could extend from four to seven days without much loss of forecast skill. Performance varied across districts and thresholds, and no correctly predicted floods were found in the northern districts that were evaluated. At a seven-day lead time, Google Flood Hub’s false-alarm ratio was around 0.8 across discharge thresholds, compared with around 0.5 for GloFAS. The authors describe GloFAS as more balanced in several comparisons. They used a ten-day matching window to compare forecasts with reported impacts, which affects the interpretation of performance. This was a retrospective forecast evaluation; it did not measure benefits from an implemented early action. The researchers are independent of Google, although one coauthor works at the Joint Research Centre, which contributes to GloFAS.

record.title: Quartz Solar AI Cloudcasting - predicting cloud movements through satellite imagery
record.summary: Open Climate Fix reports that predicted satellite images from its Cloudcasting model raised the accuracy of its PVNet solar forecasts by 5% at two hours ahead.
record.account: Cloudcasting began as a 2024 Manchester Prize entry by Open Climate Fix with the Alan Turing Institute. As a finalist, the project received £100,000 in the prize, which the UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology runs. On 20 February 2025, Open Climate Fix published an early evaluation of the model. It reported that Cloudcasting input gave a 5% accuracy gain at a two-hour horizon when integrated into PVNet, its solar forecasting model. By its measure, cloud forecasts from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) added 2.5% when integrated into PVNet. Open Climate Fix planned to add Cloudcasting to Quartz Solar in the United Kingdom by summer 2025. In its release of 6 November 2025 on the adoption of Quartz Solar in the control room of the National Energy System Operator, Open Climate Fix does not mention Cloudcasting. In the developer's code repository, the model is described as running live in production. The repository received updates in August 2026. No measured effect of Cloudcasting in live forecasts has been reported. The annual carbon savings remain projected.

fields.account: Cloudcasting began as a 2024 Manchester Prize entry by Open Climate Fix with the Alan Turing Institute. As a finalist, the project received £100,000 in the prize, which the UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology runs. It reported that Cloudcasting input gave a 5% accuracy gain at a two-hour horizon when integrated into PVNet, its solar forecasting model. By its measure, cloud forecasts from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) added 2.5% when integrated into PVNet. In the developer's code repository, the model is described as running live in production. The repository received updates in August 2026. No measured effect of Cloudcasting in live forecasts has been reported. The annual carbon savings remain projected.

record.summary: Hangzhou Dianzi University reports that its content moderation system detected deepfakes with about 95% accuracy in a challenge. It reports that public security bureaus in China apply it.
record.account: The organizers of the Inclusion 2024 deepfake detection challenge report that 1,500 teams took part. They report that they ranked entries by the area under the curve (AUC). In their report, published on 30 December 2024, they do not name the Hangzhou Dianzi University team. In its account for the International Telecommunication Union, the university describes a system that detects forged media. It checks generated content. The account gives Tong Qiao of the university's School of Cyberspace as the contact. The university reports that the system reached about 95% detection accuracy in the challenge. It reports applications with police. It describes further development of the platform. The university has published no measure of prevented fraud losses. It has published none of effects on public safety. The police have published neither measure.

record.title: Radiolytica - Using AI Tools to Protect Communities from Harmful Content in Eastern DRC
record.summary: Fondation Hirondelle's Radiolytica transcribes French and Swahili community radio to detect hate speech in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. No measured result has been reported.
record.account: Radiolytica combines speech recognition with language models to monitor French and Swahili radio. Human review is part of it. In its 2024 annual report, Fondation Hirondelle states that a pilot to detect hate speech with AI on community radio in Goma and Bukavu was set up in 2024. In its June 2025 account, the foundation describes a research prototype that it plans to expand. On a project page for the 2025 AI Action Summit, the foundation wrote that it monitors community radio stations in the east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It wrote that it broadcasts adapted radio content in response to the hate speech that it detects. Faster monitoring is an intended benefit. Counter-messaging is an intended benefit. No response to a particular broadcast is documented. No measured reduction in harm is documented. In its project sheet of April 2026, the foundation sets the goal of extending this monitoring to 100 radio stations in 2026. It reports no measured result.

In its 2024 annual report, Fondation Hirondelle states that a pilot to detect hate speech with AI on community radio in Goma and Bukavu was set up in 2024. On a project page for the 2025 AI Action Summit, the foundation wrote that it monitors community radio stations in the east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. In its project sheet of April 2026, the foundation sets the goal of extending this monitoring to 100 radio stations in 2026. It reports no measured result.

record.title: A live GraphCast run may have forecast Hurricane Lee's landfall in Nova Scotia about nine days ahead
record.summary: DeepMind says that a live GraphCast run predicted about nine days in advance that Hurricane Lee would make landfall in Nova Scotia. No source shows that a forecaster used the run.
record.account: The European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) wrote an editorial in its Newsletter 177 (Autumn 2023). In it, ECMWF confirms that GraphCast, Pangu-Weather and FourCastNet were made available on its public charts pages. They ran from ECMWF's own initial conditions. In a blog post of 14 November 2023, Google DeepMind states that a live version of its public GraphCast model ran on the ECMWF website in September 2023. It says that the model predicted about nine days in advance that Hurricane Lee would make landfall in Nova Scotia. DeepMind dates the forecast only as “September”. Lee, by then post-tropical, made landfall on Long Island in southwestern Nova Scotia around 2000 UTC on 16 September 2023. Its maximum sustained winds were about 55 knots. On 14 November 2023 MIT Technology Review relayed the nine-day claim from Rémi Lam, a staff research scientist at DeepMind. It added that traditional forecasting models pinpointed Nova Scotia only six days in advance. The magazine quotes no ECMWF staff on Lee. In its tropical cyclone report on Lee, dated 21 March 2024, the National Hurricane Center (NHC) records the landfall. It mentions no AI model. It reports that official NHC track errors were exceptionally low through 72 hours. They were below five-year means through 120 hours. The NHC's verification report for 2023 has no entry for an AI model. No ECMWF document recording the Lee forecast has been found. Researchers at the Cooperative Institute for Research in the Atmosphere (CIRA) at Colorado State University are independent of DeepMind. In a preprint, they mention Lee only for two features. One is its intensity. The other is its structure. In October 2025 researchers at CIRA published a verification of AI weather models for the 2023 cyclone season, run from initial conditions of the Global Forecast System. They found that GraphCast had the lowest mean track errors from 96 hours onward, by up to 13% against the ECMWF model, although the differences were not statistically significant. They do not report a track result for Lee. No forecaster is known to have acted on the GraphCast run for Lee. No authority is known to have acted on it.

data.retained_case_account: Google DeepMind's blog post of 14 November 2023 describes a live version of its publicly available GraphCast model, deployed on the ECMWF website. In September 2023 it predicted about nine days in advance that Hurricane Lee would make landfall in Nova Scotia. MIT Technology Review (14 November 2023) relayed the claim from DeepMind staff research scientist Rémi Lam. It added that traditional forecasting models pinpointed Nova Scotia only six days in advance. The article quotes no ECMWF staff on Lee. ECMWF's Newsletter 177 editorial (Autumn 2023) confirms that GraphCast, Pangu-Weather and FourCastNet were made available on ECMWF's public charts pages from ECMWF's own initial conditions. The NHC tropical cyclone report on Lee (21 March 2024) records the landfall. Lee, by then post-tropical, made landfall on Long Island in southwestern Nova Scotia around 2000 UTC on 16 September 2023. Maximum sustained winds were about 55 kt. NHC official track errors were exceptionally low through 72 h and below five-year means through 120 h. The report mentions no AI model. No ECMWF document recording the Lee forecast is on record, and the NHC 2023 verification report contains no AI-model entry. It found only an intensity-structure mention of Lee in the independent CIRA preprint. The forecast itself is dated only as “September” by the vendor. No cited source documents a forecaster or authority acting on the GraphCast Lee run.

The AI output is therefore documented as a forecast, not as an input to any decision.

fields.account: The European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) wrote an editorial in its Newsletter 177 (Autumn 2023). In it, ECMWF confirms that GraphCast, Pangu-Weather and FourCastNet were made available on its public charts pages. They ran from ECMWF's own initial conditions. In a blog post of 14 November 2023, Google DeepMind states that a live version of its public GraphCast model ran on the ECMWF website in September 2023. It says that the model predicted about nine days in advance that Hurricane Lee would make landfall in Nova Scotia. DeepMind dates the forecast only as “September”. Lee, by then post-tropical, made landfall on Long Island in southwestern Nova Scotia around 2000 UTC on 16 September 2023. Its maximum sustained winds were about 55 knots. On 14 November 2023 MIT Technology Review relayed the nine-day claim from Rémi Lam, a staff research scientist at DeepMind. It added that traditional forecasting models pinpointed Nova Scotia only six days in advance. The magazine quotes no ECMWF staff on Lee. In its tropical cyclone report on Lee, dated 21 March 2024, the National Hurricane Center (NHC) records the landfall. It mentions no AI model. It reports that official NHC track errors were exceptionally low through 72 hours. They were below five-year means through 120 hours. The NHC's verification report for 2023 has no entry for an AI model. No ECMWF document recording the Lee forecast has been found. Researchers at the Cooperative Institute for Research in the Atmosphere (CIRA) at Colorado State University are independent of DeepMind. In a preprint, they mention Lee only for two features. One is its intensity. The other is its structure. In October 2025 researchers at CIRA published a verification of AI weather models for the 2023 cyclone season, run from initial conditions of the Global Forecast System. They found that GraphCast had the lowest mean track errors from 96 hours onward, by up to 13% against the ECMWF model, although the differences were not statistically significant. They do not report a track result for Lee. No forecaster is known to have acted on the GraphCast run for Lee. No authority is known to have acted on it.

The differences were not statistically significant, and the researchers give no track result for Lee.

It says that the model predicted about nine days in advance that Hurricane Lee would make landfall in Nova Scotia. DeepMind dates the forecast only as “September”. Lee, by then post-tropical, made landfall on Long Island in southwestern Nova Scotia around 2000 UTC on 16 September 2023. Its maximum sustained winds were about 55 knots. On 14 November 2023 MIT Technology Review relayed the nine-day claim from Rémi Lam, a staff research scientist at DeepMind. It added that traditional forecasting models pinpointed Nova Scotia only six days in advance. The magazine quotes no ECMWF staff on Lee. In its tropical cyclone report on Lee, dated 21 March 2024, the National Hurricane Center (NHC) records the landfall. It mentions no AI model. It reports that official NHC track errors were exceptionally low through 72 hours. They were below five-year means through 120 hours. The NHC's verification report for 2023 has no entry for an AI model. No ECMWF document recording the Lee forecast has been found. Researchers at the Cooperative Institute for Research in the Atmosphere (CIRA) at Colorado State University are independent of DeepMind. In a preprint, they mention Lee only for two features. One is its intensity. The other is its structure. In October 2025 researchers at CIRA published a verification of AI weather models for the 2023 cyclone season, run from initial conditions of the Global Forecast System. They found that GraphCast had the lowest mean track errors from 96 hours onward, by up to 13% against the ECMWF model, although the differences were not statistically significant. They do not report a track result for Lee. No forecaster is known to have acted on the GraphCast run for Lee. No authority is known to have acted on it.

record.title: In 2021 UN OCHA's CERF adopted 510's machine-learning model of typhoon impact as the trigger for anticipatory action in the Philippines, though no activation on that trigger is documented through October 2026
record.summary: UN plans for early typhoon aid in the Philippines have used 510's XGBoost model of house damage as the trigger since 2021. The only documented activation, in 2025, came from observed wind speed.
record.account: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) posted its Anticipatory Action (AA) Framework for Philippine typhoons on ReliefWeb on 15 September 2021. It set up a US$7.5 million pilot from the Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF) for about 270,500 people in Regions 5 and 8 with FAO, IOM, UNFPA, UNICEF and WFP. It has a two-stage trigger. The readiness trigger is PAGASA and 510 forecasts of a category 4 or stronger cyclone. The activation trigger, within 72 hours of landfall, is the number of totally damaged houses predicted by the IFRC/Netherlands Red Cross 510 probabilistic typhoon impact prediction model. OCHA says in the framework that the model partly uses a machine learning model relating wind speed to housing damage. In its After Action Review of 31 March 2022, OCHA records that Typhoon Rai (Odette) in December 2021 rapidly intensified. It records that the typhoon did not meet the activation criteria. There was a near activation with staff pre-deployed. The 2023 revision retained the 510 model. The model's makers at 510 published a paper in Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences in 2024. They state that the XGBoost model served in 2021 as the trigger model for the UN OCHA AA pilot. In its June 2025 report, OCHA says that the readiness trigger was met for Super Typhoon Pepito (Man-yi) in its November 2024 to April 2025 reporting period. Activation thresholds were not reached. CERF AA resources were reallocated to the response. The framework endorsed on 19 October 2025 covers US$6 million from CERF. It covers about 955,507 people in Regions 5, 8 and 13. Under it, OCHA and its Centre for Humanitarian Data compute predicted totally damaged buildings with the 510 model every 6–12 hours. The framework adds an observational trigger for super typhoons of 185 km/h or more reported by PAGASA. On 6 November 2025 CERF AA was activated for Super Typhoon Fung-Wong (Uwan) after the observational wind-speed threshold was triggered. OCHA reports that nearly US$6 million was released. It reports that WFP alone reached 42,100 families. An after-action review was held in April 2026. OCHA's framework for 2026 and 2027, endorsed on 22 October 2026, keeps the 510 model as the activation trigger for Regions 2, 3, 5 and 8. In it, OCHA states that the 2025 activation came from the observational trigger. No activation produced by the 510 model's output has been recorded.

data.retained_case_account: OCHA's Anticipatory Action (AA) Framework for Philippine typhoons was posted on ReliefWeb on 15 September 2021. It set up a US$7.5 million CERF pilot for about 270,500 people in Regions 5 and 8 with FAO, IOM, UNFPA, UNICEF and WFP. It has a two-stage trigger. The readiness trigger is PAGASA and 510 forecasts of a category 4 or stronger cyclone. The activation trigger, within 72 hours of landfall, is the IFRC/Netherlands Red Cross 510 probabilistic typhoon impact prediction model's predicted number of totally damaged houses. The framework says that model partially uses a machine learning model relating wind speed to housing damage. 510's 2024 NHESS paper (vendor-authored) states the XGBoost model served in 2021 as the trigger model for the UN OCHA AA pilot. OCHA's After Action Review of 31 March 2022 records that Typhoon Rai (Odette) in December 2021 rapidly intensified and did not meet the activation criteria. There was a near activation with staff pre-deployed. The 2023 revision retained the 510 model. The framework endorsed on 19 October 2025 covers US$6 million CERF and about 955,507 people in Regions 5, 8 and 13. OCHA and its Centre for Humanitarian Data compute predicted totally damaged buildings with the 510 model every 6–12 hours. It adds an observational trigger for super typhoons of 185 km/h or more reported by PAGASA. OCHA's June 2025 report says the readiness trigger was met for Super Typhoon Pepito (Man-yi) in its November 2024 to April 2025 reporting period. Activation thresholds were not reached and CERF AA resources were reallocated to the response. On 6 November 2025 CERF AA was activated for Super Typhoon Fung-Wong (Uwan) after the observational wind-speed threshold was triggered. OCHA reports nearly US$6 million released and WFP alone reaching 42,100 families. No cited document records an activation produced by the 510 model's output.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: OCHA's 2021, 2023 and 2025 frameworks name the IFRC/510 impact model as the activation-trigger model. The 2021 framework describes it as partially a machine learning model. This is documented by the deployer, not only the maker. The model's forecasts were monitored during the December 2021 near activation (Typhoon Rai) without meeting criteria. The 2024 readiness phase for Pepito ended with CERF AA resources reallocated to response. OCHA's flash update attributes the 6 November 2025 activation for Uwan to the observational threshold (forecast peak 195 km/h against the 185 km/h trigger). It does not state that the 510 model's estimates reached the activation matrix. The AI's contribution to any payout is therefore not established. The maker's NHESS paper is the only source describing the algorithm (XGBoost).

fields.account: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) posted its Anticipatory Action (AA) Framework for Philippine typhoons on ReliefWeb on 15 September 2021. It set up a US$7.5 million pilot from the Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF) for about 270,500 people in Regions 5 and 8 with FAO, IOM, UNFPA, UNICEF and WFP. It has a two-stage trigger. The readiness trigger is PAGASA and 510 forecasts of a category 4 or stronger cyclone. The activation trigger, within 72 hours of landfall, is the number of totally damaged houses predicted by the IFRC/Netherlands Red Cross 510 probabilistic typhoon impact prediction model. OCHA says in the framework that the model partly uses a machine learning model relating wind speed to housing damage. In its After Action Review of 31 March 2022, OCHA records that Typhoon Rai (Odette) in December 2021 rapidly intensified. It records that the typhoon did not meet the activation criteria. There was a near activation with staff pre-deployed. The 2023 revision retained the 510 model. The model's makers at 510 published a paper in Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences in 2024. They state that the XGBoost model served in 2021 as the trigger model for the UN OCHA AA pilot. In its June 2025 report, OCHA says that the readiness trigger was met for Super Typhoon Pepito (Man-yi) in its November 2024 to April 2025 reporting period. Activation thresholds were not reached. CERF AA resources were reallocated to the response. The framework endorsed on 19 October 2025 covers US$6 million from CERF. It covers about 955,507 people in Regions 5, 8 and 13. Under it, OCHA and its Centre for Humanitarian Data compute predicted totally damaged buildings with the 510 model every 6–12 hours. The framework adds an observational trigger for super typhoons of 185 km/h or more reported by PAGASA. On 6 November 2025 CERF AA was activated for Super Typhoon Fung-Wong (Uwan) after the observational wind-speed threshold was triggered. OCHA reports that nearly US$6 million was released. It reports that WFP alone reached 42,100 families. An after-action review was held in April 2026. OCHA's framework for 2026 and 2027, endorsed on 22 October 2026, keeps the 510 model as the activation trigger for Regions 2, 3, 5 and 8. In it, OCHA states that the 2025 activation came from the observational trigger. No activation produced by the 510 model's output has been recorded.

fields.summary: UN plans for early typhoon aid in the Philippines have used 510's XGBoost model of house damage as the trigger since 2021. The only documented activation, in 2025, came from observed wind speed.
fields.account: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) posted its Anticipatory Action (AA) Framework for Philippine typhoons on ReliefWeb on 15 September 2021. It set up a US$7.5 million pilot from the Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF) for about 270,500 people in Regions 5 and 8 with FAO, IOM, UNFPA, UNICEF and WFP. It has a two-stage trigger. The readiness trigger is PAGASA and 510 forecasts of a category 4 or stronger cyclone. The activation trigger, within 72 hours of landfall, is the number of totally damaged houses predicted by the IFRC/Netherlands Red Cross 510 probabilistic typhoon impact prediction model. OCHA says in the framework that the model partly uses a machine learning model relating wind speed to housing damage. In its After Action Review of 31 March 2022, OCHA records that Typhoon Rai (Odette) in December 2021 rapidly intensified. It records that the typhoon did not meet the activation criteria. There was a near activation with staff pre-deployed. The 2023 revision retained the 510 model. The model's makers at 510 published a paper in Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences in 2024. They state that the XGBoost model served in 2021 as the trigger model for the UN OCHA AA pilot. In its June 2025 report, OCHA says that the readiness trigger was met for Super Typhoon Pepito (Man-yi) in its November 2024 to April 2025 reporting period. Activation thresholds were not reached. CERF AA resources were reallocated to the response. The framework endorsed on 19 October 2025 covers US$6 million from CERF. It covers about 955,507 people in Regions 5, 8 and 13. Under it, OCHA and its Centre for Humanitarian Data compute predicted totally damaged buildings with the 510 model every 6–12 hours. The framework adds an observational trigger for super typhoons of 185 km/h or more reported by PAGASA. On 6 November 2025 CERF AA was activated for Super Typhoon Fung-Wong (Uwan) after the observational wind-speed threshold was triggered. OCHA reports that nearly US$6 million was released. It reports that WFP alone reached 42,100 families. An after-action review was held in April 2026. OCHA's framework for 2026 and 2027, endorsed on 22 October 2026, keeps the 510 model as the activation trigger for Regions 2, 3, 5 and 8. In it, OCHA states that the 2025 activation came from the observational trigger. No activation produced by the 510 model's output has been recorded.

record.title: In a simulated trial by the Japan Coast Guard at the Tokyo Wan Vessel Traffic Service Center, predictions of collision risk from Fujitsu's Zinrai help controllers warn vessels about two minutes earlier, with nearly twice as many warnings
record.summary: At a Tokyo Bay traffic center, controllers replayed past near misses with collision-risk predictions from Fujitsu Human Centric AI Zinrai. They sent warnings about two minutes earlier.
record.account: From December 2019 to March 2020, Fujitsu Limited and the Japan Coast Guard tested an artificial-intelligence system to predict vessel collisions at the Tokyo Wan Vessel Traffic Service Center. The center supports vessel traffic under an outsourcing contract with the Coast Guard. The system uses Fujitsu Human Centric AI Zinrai from Fujitsu Laboratories. The technology detects near misses between vessels. It predicts areas where collision risk concentrates in Tokyo Bay. In the center's training environment, six experienced maritime traffic controllers and instructors simulated control tasks based on past near-miss accidents. They compared conventional operation with operation supported by risk information. The system computed it from past Automatic Identification System (AIS) data with the Coast Guard's records of risk recommendations. The risk information shortened the time before a controller sent a risk warning to a vessel by an average of about two minutes. In the simulation, the number of warnings issued to risk-prone vessels nearly doubled. Fujitsu reports that the technology was particularly effective for newcomers. The 2020 results come from a simulation of past cases. Fujitsu announced the figures in a press release of 15 April 2020. The Maritime Executive restated them the same day. The Maritime Executive cites the Japan Transport Safety Board's count of 2,863 marine collisions in Japan from 2009 to 2019. In the release the Japan Coast Guard said that it would verify more complex traffic conditions and improve the accuracy of the technology as it planned to implement the development. Fujitsu then ran a second field trial at the same center from 17 November 2020 to 2 September 2021 with an added course-following algorithm. Fujitsu reported about 90% fewer unnecessary alerts than with the earlier technology. It planned a commercial service for vessel traffic from March 2022.

fields.summary: At a Tokyo Bay traffic center, controllers replayed past near misses with collision-risk predictions from Fujitsu Human Centric AI Zinrai. They sent warnings about two minutes earlier.
fields.account: From December 2019 to March 2020, Fujitsu Limited and the Japan Coast Guard tested an artificial-intelligence system to predict vessel collisions at the Tokyo Wan Vessel Traffic Service Center. The center supports vessel traffic under an outsourcing contract with the Coast Guard. The system uses Fujitsu Human Centric AI Zinrai from Fujitsu Laboratories. The technology detects near misses between vessels. It predicts areas where collision risk concentrates in Tokyo Bay. In the center's training environment, six experienced maritime traffic controllers and instructors simulated control tasks based on past near-miss accidents. They compared conventional operation with operation supported by risk information. The system computed it from past Automatic Identification System (AIS) data with the Coast Guard's records of risk recommendations. The risk information shortened the time before a controller sent a risk warning to a vessel by an average of about two minutes. In the simulation, the number of warnings issued to risk-prone vessels nearly doubled. Fujitsu reports that the technology was particularly effective for newcomers. The 2020 results come from a simulation of past cases. Fujitsu announced the figures in a press release of 15 April 2020. The Maritime Executive restated them the same day. The Maritime Executive cites the Japan Transport Safety Board's count of 2,863 marine collisions in Japan from 2009 to 2019. In the release the Japan Coast Guard said that it would verify more complex traffic conditions and improve the accuracy of the technology as it planned to implement the development. Fujitsu then ran a second field trial at the same center from 17 November 2020 to 2 September 2021 with an added course-following algorithm. Fujitsu reported about 90% fewer unnecessary alerts than with the earlier technology. It planned a commercial service for vessel traffic from March 2022.

record.summary: OPTiM says that its AI Physical Security Service analyzes camera video from JR Kyushu stations in real time to alert administrators to anomalies. No trial result has been published.
record.account: Kyushu Railway Company (JR Kyushu) made Wajiro and the other Kashii Line stations except Kashii and Chōjabaru unstaffed from 14 March 2015. It serves their passengers remotely. OPTiM Corporation announced on 6 October 2017 a demonstration trial of its “AI Physical Security Service” from 10 October 2017. It would run at two JR Kyushu stations: 和白駅 (Wajiro) on the Kashii Line and 二島駅 (Futajima) on the Chikuho Main Line. The service, on “OPTiM Cloud IoT OS”, has AI monitor network-camera video in real time. When it detects an anomaly, it shows an alert. It sends administrators an email. OPTiM says that this is to reduce the burden on operators who watch many monitors. It says that a second aim is to raise safety in the station. The release includes an image of the analysis of footage from a station camera. In it, the system identifies people, trains and the yellow platform line. OPTiM published the release on optim.co.jp. @Press republished it. The release is the only account of the JR Kyushu trial. JR Kyushu is not quoted. OPTiM gives no end date for the trial. It does not list what the system was to detect. No result of the JR Kyushu trial has been published. The only reported detection rate comes from OPTiM's later trial at JR East's Sawa station, announced on 26 June 2018. It was 96.2% against a 90% target.

data.retained_case_account: OPTiM Corporation announced on 6 October 2017 a demonstration trial of its “AI Physical Security Service” from 10 October 2017. It would run at two Kyushu Railway Company (JR Kyushu) stations: 和白駅 (Wajiro) on the Kashii Line and 二島駅 (Futajima) on the Chikuho Main Line. The service, on “OPTiM Cloud IoT OS”, has AI monitor network-camera video in real time. When it detects an anomaly, it shows an alert and emails administrators. This is to reduce the burden on operators who watch many monitors and to raise safety in the station. The release includes an image of station camera analysis identifying people, trains and the yellow platform line. The release is the only source (on optim.co.jp and republished by @Press). JR Kyushu is not quoted, no trial end date, detection target list or result is given, and no later report of outcomes was found. Station romanizations are ours.

fields.account: Kyushu Railway Company (JR Kyushu) made Wajiro and the other Kashii Line stations except Kashii and Chōjabaru unstaffed from 14 March 2015. It serves their passengers remotely. OPTiM Corporation announced on 6 October 2017 a demonstration trial of its “AI Physical Security Service” from 10 October 2017. It would run at two JR Kyushu stations: 和白駅 (Wajiro) on the Kashii Line and 二島駅 (Futajima) on the Chikuho Main Line. The service, on “OPTiM Cloud IoT OS”, has AI monitor network-camera video in real time. When it detects an anomaly, it shows an alert. It sends administrators an email. OPTiM says that this is to reduce the burden on operators who watch many monitors. It says that a second aim is to raise safety in the station. The release includes an image of the analysis of footage from a station camera. In it, the system identifies people, trains and the yellow platform line. OPTiM published the release on optim.co.jp. @Press republished it. The release is the only account of the JR Kyushu trial. JR Kyushu is not quoted. OPTiM gives no end date for the trial. It does not list what the system was to detect. No result of the JR Kyushu trial has been published. The only reported detection rate comes from OPTiM's later trial at JR East's Sawa station, announced on 26 June 2018. It was 96.2% against a 90% target.

outcomes[].duration.reason: The duration of the claimed benefit is not separately established. Dated follow-up on the same outcome is needed to distinguish a one-time result from recurring or sustained benefit; later work on another system or population does not establish persistence here. The recorded follow-up says: OPTiM announced on 26 June 2018 that a trial of the same service with Itec Hankyu Hanshin at JR Sawa station on the Joban Line achieved a 96.2% detection rate of people or objects crossing the platform's yellow line while no train was present, against a 90% target; no result for the JR Kyushu stations was found.
